News.title: Chancellor must cut spending instead of tax rises, Rishi Sunak warns ahead of dreaded Budget
News.content:
STEADY THE SHIP Chancellor must cut spending instead of tax rises, Rishi Sunak warns ahead of dreaded Budget

CHANCELLOR John Healey must cut spending in his first Budget instead of hiking taxes, Rishi Sunak said.

The former Prime Minister said his successor in the Treasury should signal to the markets he will control public spending.



Mr Sunak wrote in The Sunday Times: “He should make clear that he’ll not increase taxes in the budget and that if adjustments need to be made, he’ll cut spending.

“That would provide the certainty needed in an increasingly uncertain world.”



He said Mr Healey must avoid repeating the mistakes of Rachel Reeves with “constant, confidence-sapping speculation about which taxes will rise”.



The new Chancellor will give a speech on Monday in the West Midlands outlining his vision for economic growth.

However, he set a gloomy tone in an interview with the Financial Times in which he warned of a tough Budget this autumn due to the Iran war.

He said: “What’s happening in the Middle East is hitting inflation, it’s hitting growth, it’s hitting borrowing costs. It’s part of a more dangerous world that is more uncertain.”

His tone is in stark contrast to bouncy Prime Minister Andy Burnham who entered No10 with costly ambitions to please voters.



Shadow Chancellor Andrew Griffith warned: “It would be completely wrong for John Healey to raise taxes on hard working families.

“Especially given our people pleasing Prime Minister will only use the money for more handouts rather than defending our nation.”

It comes as the Government announced a plan to free businesses from costly red tape.

They promised to slash complicated reporting rules under a change that will save businesses more than £450 million a year in total.

Currently, the rules require small cafes chains and hotels to spend thousands on wordy reports.



Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said: “No-one goes into business to fill out forms.

“For years, hardworking firms in this country have been weighed down by pen-pushing paperwork and frustrating costs, ticking boxes that do nothing to help them grow their business.

“We’re stripping back outdated bureaucracy and building a common-sense system fit for a 21st-century economy. This will cut the cost of doing business, giving breathing room to bosses across the country, and free them up to focus on what they do best, creating jobs and growth.”

News.title: Probe launched after ‘unexplained’ death of child next to fishing lake in UK woodland
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

TRAGIC DEATH Probe launched after ‘unexplained’ death of child next to fishing lake in UK woodland

COPS have launched an investigation after the “unexplained death” of a child close to a fishing lake.

The youngster was found after emergency services were called to reports of a person in cardiac arrest.



Police and an air ambulance rushed to woodland near Strawberry Lane in Great Wyrley, Staffordshire, at around 8.45am today.

Despite desperate efforts by paramedics, the child was pronounced dead at the scene a short time later.



Staffordshire Police said the death is currently being treated as unexplained.

The force has not confirmed the child’s age or released any further details.

Officers were called by colleagues from West Midlands Ambulance Service, who had been responding to the cardiac arrest report.

Midlands Air Ambulance was also sent to the scene as emergency crews raced to save the child.



But tragically, the youngster could not be saved.

Roads around the area were closed throughout the day as detectives began piecing together what had happened.

Police were expected to remain at the scene into the evening as their investigation continued.

The circumstances surrounding the child’s death remain unclear.

A Staffordshire Police spokesperson said: “We were called to land off Strawberry Lane, Great Wyrley, at 8.45am today (Saturday 5 September) by colleagues from West Midlands Ambulance Service, who were responding to a report of a child in cardiac arrest.



“Officers attended alongside Midlands Air Ambulance.

“Sadly, the child was pronounced dead by paramedics a short time later.

“The death is currently being treated as unexplained.

“Officers remain at the scene.”

News.title: Ex-boyfriend ‘kidnapped former girlfriend and locked her in car boot before hurling her from 130ft motorway bridge’
News.content:
'KILLER' EX Ex-boyfriend ‘kidnapped former girlfriend and locked her in car boot before hurling her from 130ft motorway bridge’

A TWISTED man allegedly kidnapped his ex-lover and hurled her over a motorway bridge – before jumping to his death.

The suspected murder-suicide unfolded at around midday after Federico Vella, 36, lay in wait for Lorena Isceri, 46, at her home in Florence, Italy.



Police said the car rental manager waited in the garage at his ex-girlfriend’s house before pouncing when she came home for lunch.

He reportedly beat Lorena, zip-tied her legs and stuffed her in the boot of her own Audi, before driving off.



Desperate to escape, Lorena secretly dialled the police with a phone she found in a rucksack in the boot of the car.

As Vella cruised north towards Bologna, Lorena told operators she had been kidnapped and tried to share her location, also giving a description of her attacker.



She also tried, without success, to call her mum and a friend at around 2pm.

Florence authorities traced the signal as it raced down the motorway and dispatched traffic police to intercept the car.

But tragically, Vella noticed that his ex had managed to call the police and reportedly shouted: “What are you doing?”.

Police said he then pulled over at around 2:40pm and snatched the phone from Lorena.



He then grabbed his ex and allegedly threw her off the 131ft bridge.

Horrified cops, who had just arrived on the scene, reportedly screamed: “what have you done?”

He reportedly replied: “She betrayed me, she treated me badly, she attacked me.” Officers said he then leapt to his death.



Both bodies were found on the concrete ground below.

Lorena had worked in marketing for a vet practice where she was described as bright and devoted to her job.

Police have launched a probe into the deaths and have seized the car for examination.

Just hours before the horrifying attack, Federico Vella, 36, had posted a chilling message to social media, writing: “Goodbye to everyone.”

Lorena had broken up with Vella three weeks earlier on August 31.



YOU'RE NOT ALONE EVERY 90 minutes in the UK a life is lost to suicide. It doesn’t discriminate, touching the lives of people in every corner of society – from the homeless and unemployed to builders and doctors, reality stars and footballers. It’s the biggest killer of people under the age of 35, more deadly than cancer and car crashes And men are three times more likely to take their own life than women. Yet it’s rarely spoken of, a taboo that threatens to continue its deadly rampage unless we all stop and take notice, now. That is why The Sun launched the You’re Not Alone campaign. The aim is that by sharing practical advice, raising awareness and breaking down the barriers people face when talking about their mental health, we can all do our bit to help save lives. Let’s all vow to ask for help when we need it, and listen out for others…You’re Not Alone. The day before the break-up, Vella had shared a series of now-sinister posts, writing: “Some instances are so perfect that, even if you separate them, the shape of the other remains with you forever.”

News.title: Woman, 38, dies after car crashes into brick wall in UK city
News.content:
SMASH TRAGEDY Woman, 38, dies after car crashes into brick wall in UK city

A WOMAN has died after a car left the road and smashed into a brick wall in a horrific tragedy.

The 38-year-old was driving a red Nissan Juke when the crash happened late last night.

Emergency services scrambled to Allerton Road in Woolton, Merseyside, shortly after 11.30pm on Friday.

But despite their efforts, the woman was pronounced dead at the scene.





Her devastated family have been informed and are being supported by a specially trained family liaison officer.

Cops are now appealing for witnesses as they work to establish exactly what happened.

Sergeant Phil Everett, of Merseyside Police‘s Matrix Roads Policing department, said: “Our thoughts are with the family members of the woman who sadly died following the collision late last night and they are being supported by a specially trained family liaison officer.

“We are in the early stages of an investigation into this incident and it is now our priority to confirm exactly how the collision occurred.



“We know this happened late last night when many residents may have been inside their homes but if anyone saw what happened or were driving through the area just before the incident occurred then please get in touch.

“Similarly, if you live in the area and have doorbell footage of the incident, please contact us.

“You may have information or footage that could be vital to our investigation.”

A police scene was in place on Allerton Road whilst forensic investigators carried out their examinations, but all roads are now reopened.



Anyone with information or footage which could help the investigation is urged to contact Merseyside Police quoting reference 26000727021.

News.title: My son, 17, was stabbed on dancefloor then died after open heart op at roadside…what I saw in court was more traumatic
News.content:
GRIEF-STRICKEN Martin Cosser could barely compose himself as the traumatic footage was shown to a stunned-silent courtroom.

The horrific mobile phone video was being shown – again – depicting his son Charlie, 17, staggering from a music festival marquee having just suffered a horrific stab wound. He would go on to collapse and later die.



It was one of the several gut-wrenching times that Martin and his family had to watch the life slowly drain from their beloved son during an utterly traumatic trial – that could have been avoided had his killer enter a guilty plea.

Tragic Charlie was viciously attacked by thug Yura Varybrus, also then 17, on the dancefloor at BalFest in Warnham, Sussex, in the early hours of Sunday, July 23 2023.

Dad-of-three Martin, 51, promised Charlie – a former Brentford youth academy player – on his deathbed days later he would dedicate his life to preventing other families from experiencing the same devastating loss.



Today he speaks to The Sun as part of a joint campaign with Fearless – the youth branch of charity CrimeStoppers – to encourage young people to utilise an anonymous reporting tool to flag individuals carrying knives.

Martin says: “I’ve made it my mission to put an end to this.

“The world deserves to know Charlie. Look at his picture, he’s everyone’s son, the boy next door – he wasn’t involved in gangs or crimes.

“He was a lovely lad, the centre of our lives, and he never hurt anyone. But that didn’t save him.”

He adds: “No families should have to go through what we have.”



Martin says he felt like he was “living in a bubble” after his son’s death, and his trauma was only magnified by the agonising murder trial.

Varybrus, whose identity was initially protected due to reporting restrictions, pleaded not guilty, meaning Charlie’s family were left to endure the full details of Charlie’s death in court.

Martin says: “My family had to hear from eyewitnesses, emergency service personnel, a pathologist.



“We now know that at two minutes to midnight, after Charlie was first stabbed, until 28 minutes past, when he went into traumatic cardiac arrest, how scared he was, how much he was suffering, things we’d be protected from if Charlie’s murderer pleaded guilty.”

The family also had to watch a video showing the aftermath of the attack, filmed inadvertently by a festivalgoer to upload to social media.

“Every day we had to watch Charlie stagger out of the marquee and collapse,” says Martin.

“He put us through that for nothing… that lives with us, and that has scarred us, and those are scars that will never be able to be unpicked.

“That’s trauma we live with until the day we die.”



Martin says the court proceedings reminded him of “some kind of circus act”, in which both legal teams were pitted against each other, rather than a process where the goal was justice being served.

He described at one stage a law from 1912 being referred to, calling it “archaic” and “100 years out of date”, as well as questioning how it is fair Charlie’s killer’s identity was initially protected but his son’s wasn’t.

“It’s barbaric,” he continues. “The criminal justice system is broken.”



He adds: “It was actually worse than when Charlie died, for my family and I.”

Varybrus was ultimately found guilty by a jury after just three-and-a-half hours, and was sentenced to 16 years in prison.

Martin says: “They call it life, but we have the life sentence, not him.”

Charlie, just weeks from his 18th birthday, had attended the festival with a couple of pals.

Martin recalled having almost a sixth sense as he had an unusual urge to watch his son from the window as he walked up the driveway and got into his friend’s car.



Then, at around 12.30am, there was a knock at the door.

Martin, who was asleep, dashed downstairs in his underwear and found two police officers standing outside.



He recalls: “They said ‘I’m afraid your son Charlie has been stabbed and he’s critical’.”

Martin, wife Tara and their daughter Eloise, then 15, were driven to hospital by the officers.

Martin says: “They performed an open heart aortic repair procedure in the road.

“No patient in medical history has survived that procedure outside of a hospital.



“Charlie did, he made it to hospital, he had another traumatic cardiac arrest.

“We were told he probably wouldn’t survive surgery, he did, we were told he probably wouldn’t survive the night, he did.”

The following day, the family were momentarily relieved when they were told his heart was doing well and “he was probably going to make it”, said Martin, holding back tears.

But half an hour later it was found he had fluid on the brain and was once again rushed to surgery – but it had caused irreversible brain damage.



On Tuesday, Charlie’s family and closest friends said their goodbyes to the teenager.

Martin recalls: “That was when I told Charlie how much I loved him and how much of an honour and a privilege it had been to be his dad – and I would spend the rest of my life educating young people on the dangers and impact of knife crime.”

Martin and Tara ultimately set up the charity Charlie’s Promise, with the heartbroken dad having given countless talks, including in schools and prisons.

“I’ve had hardened criminals, killers, in tears at my talks because it’s real,” he says.



What is Fearless and Charlie's Promise? FEARLESS is the dedicated youth service of the independent charity Crimestoppers, designed to give young people aged 11 to 16 a safe way to pass on information about crime 100% anonymously. It can be accessed here using any smartphone, tablet or computer-based web browser. Fearless has partnered with fellow-charity Charlie’s Promise to launch its biggest-ever awareness campaign. Charlie’s Promise is dedicated to helping the fight against the rising issue of knife crime in Surrey and across the UK. A new film, featuring Charlie’s parents and charity founders Martin and Tara has been released as part of the scheme. It’s described as aiming to “empower young people to use their voice for change, highlighting anonymous reporting as a safe route to share information about crime before violence escalates”. Martin said: “Charlie’s death has left a hole in our family that can never be filled. No parent should have to experience the pain of losing their child to knife crime. “There may be young people who know someone is carrying a knife but feel frightened, uncertain or worried about what will happen if they speak up. “I want them to understand that they do not have to give their name or put themselves at risk. “Even a small piece of information could prevent another young person from being hurt and another family from suffering the heartbreak we live with every day.”

“Most kids won’t tell their parents if they know about someone with a knife because they don’t want to worry them. They don’t trust them.

“Varybrus had been known to have been carrying a knife in the days and weeks before Charlie’s death – but nothing was done.

“If the kids around him knew about Fearless, they could’ve done something.”

He adds he makes schoolkids promise they will never pick up a knife for the wrong reason and they’ll report anyone who does.

Martin says: “Life is hard, for me it’s like walking a tight rope – one side is the abyss, it’s pain I literally can’t articulate – but the other side is a superpower driven by love, it can make a change.



“That’s the side I stay on.”

News.title: Dad, 36, butchered by three strangers with ‘arsenal of knives’ on housing estate as ‘wicked’ trio caged for 68 years
News.content:
VILE KILLING Dad, 36, butchered by three strangers with ‘arsenal of knives’ on housing estate as ‘wicked’ trio caged for 68 years

THREE violent men have been jailed for a combined 68 years after using “an arsenal of knives” to hack a dad to death.

Gregory Catillo Volquez, 36, had been out at night with his friends in north London when he was murdered in January 2025.



Yesterday, Benito Ramirez Kones, 20, and 22-year-old Carlos Akum Metumbe, of Spain, and Italian national, Luiggi Perelli Santana, 23, were sentenced at Southwark Crown Court.

The “wicked” trio, who did not know Gregory, seemingly randomly attacked him with a machete and a crutch out of sight of CCTV.



A murder investigation was launched when Gregory was found lying in the street, dying from 22 stab wounds.

The post-mortem found many of the fatal injuries were caused by a long knife, as well as bruises from a blunt object.



Cops hunted the killers and detained Kones in Swansea, five days after the attack, where his trainers were seized and traces of Gregory’s blood was found on them.

Metumbe and Santana managed to flee to Spain, but were traced by cops and extradited back to the UK in August and October 2025.



They were both captured on CCTV raining blows on Gregory with a machete and the crutch, and Santana’s bloody fingerprints were identified on the crutch and knife.

In court, the judge told the defendants: “In your evidence the two of you each attempted to restrict your involvement in this offence to what you considered could be proved against you from the CCTV footage and forensic evidence.

“Apart from your admission to limited involvement with a machete in the initial stages of the events, by you, Mr Metumbe… none of you accepted repeatedly stabbing the deceased with the arsenal of knives which was subsequently seized by the police.”

All three men were found guilty of murder and each given a life sentence for their horrific crime.

Kones and Santana must serve a minimum of 23 years, while Metumbe, 22 must serve a minimum of 22 years.



In a victim impact statement read out to the court, Gregory’s partner, Teresa said: “We have a daughter, a little girl, who misses her dad.

“She asks for him, she still expects to see him coming back. She needs his hugs, his words, and his presence.

“It is very painful to see a little girl suffering the absence of her father and how she tries to understand why he is not with us.

“They robbed her of the opportunity to grow up beside him, to share her birthdays, graduations and all the important moments of her life.

She added: “This tragedy not only destroyed our lives, but also broke the heart of a mother, who lost her only son.



“There are no words that can describe the suffering of this mother who had to say goodbye to her son in such a cruel and unjust way.

“Our family has been marked forever.”

Detective Inspector Jim Barry, who led the investigation, said: “Our thoughts go to Gregory’s loved ones who have demonstrated commendable togetherness and strength throughout this turbulent process.

“I know nothing will bring him home but am hopeful that this result offers justice and closure for his family, who have been left without a much-loved dad, brother, and son.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Our team of officers showed huge tenacity to build a solid case with undisputable forensic evidence which resulted in these violent men being taken off our streets for a long, long time.



“It’s this hard work that is enabling the force to secure a positive outcome from 95 per cent of our murder investigations.”

News.title: Farage admits ‘we will make mistakes’ but vows Reform UK will win next election in closing speech amid donation row
News.content:
NIGEL Farage admitted “sometimes we will get things wrong” as he delivered his closing speech at Reform UK’s party conference.

It comes amid a row over donations marring the event – but the defiant party leader vowed to win the next election and end the UK’s “terminal decline”.



Taking to a sparkler – filled stage in a light blue suit, Mr Farage said he will pick himself up again.

Following this week’s investigation into Reform’s donations, Mr Farage made an effort to rouse his “people’s army“.



The Reform leader said: “I’ll tell you what we learned yesterday and today.

“There will be times in this journey when there are good days and times when there are difficult days.



“More often than not, things will be put upon us that are unfair.

“But sometimes we will make mistakes, sometimes we will get things wrong and get a bit of a kicking for it.



“But what this conference has shown is whatever you throw at the leadership, whatever you throw at you, the people’s army, we immediately pick ourselves up, dust ourselves down and start all over again.”

The party chief also said he predicted there would be another general election before May.

He added: “I want us to win the next election because I believe I can lead us into the kind of fundamental change of direction that this country needs.

“And if we don’t take it, if we don’t take it, well, it might be our last chance to turn the country around before we head for terrible and, frankly, terminal decline.”

“That is why I am here.”



Two Reform UK figures – Dan Jukes and James Orr – both were removed from their jobs this week after an investigation into foreign donations.

Both deny wrongdoing – but were filed talking about how to get money to the party from an American donor.

Farage described the row was built on nothing but “loose pub talk” – and it comes after he faced questions over a £5million gift which led to his resignation and relection as an MP.

On the stage today, he returned again to his plan for his first 100 days in government.

The leader said he would sack any failing minister as he want “men and women of action”.



To close the conference all the weekend’s speakers took to the stage and sang the national anthem.

This follows a disrupted speech from Mr Farage last night.

The leader failed to appear and deliver his remarks before security personnel and a search dog were seen gathering behind the stage.

Counter-terror cops were also seen in the venue with several stepping up onto the stage as the speech was stalled.

When he finally took to the stage, his speech saw multiple interruptions from protesters in the crowd.



A number of people were reportedly dragged from the hall while Mr Farage was speaking.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Widely shared video however appears to show one protester was manhandled by the crowd as she was led out – with footage seeming to show her hair being pulled and her head grabbed.

Police have urged the woman to come forward as they are investigating the incident – but added that they have not received a formal complaint.

News.title: Lindsay Clancy neighbors say ‘devil was in killer mom’ as they relive horror of scene on night three kids died
News.content:
LINDSAY CLANCY’S neighbors have revealed the horror which darkened their doors on the night she murdered her three young children.

Clancy, 36, pleaded not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility to the 2023 murders of her three children, Cora, five, Dawson, three, and eight-month-old Callan.



The shocking killings destroyed her young family and set in motion a murder trial which has gripped a nation.

Now, neighbors who watched police descend on the normally quiet street have opened up about the unimaginable tragedy which has irreparably rocked their tight-knit community.



During a rollercoaster, five week trial, prosecutors allege Clancy knew what she was doing when she strangled her children with exercise bands at the family’s Duxbury home on January 24, 2023, before jumping from a second-floor window.

Clancy survived the fall but was left paralyzed.

Her defense argues she was suffering from severe mental illness and hearing voices at the time of the killings.

Ruth Hearson, 81, lives directly opposite Clancy’s former home.

She said the family largely kept to themselves and that she would occasionally see the former delivery nurse with her children.

“I saw four ambulances and I said, ‘Oh, it must be the CO2, carbon monoxide poisoning.’ That’s what I thought,” Hearson told The U.S. Sun.



“No one in their right mind kills their babies and jumps out a window on the second floor, thinking they’re gonna kill themselves. It’s not something you see every day.”

Hearson said she did not learn what had actually happened until a day or two after the killings.

She said the first responders who arrived at the home were deeply affected by what they encountered.

“The police, they were all traumatized. Coming down, seeing the babies, and some of them couldn’t go back to work,” she said.

“They were so bad.”



Asked how she felt about Clancy potentially facing life in prison, Hearson is sympathetic.



“I feel bad. When you’re like that, you’re not guilty. Because it wasn’t you doing it,” she said.

“They were her babies and she loved them. The devil was there. The devil did it.”

Clancy had reportedly struggled with her mental health before killing her children, although those living nearby didn’t suspect a thing.

Hearson said she had occasionally seen Clancy pushing her children in a stroller and assumed her family life behind closed doors was anything but the unimaginable nightmare it would become.

“Once in a while I’d see Patrick and I’d say, ‘Hey, hello.’ Or we saw a deer jump over my yard into their yard. They were across the street from me. It’s just so tragic. The babies were so cute,” she continued.



“I said to my pastor, I said, ‘I feel so bad there was nobody to welcome them into heaven because the grandparents are all here. They hadn’t died yet.’”

The terrifying case has dramatically shed light on postpartum psychosis and whether the healthcare system failed Clancy in her hour of need.

The 12-person jury, which consists of nine women and three men, has wrestled with her state of mind during a lengthy deliberations this week.

Clancy was admittedly suffering from depression and was on numerous medications.

Jurors heard that she had been prescribed 13 psychiatric meds during the four months before the killings, including antidepressants, anti-anxiety medications and antipsychotics.



She complained about the effects of the drugs, at one point saying she felt “completely numb” and “like a zombie.”

A note on her phone, last modified the day before the killings, said medication had “stole[n] me from my own body.”

“If you’re in a psychotic state, that’s what’s in control of you. Not your regular mind,” the neighbor said.

“And she had all those drugs in her, that’s what was controlling her. I really believe that.

“I’m heartbroken for her because she doesn’t have her babies.



“My mother, when she went into postpartum depression, they didn’t have pills. They had shock treatments. That’s what they did. Swear to God. 65 years ago.”

Other Duxbury residents have also questioned whether Clancy’s treatment contributed to her deterioration.

Another neighbor, who asked to remain anonymous and admitted she has tried to not talk about the murders with her own family, said the tragedy has been deeply stressful for the community.

“I want it to be over with. I don’t like seeing it every day [the trial coverage],” she told The U.S. Sun.

She remembered the night of the killings, when police descended on the neighborhood as the enormity of the tragedy began to sink in.



“I just knew it had to be something really big, all of the police cars, the whole area was blocked off. It was beginning to get dark,” she said.

“I saw them taking a stretcher out of the back, which looked like it had a woman on it.”

The woman said she was in “disbelief” when she later learned that Clancy’s children had died, and that their mother had jumped from a window.

“It’s stressful. Ever since it happened I think about it. I just want it over with. I don’t want to see her face anymore,” she continued.

“I don’t want any of that. For a long time people who live here were dropping off things at the house – teddy bears, flowers.”



She said signs were later put up around the property as feelings within the neighborhood changed.

“I don’t have good feelings about her, and what she did,” the local resident said. “But at the same time I don’t know too much about that mental illness.”

Eric McDonald told The U.S. Sun that he believes she should be hospitalized rather than imprisoned.

“She’s not going to get that in prison,” Duxbury resident McDonald said. “She’s just going to get worse.

“They just threw meds at her and hoped it would help and, you know, turn her into a zombie.”



Local man Mark Shortt, 62, said he believes medical professionals failed her.

“Whatever they did, it didn’t work,” he said.

Valerie Franks, a part-time Duxbury resident, questioned the number of medications Clancy had been prescribed.

“How can one person be sane with all that going into their body?” she asked.

“Personally, I think she’ll be better off in a hospital.”



Clancy was remembered by neighbors as a quiet mother who would push her youngest child in a stroller while her older children rode bikes and played outside.

Hearson said the family had a backyard jungle gym and generally kept to themselves.

The tragedy has nevertheless left a lasting mark on Duxbury, which residents described as a friendly beach town where serious crime is unusual.

Local churches have held memorial services, including at Holy Family Catholic Church.

But Hearson remains critical of the focus on religion during the trial.



“The prosecutor, she’s a little devil herself,” she said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I really think they should mind their own business, you know? It’s her medical [history] that they should concentrate on.”

News.title: Krystian Bielik appears to grab young Portsmouth fan by the throat during Cardiff City chaos
News.content:
Krystian Bielik appears to grab young Portsmouth fan by the throat during Cardiff City chaos

Portsmouth's 2-0 win over Cardiff City at Fratton Park on Saturday was marred by unsavoury scenes after Krystian Bielik allegedly clashed with a home supporter

View 3 Images

Cardiff defender Krystian Bielik allegedly grabbed a young Portsmouth fan by the throat during an angry clash in Saturday's Championship game between the two sides.

‌



The altercation happened midway through the second half of the match, which Portsmouth won 2-0. Bielik had headed over to the touchline to try and retrieve the ball for a throw-in, only to become embroiled in a heated clash with a young home fan.

‌



Replays of the incident, which quickly went viral on social media, allegedly show the 28-year-old grab the supporter around the throat. The Pompey fan retaliated by directing what appeared to be a slap at Bielik. The game was briefly paused while the referee attempted to restore order.

‌



The supporter was later ejected from the stadium following the incident. Bielik, who was booked earlier in the game, escaped further punishment, though it is likely The FA will investigate the incident, with Bielik potential facing a lengthy ban and a significant fine.

View 3 Images The clash occurred when Bielik went to retrieve the ball

View 3 Images

‌



On the pitch, goals from Conor Shaughnessy and Marezi Marezi did the damage for Pompey, who move into midtable.

Defeat at Fratton Park means Cardiff are without a win this season; they have drawn three of their five league games since winning promotion and drop into the bottom three.

Cardiff boss Brian Barry-Murphy said of the incident post-match: "I wanted to make sure he (Bielik) was protected and make sure he was okay, which he is.

‌



"I thought the referee and his staff handled the incident impeccably. I was assured by him the correct processes will take place.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"He said he’d seen everything which occurred really clearly, so he diffused the situation and implemented the correct processes from there.

‌



"The players are always subjected to different things that’s not acceptable. My job is to protect the players, but really I’m trying to make sure that we play well and win.

"I’m sure the FA will look at it and implement the correct processes."
