A chunk of ceiling fell inside a main hallway of the Kennedy Center, according to a spokesperson who said the damage underscores the need to shut down the historic arts venue for renovations sought by President Donald Trump.

No one was injured when a piece of the ceiling inside the Kennedy Center's grand foyer collapsed Friday evening, said Roma Daravi, the center's vice president for public relations.

Photos provided by the center showed a large hole in the high ceiling and debris littering the red carpet in part of the hallway that connects the Kennedy Center's three main performance auditoriums. The damage occurred during stormy weather in Washington.

The Kennedy Center's Trump-aligned board is fighting in court to move forward with plans to add Trump's name to the building's facade and to close the center for two years as it undergoes $250 million in renovations.

Daravi called the partial ceiling collapse Friday “another example of the urgent need to close for renovation and revitalization, as our Chairman President Trump has championed."

"This structural failure stems from decades of neglect and deferred maintenance by the previous leadership, and there’s no justification for further delays in restoring America’s cultural center,” Daravi said in a statement.

Trump's efforts to add his name and make other big changes to the center established to honor President John F. Kennedy following his assassination are just part of Trump's broader second-term agenda to reshape Washington.

Trump already has demolished the East Wing of the White House to make way for a ballroom. He also plans a triumphal arch near Arlington National Cemetery and a renovated golf course along the Potomac River.

U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper ruled in May that Trump's name had been added to the Kennedy Center illegally and ordered that it be taken down. He also blocked the administration from closing the venue for renovations.

Now before the judge is an August vote by the Kennedy Center's board to return Trump's name to the facade so reads: "The John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts Restored and Renovated By President Donald J. Trump.” Justice Department lawyers have argued donations for renovations will dry up without Trump's name on the building.

Other changes have moved forward. Last week, the Kennedy Center took down a large stick figure sculpture known as Blue that had stood outside the center in 2019. The Kennedy Center gave no reason for its removal, but said in a statement “we are honored to have been stewards” of the late sculptor Joel Shapiro's work.

Grace Terpstra of Keep the KC, a community group fighting the Kennedy Center's closure, said she suspects the board will seize on what appears to be limited ceiling damage “to make the point that the whole thing needs to be shut down, that it’s going to fall on everybody."

“I think they’ll try to make it into a bigger thing and show that they’ve found a lot of other things,” said Terpstra, the group's founder.

___ Bynum reported from Savannah, Georgia, and Sloan reported from Rehoboth Beach, Delaware.

News.title: How cheaper buys outshone £125m Enzo Fernandez on Manchester City bow
News.content:

Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

The previous time Enzo Fernandez had started a match, he exited in disgrace. A few weeks and £125m later, some Manchester City fans stood to applaud their most expensive debutant ever.

From being sent off in the World Cup final to being parachuted in for an unexpected start, it has been an eventful few weeks for the Argentinian. Relatively speaking, this was the calm after the storm.

The taunts from the Coventry fans as he was substituted are a sign of a growing notoriety, even if Fernandez was on his best behaviour as he turned in a performance that was more encouraging than astounding. Yet if City could thank one deadline-day signing for victory, it was not him but Gianluigi Donnarumma, who arrived at the end of the window last summer and who made three terrific saves.

But for Fernandez, it may have been a taste of things to come. Opposition supporters booed him, Erling Haaland scored, and City won at home to top the table.

Many of the most eye-catching moments stemmed from the excellent Rayan Cherki, the outstanding outfield player on the pitch. But the eye was drawn to Fernandez. City planned to give the British record signing a watching brief at the beginning, but then Nico O’Reilly suffered a back problem in the warm-up, and he was summoned to start.

And so he formed half of the costliest midfield double act in Premier League history. The £116m Elliot Anderson, stripped of his title as City’s record buy, operated deeper. Fernandez played as the No 8, with more licence to get forward and, though he had only played 25 minutes since the World Cup final, the sharpness to do so.

He was prominent; after engineering his exit from Chelsea and some of his antics at the World Cup, City may have been relieved there was nothing controversial about Fernandez's contribution. Briefly, it seemed he had an assist when he hooked the ball to Haaland for a tap-in, but the Argentinian was ruled offside.

But Fernandez had a part in the winner, feeding Antoine Semenyo, who whipped in a cross. Haaland met it with a bullet header. Fernandez, the instigator of many a move, could get quite a few pre-assists at City, playing the pass before the pass before a goal.

open image in gallery Rayan Cherki was the best player on the pitch ( AP )

For Enzo Maresca, also his manager at Chelsea, it was a seamless introduction. “An ideal start,” said the Italian. “It is much more easy with a player you already share time together because they know exactly what you want. We know each other very well, and I know he is going to help the team win games.”

That sense that Fernandez can slot straight in because he understands Maresca’s demands was amplified by the manager’s verdict on City’s other deadline-day arrival. Iliman Ndiaye made his bow after his £60m move from Everton.

“Most of the time he was moving in the wrong way, but he needs to learn,” said Maresca; it was not meant as a harsh appraisal, simply that the Senegalese has to spend more time in the final third and less dropping deep.

It may have been a reason why City did not fully click in attack, despite their 100 per cent record. “The good thing for me is that all of the wins have been different,” said Maresca. “I think [in the] first half we deserve more goals.”

open image in gallery Gianluigi Donnarumma was called into several crucial saves ( PA Wire )

Cherki had come close to an opener, drilling a shot against the inside of the post. He was twice Haaland’s supplier when the Norwegian was denied by Carl Rushworth; superb for Coventry on loan last season, the goalkeeper looks a fine buy. When Cherki went off and Phil Foden came on, the substitute was denied by a goal-line clearance from Bobby Thomas.

Meanwhile, Coventry could look back at four chances, two before Haaland scored, two after, and each a fine opportunity to get their first top-flight goal since Mustapha Hadji scored in 2001.

Semenyo’s assist almost came for the visitors, accidentally sending Taiwo Awoniyi clear on goal with a misdirected pass; he was presumably relieved to see the Coventry striker shoot wide. Donnarumma then began his fine display by repelling Jack Rudoni’s header.

As Coventry sought an equaliser, the Italian made terrific saves to deny the substitutes Loum Tchouna and Ellis Simms, the latter with his face. “Nine of 10 times of this kind of game you end up conceding, but not all the wins are going to be nice wins,” rationalised Maresca. “We need some kind of these wins in [an] ugly way.”

Certainly Coventry would appreciate an ugly win. The fixture list conspired against the promoted club, with trips to Arsenal and City in their first three games, but their search for a first goal and point goes on. But, outclassed at the Emirates Stadium, they impressed at the Etihad.

“Going to Arsenal felt very different; it felt [like] our first game in the Premier League for 25 years,” said manager Frank Lampard. “This felt [like] a competitive Premier League game. I thought we deserved something. Probably a draw is a fair result.”

News.title: Relentless Springboks punish All Black errors to come from behind for 2-1 series lead
News.content:
There will be no repeat of the All Blacks historic Test series victory in South Africa 30 years ago, after the home side ensured they will lead 2-1 going into the concluding weekend.

And the manner in which the Springboks blew away their fierce rivals in the last 15 minutes make Rassies Eramus’s men overwhelming favourites to finish the job in America next Saturday.

However, there were passages of this brutal battle that suggested that Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry could still produce a finale worthy of the billing if New Zealand can learn the lessons from this brutal encounter at the FNB Stadium in Johannesburg.

There was a late Kiwi try to give the scoreboard a humdinger hue but Erasmus’s side were well deserving of their second victory in as many Saturdays over their fierce rivals, and credit to the South African head coach for outwitting counterpart Dave Rennie without needing to change his starting XV just before the kick-off, like he did seven days before. Amazing what one can do with a simple but chilling game plan.

But New Zealand will still fancy their chances of levelling it, especially after matching their opponents’ haul of four tries. Their fly-half, Ruben Love, missed five simple-enough points and until that last quarter it was an even contest. Yet, as it tends to, South Africa’s physical intensity and their almighty scrum eventually prevailed.

News.title: Mudryk fails to help Tottenham break their duck as VAR denies Forest
News.content:
Mykhailo Mudryk made his first appearance in almost two years but Tottenham are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season.

The grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow burner and Tottenham were fortunate to avoid a third league defeat after a moment of controversy denied Oliver Glasner his first win at Nottingham Forest.

Neco Williams was adjudged to have handled the ball in the 65th minute after a VAR review, a decision which infuriated Glasner and the home team. Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot.

Tottenham do have their first point of the season and it is only Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair.

Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk has not played a competitive match since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off and this was a scrappy match with an erratic performance from referee Craig Pawson.

One of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. Forest improved in the second half and were denied the goal after a period of sustained pressure.

Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goalline. A subsequent VAR review ruled that the Wales international did handle it.

News.title: Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

News.title: Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fightback for draw
News.content:
A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

News.title: ‘It’s just a useless gimmick’: Telegraph readers react to Dyson’s latest gadget
News.content:
Would you spend over £400 on a toothbrush? Telegraph readers aren’t convinced.

The new Dyson CameraJet has just launched, retailing for £419.99, which brushes, flosses and mouth-washes in one, with the help of a camera.

After Rebecca Astill gave her verdict on the gadget, we asked Telegraph readers for their views and whether Dyson can convince them to trade in their old faithfuls.

They share the toothbrushes they swear by, from manual to electric models, and whether they see any reason to upgrade. Here’s what they had to say.

Why readers are unconvinced

The majority of readers seem unconvinced by the CameraJet, with John arguing that a toothbrush and a smartphone “sounds like two accidents waiting to happen. Squirted in the eye with mouthwash as you drop the phone down the toilet”.

“It’s just a useless gimmick,” argues reader Donald Mckie, a retired NHS dentist. “The average patient wouldn’t have a clue what they would be looking at in their mouth on a phone screen,” he adds.

“Dyson as a brand is an aspiration for many but I don’t know how this appliance would improve anyone’s oral health.”

In his view, “the tank for the mouthwash at 12.5ml is far too small, the industry average will be somewhere near 250-300ml” to last long enough and successfully dislodge sticky plaque.

He also questions the picture quality of the camera with water spray, saliva, lips, facial hair and toothpaste in the way. “People nowadays will expect pin sharp detail, which I doubt this will deliver.”

News.title: DiCaprio’s Amazonian warrior queen
News.content:
It was while she was in hiding after recovering from the sixth attempt on her life, that the activist Juma Xipaia got a call asking if she would agree to be the subject of a documentary. The first female chief of the Middle Xingu region of the Brazilian Amazon, Xipaia was well known in Brazil for her passionate attempts to protect her indigenous community from the effects of deforestation, illegal gold-mining and – in particular – the catastrophic environmental consequences of the $11 billion Belo Monte hydroelectric dam project, a wildly ambitious and destructive endeavour that has affected livelihoods, fish stocks, ecosystems and biodiversity, with legal challenges still ongoing today.

Thirty-four-year-old Xipaia’s outspoken resistance and exposure of corruption relating to the dam’s construction led to the threats on her life. The last attempt was by poisoning, via a food delivery company, which resulted in her being on a ventilator with 70 per cent organ failure. She was on the verge of death, when, she says, she had a dream that she was given a choice – to take the easy path of dying, or the difficult path of coming back, and because she’s a fighter, that’s the one she chose. And a week later she walked out of the hospital.

Leonardo DiCaprio described the activist as one of the most incredible people he’d ever met Credit : Lalo de Almeida/Folhapress, FSP

Like many activists representing indigenous communities she walked a tightrope between protecting the interests and traditions of her people, and not being perceived as standing in the way of progress in terms of the economic development that benefits Brazil as a whole, a paradox that was defined when President Lula da Silva regained power in 2023, and brought Xipaia into government.

Richard Ladkani, a film director who has made vibrant environmental documentaries such as The Ivory Game (about poaching) and Sea of Shadows (marine activists), was the man who called her. It was 2019, when Brazil was still under the brutal rule of Jair Bolsonaro and destruction of the Amazon was at its peak – an area of rainforest the size of Belgium was burned during his presidency, and thousands of illegal goldmines flourished, contaminating the forest, polluting the river with mercury (mercury is used to bind gold) and bringing crime and disruption to previously pristine areas.

Film-maker Richard Ladkani in the Brazilian Amazon Credit : Courtesy of Malaika Pictures

“All summer long we had seen these dramatic apocalyptic images,” says Ladkani. “And I was posing for photos at the premiere of Sea of Shadows, with [executive producers] Leo DiCaprio and Jane Goodall, when Leo leaned over and whispered, ‘So Richard, what’s next?’

“And I said, 'We've got to do something about the Amazon.’”

DiCaprio came onboard as producer, and Goodall as an ambassador. Ladkani knew he had to find a powerful central figure to provide human and emotional context, someone who would be the voice of the Amazon. He drew up a list of possible candidates, until the Brazilian journalist Eliane Brum told him “do not make a decision until you have spoken to Juma Xipaia – when she speaks, the world listens. She can silence a whole room with her energy.”

‘For a long time I had been seen as a soldier, an army of one’

Right now, in a small restaurant in New York, Xipaia is not really in the mood to talk. It is February, and it’s snowing, and Ladkani, Xipaia and her husband, Hugo Loss, are here to publicise the resulting documentary, Yanuni – which took six years to make – at a screening attended by UN representatives and Brazilian diplomats. The recent news about Trump’s exploits in Venezuela has shaken them all and, more specifically, Juma has had a bad experience with American food which doesn’t really agree with her. She is a little reticent at first, but soon opens up with the help of an interpreter, and explains to me what it meant to be a cacique (chief), and how she was selected.

Indigenous leader Juma Xipaia and her husband Hugo Loss in the city of Aracaju, Brazil Credit : Lalo de Almeida/Folhapress, FSP

“I never chose to be a cacique,” she says, “but I couldn’t stay quiet in the face of exploitation of my people – there was violence, and women being harassed and raped.” She is referring to the collateral damage that importing thousands of workers to build a dam inevitably brings. “Usually the role of cacique is given to the oldest male in the community – my dad and my uncles and my brother were all caciques, but the elders knew that they could trust me never to negotiate our rights with corporations or politicians, never to compromise. For a long time I had been seen as a soldier, an army of one. I accepted the position for two years, with the goal of strengthening on our territories and bringing sovereignty to our people.”

Xipaia was born in 1991 and had an idyllic childhood, she says, growing up in Tucumã, a small indigenous community along the Iriri River, about 250 miles west of the city of Altamira. They lived in wooden houses and ate fruit and nuts from the forest and fish from the river, and in 2006 she moved to Altamira for her education. But threats were encroaching her community, with land opened up for mining and farming, and in 2011, a licence was granted to construct the Belo Monte Dam, to stop up parts of the Xingu River, one of the most species-rich areas of the Amazon.

Aged just 21, Xipaia spoke out against the dam at a public hearing, but despite lawsuits, protest from indigenous people and large sections of society, construction went ahead. Xipaia attended law school in Altamira and studied plans put forward by Norte Energia, the company that built Belo Monte, helping to expose corruption that was going on within. In 2015, at the age of 24, she became a cacique, the first female leader of her people. Other communities had been bought off by Norte Energia with gifts of stoves, fridges, TVs.

In November 2019, she led a protest of angry Brazilian landowners and farmers to disrupt the Amazon: Center of the World international conference in Altamira. But by now she had become a target, and by the time Ladkani called her she had survived six attempts on her life, including her car being rammed with children in the back, and a threat to kidnap her son. She went into hiding for a year and she didn’t want to talk to anyone.

“She thought, the only way I’m going to survive is if I stop talking, because when I talk, people want to kill me,” Ladkani says. But she was finally convinced to take a call from him, and from the first moment, he says, he knew he had found the voice for his film. “Her poetry is the thing that stands out – the way she can describe emotions and feelings and put things into context, I felt it was unique. And when she told me the story of how she almost died because of the poisoning, I was in tears.

“I told her I wanted her to be the voice in the film and also offered her the role of producer. Because I knew nothing of indigenous life and I needed her to lead the way.”

An aerial view of the Belo Monte hydroelectric dam in Altamira Credit : CARLOS FABAL

It was a struggle from the word go. Xipaia was not happy about a translator being involved because of security reasons; she couldn’t trust anyone. So Ladkani, who is Austrian, took intensive lessons in Portuguese and within six months was fluent. “It was a key thing to show that I meant business and took her concerns very seriously,” he tells me.

The security budget for the film was huge, they needed the best, most experienced people: safe houses, secure drivers. And the arrangements had to extend for a year after filming was completed – a total of seven years. “Leo was extremely important here because he raised the first third of the budget, and this encouraged other philanthropists to be part of it.”

Filming began in 2020. There was no script and Ladkani didn’t know what he was going to get from it, just that he needed to tell the story of the pillaging of the Amazon via Xipaia’s voice.

And in the end it was a wild ride: it started with Xipaia leading protests against Bolsonaro, but after Lula was elected in 2023, he established a Ministry for Indigenous Rights, of which Xipaia was made state secretary, implementing a series of bills for the protection of the forest and employing lawyers, biologists and engineers to combat the destruction of the Amazon.

Juma Xipata and Leonardo DiCaprio at the Yanuni Premiere during the 2025 Tribeca Festival in New York City. Credit : John Nacion/Getty Images for Tribeca Festival

The film documents her move from her village to set up home in Brasilia with her son; getting together with her husband Hugo Loss, head of special operations for Ibama (the Brazilian Institute of Renewable and Natural Resources), an elite outfit conducting raids on illegal mines; and the birth of their first child, who was called Yanuni.

It was a lengthy, exciting journey, an improvisation which resulted in thousands of hours of film. “I just had to go with the unpredictable. The strength of any documentary is when unforeseen things happen, because a twist in direction is the greatest thing of any film structure.

“And we had that multiple times. I had chosen a woman to be the voice of the Amazon and two years later she became the second most powerful woman in the Indigenous Ministry – I get goosebumps now at the sheer luck. That was the first twist, and then Hugo enters her life, who happens to be this charismatic soldier of an elite force who would take me to the frontline of the Amazon resistance, and then Juma becomes pregnant and gives birth to Yanuni. Holy s**t. If I had written that as a script, everyone would have thrown it out as complete fiction.”

‘I said, how dangerous is it? And he said, “Well, the risk of you dying is 50 per cent”’

Leo DiCaprio was a producer on the film (rather than his usual role of executive producer), which meant he was far more involved. “He not only provided the money, but he gave me meaningful support throughout the production,” says Ladkani. In November 2021 DiCaprio attended Cop 26 in Glasgow, where he met Xipaia for the first time. “That meeting was spectacular – Leo posted a picture of the two of them together and said that she was one of the most incredible people he’d ever met.” The resulting attention helped to protect Xipaia, because a public profile is to some extent a safeguard. “There she is next to DiCaprio, so she’s not just a voiceless indigenous person from somewhere in the Amazon.”

There were many technical challenges. Because of security, Ladkani couldn’t film in the normal way, with lighting and a crew. “I had a second cinematographer, a brilliant guy from Brazil, called Fábio Nascimento, and I took him with me when I could – but that was only 30 per cent of the time. The rest I shot alone. I downsized my gear and basically shot the film with a DSLR, like a photo camera, so I looked like a tourist. To an outsider, I was just a white gringo taking pictures.” Xipaia had a hidden microphone beneath her shirt. If Ladkani was ever confronted, he claimed to be a YouTuber.

“Security demanded that we shot the film incognito, and that became its strength, because I was embedded within the family to the extent that they stopped noticing me,” says Ladkani.

An illegal gold-mining ship destroyed by Ibama in the Brazilian Amazon – it is dangerous work, with agents risking serious injury and even their lives Credit : Courtesy of Malaika Pictures

Hugo Loss’s job involved protecting indigenous communities and flying over the forest and rivers of the Amazon routing out illegal goldmines, dredgers and excavators. His small team lands, arrests the miners and sets fire to all the expensive equipment, which is too bulky to confiscate. In the film we see massive plumes of thick black smoke rising above the forest. Penalties for environmental crime are insubstantial, but, says Loss, “It’s not for President Lula to change those things, it’s Congress, and it’s hard to change the law. But destroying the equipment is a real deterrent, because the machines are expensive, so it’s a risky investment.”

An illegal gold mine in the Brazilian Amazon Credit : Courtesy of Malaika Pictures

Loss and Xipaia met when her village was attacked in 2020 by illegal goldminers; she was in Altamira, a two-day boat ride away. She put out a cry for help on social media and Loss, who was also in Altamira, saw it and responded right away. He picked Xipaia up in a helicopter and asked her to take him to the exact location of the miners’ dredger. The attackers spotted them and ran, but Ibama were able to seize their boat and secure the area. “He saved her village and her people and her parents from an immediate attack and they fell in love and have been together ever since,” says Ladkani.

“I’m usually very shy about these things but from the first time I saw her in the helicopter I couldn’t stop thinking about her,” admits Loss. “Three months later I was doing an Ibama operation on land to remove some illegal loggers and I saw a hawk’s nest and I took a picture of it and sent it to her,” says Loss.

“It’s the bird whose feather I wear in my headdress,” interrupts Xipaia, shyly. She admits that she had first met Loss before the helicopter ride, at a meeting, but he was leaving as she arrived. “He shook my hand and I made eye contact with him and something told me – I can’t really explain what – that he was going to be my husband.”

Loss holds a Master’s degree in social anthropology from the University of Brasília and is one of Ibama’s most experienced field agents, yet he spent a good part of his career sidelined by Bolsonaro, who had no interest in protecting the environment. In February 2023, under Lula, he was appointed Ibama’s coordinator of enforcement.

Loss has taken part in hundreds of operations. His job is a dangerous one. We watch him flying helicopters over swathes of forest to spot mines, or patrolling the rivers looking for dredgers. Recently one of his team was killed in an ambush, another got burns over 60 per cent of his body.

Hugo Loss, Xipaia’s husband, on a mission to destroy illegal mining equipment for Ibama, Brazil’s government enforcement agency

Ladkani asked to accompany Loss on a raid. “Hugo told me, it's too dangerous, the risk of you dying is too high. It’s a small team, and you would be taking the place of a soldier on the helicopter so we would be down one security man, which means our job is much harder, and by the way, if we get into a gun fight, we are not your bodyguards, we are there to finish a job. You would have to save yourself.

“I said, how dangerous is it? And he said, ‘Well, the risk of you dying is 50 per cent.’ I laughed – and then I realised he wasn’t joking.

Film-maker Richard Ladkani in the Brazilian Amazon Credit : Courtesy of Malaika Pictures

“Of course I had to think about that – I have a wife and two daughters. My wife and I discussed it. She grew up in a war zone in Beirut, so she understands threats, and how you can mitigate risks as well. She is also the producer of this film. We have had a long journey together – making conflict zone films like Sea of Shadows and The Ivory Game was no joke. But this one felt like a different level because of the 50 per cent quote.” He smiles.”‘I did hostile-environment training and we augmented the security to a degree where I felt it wasn’t 50 per cent any more.”

An illegal airbase in the Brazilian Amazon being destroyed Credit : Courtesy of Malaika Pictures

So Ladkani joined the team, and the resulting episode is terrifying: they are patrolling the river when they find a huge illegal dredger, used for gold mining. They board the dredger, its crew of illegal miners are put in a small boat and dispatched, and Loss’s team set fire to it. Attempting to get away, they realise their boat is still attached to the dredger by a chain, and they have only moments before an oxygen tank below the deck of the dredger explodes. Loss has to shoot the chain, but he has to hit it while it is taut, or the bullet would glance off. “The oxygen tank is steel and if it had exploded we would have been killed by the fragments if we were within 100 metres of that boat – and we were six metres away. It was Hugo who shot the chain – it took 50 shots at least. When Juma saw that footage she broke down and sobbed,” says Ladkani.

Do you like your job? I ask Loss.

He smiles. “Yes I do.”

Back in the 1970s, when two major roads were originally carved into the Amazon rainforest, of which 60 per cent is in Brazil, it opened it up for settlers to devastating effects – the population of the Brazilian Amazon quadrupled and millions of acres of trees were cut down for timber or land clearance and farming, and the rivers became polluted. Thousands of garimpeiros (prospectors) arrived, bringing disease, destruction and violence.

Indigenous people from the Mura tribe in a deforested area inside the Amazon rainforest near Humaita, Amazonas State, Brazil Credit : Ueslei Marcelino/REUTERS

Despite the protected reserves created by Lula during his first tenure (2003 to 2011), when Bolsonaro took over, he vowed that he would not demarcate a single millimetre of Indigenous land.

There was reason to be hopeful when Lula was re-elected in 2023, especially when he created the Ministry for Indigenous People. But it was an uphill struggle, and Xipaia left the post of State Secretary after about two years, and retired to her territory, where she still is. “She realised that it would be years, if not decades, before change could happen and she felt that her power was with activism from the front lines rather than being in an office in the city,” says Ladkani. “And what really hurt was her children having to grow up in the city and not having the connection to nature that she had.”

Smoke from illegal fires lit by farmers rises in Manaquiri, Amazonas state Credit : MICHAEL DANTAS

There has been a lot of progress, Juma says, compared to the Bolsonaro years “when it was genocide”. “It is hard to quantify all the changes because even though there was a change in the administration, it is important to understand that the government structure is very colonialist, no matter who is in power, and everything takes time. I entered the ministry when it was just being born.

“It was hard working in an office every day and not spending time with my children, and my son Tuppak [eight] told me that he wanted to go back to the forest, he was having a hard time at school in the city. I did not want to rob my son of that kind of childhood – being in the territory and getting his knowledge from the forest.”

I ask Loss and Xipaia if, with the way things are now, they are more inclined to hope or despair. “Most of the time I don’t think about the future,” says Loss. “I just focus on doing my work, one operation at a time.”

A wildfire consumes land deforested by cattle farmers near Novo Progresso, Para state, Brazil Credit : MICHAEL DANTAS/AFP via Getty Images

Xipaia thinks. “It depends where I am. When I’m in the forest with my family, there is immense fulfilment which is hard to explain; it gives me the hope and energy to keep wanting to protect it, and I want the whole world to get to know it.

“When I walk through the forest and harvest food there with my family and my people, it reminds me of what my ancestors were doing. The innocence of children, the idea of clean water, food without toxins – this gives me hope.”

“I don’t feel despair,” says Ladkani. “I feel like we’re in a war. There are plenty of good people fighting back, and that gives me hope. And there are lives on the line that we need to care about, which is the indigenous people, who are the frontline of our defence. They are defending nature for us so we need to make sure that they are heard and seen and respected. And we hope that the film puts a human face to that.

“We can’t pretend that destroying the biggest ecosystem on the planet is OK. If we lose the Amazon, we all lose.”

Yanuni will be released later this year

News.title: Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double
News.content:
Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

News.title: Forced displacement in the West Bank could be ‘crime against humanity’, says UN report
News.content:
Israel’s forced displacement of more than 33,000 Palestinians in the West Bank could amount to a “crime against humanity” and involves “ethnic cleansing”, according to a report published by the UN.

A report by the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) said that Israeli actions in the area had sparked the “largest and longest displacement crisis in the West Bank since 1967” – the year in which Israel captured the territory.

The report said “large-scale, long-term and systematic displacement of over 33,000 Palestinians from refugee camps … during Israel’s Operation Iron Wall [which] raises serious concerns of the crime against humanity of forcible transfer”.

It added: “The documented use of airstrikes, armoured bulldozers and controlled detonations, to render entire camps uninhabitable, to force the displacement of their residents and to prevent their return, in the absence of imperative military necessity to justify such destruction and displacement, are not permissible under international law, appear to amount to collective punishment and raise concerns of ethnic cleansing.”

The 27-page report covers the period December 5, 2024 to January 31, 2026.

In January 2025, Israeli forces launched “Operation Iron Wall” in the northern West Bank in a bid to counter what they said were terrorist threats.

They destroyed hundreds of homes, cut off water and electricity, and barred humanitarian access to the Jenin, Nur Sham and Tulkarm refugee camps.

By October 2025, 52 per cent of structures in Jenin camp, 48 per cent in Nur Shams and 36 percent in Tulkarm had been destroyed or damaged.

The three camps are among 19 in the West Bank established to shelter Palestinians after the 1948 Nakba, and are administered by the UN Relief and Works Agency (UNRWA).

Although still referred to as refugee camps, they are in fact now densely packed towns.

Sports.title: Fulham 2 Crystal Palace 3: Alvaro Arbeloa sinks to another dismal defeat as new Eagle Ben Chilwell bags late winner
Sports.content:
BEN CHILWELL announced his return to English football with the goal that earned his new manager his first Premier League win.

The former Chelsea left back had only been on for three minutes when he slammed home the winner as Palace mounted a dogged comeback fight in the battle of the rookie bosses.



New Palace chief Pierre Sage swooped for Chilwell on transfer deadline day in a cut-price £8.6 million move from French side Strasbourg.

Within four days it already looks a bargain as the experienced defender struck with his first touch of the ball after coming on as a 74th minute sub.



He replaced Tyrick Mitchell who had already pulled Palace back from behind twice as the Eagles’ left backs stole the show.

England head coach Thomas Tuchel was watching from the stands at Craven Cottage having come to watch other players on display but the left- back berth has been a bit of an issue for the national team.

Mitchell and Chilwell have both played for England and while there is no chance either would be called up for this month’s Nations League fixtures, Tuchel may well have headed for home with a few surprise dilemmas on his mind.

He had come to run the rule over Palace midfielder Adam Wharton and Fulham star Josh King.



On a dismal day for Fulham and their new manager Alvaro Arbeloa at least their star performer showed a touch of class.

He scored from the right wing to put Fulham ahead in the 11th minute, then set one up from the left flank three minutes from half time.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

King, 19, was handed a dream start to the summer, being invited to train with England’s World Cup squad prior to the tournament.

While his Fulham team-mates are struggling to get to grips with the new season he at least looks raring to go as the outstanding performer on the pitch from start to finish.

With Nations League games coming up against Spain, Croatia and the Czech Republic, King looks ready to finally kick a ball in anger for his country.



But one virtuoso performance was never going to be enough to ward off hefty booing from the Fulham fans at the final whistle.

Chants of ‘What the f*****g hell was that?’ greeted the end of a game where Fulham had their first victory of the campaign in one hand only to blow it.

They remain without a point and with former Real Madrid boss Arbeloa under mounting pressure already.

Chilly, who spent six months on loan at Palace last year, grabbed the winning goal 13 minutes from the end and ensured a frosty send off for Fulham’s manager and the players as they trudged off after a particularly demoralising defeat.

King’s goal was deflected in off Palace defender Jaydee Canvot, and new boy Cesar Palacios got off the mark three minutes before half- ti.me



RECOMMENDED STORIES

But it was at the back where Fulham suffered. Mitchell beat Fulham keeper Bernd Leno at his near post to make it 2-1 and somehow squeezed a comical goal over the line in the 54th minute when fellow new arrival Gonzalo Garcia air- kicked his clearance off the line.

Chilwell thumped home the decisive strike after more clumsy work at the back for Fulham with Joachim Andersen miscueing another clearance.

Sports.title: Brentford 1 Sunderland 1: Bees hit by double blow as goal ruled out before Sunderland get controversial penalty leveller
Sports.content:
WILSON ISIDOR might not like it, but he has turned into quite the super-sub.

Last weekend he rose from the bench and bagged the winner against Fulham at the Stadium of Light.



This time he won the penalty that was confidently converted by Enzo Le Fee as Sunderland scraped a point at Brentford.

And it was nothing less than the Black Cats deserved. Dan Ballard had the ball in the net early on before his goal was chalked off for an offside that was only spotted when VAR chimed in.



And they had the better of the chances – especially in the first half, when Le Fee clattered the post with a missile of a half-volley.

Brentford will be feeling bitter at blowing their lead after going a goal up in the 57th minute through Vitaly Janelt.



Though maybe not quite as bitter as they will feel watching Sunderland head to the San Siro just before Christmas – the Black Cats having pipped them to a Europa League spot by a single point last season.

Brentford strengthened bravely over the summer with boss Keith Andrews eager to smash through their mid-table ceiling.

Mamadou Sangare started again in central midfield but was kept quieter by Sunderland than by Tottenham or Leeds, while other newbies were brought on from the bench.

But for all their summer business – Brentford’s net spend was higher than Arsenal’s – the margins are still fine between these two sides.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Bees have been devastating from set-pieces under Andrews, and their latest crafty corner routine opened up the space for Mikkel Damsgaard to drive a low cross into the box inside five minutes, but Keane Lewis-Potter was unable to thread his effort through a gaggle of bodies.

Moments later, Sunderland showed they are no mugs from a dead ball either. Bees skipper Nathan Collins got his head on a free-kick launched from deep, but the clearance fell straight to Ballard, who slotted into the bottom corner.

It was only after the celebrations and pitchside VAR review that referee Thomas Bramall disallowed it because new Black Cats signing Kevin Danso was offside while blocking Caoimhin Kelleher’s line of sight.



Revved up, Sunderland’s Le Fee clattered the woodwork before Thomas Meunier was denied by a heroic block from young substitute Jannik Schuster.

Brentford made a triple change at the break and immediately looked more threatening, with Lewis-Potter’s cross finding Igor Thiago, whose close-range header was straight at Robin Roefs.

Janelt struck a few minutes later, blasting in Nordi Mukiele’s headed clearance to break the deadlock.



And sub Jaidon Anthony thought he had made it two when he turned in Thiago’s cross, but replays showed that he had knocked it out of Roefs’ two-handed grasp and the goal was chalked off.

Isidor was causing problems by now, and when Lewis-Potter dragged him to the ground in the box late on he had done his job yet again. Le Fee then stepped up, sending Kelleher the wrong way and the travelling fans wild.

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola sets stunning new Premier League season record on Liverpool debut just days after £123million transfer
Sports.content:
BRADLEY BARCOLA has wasted no time making his mark at Liverpool after setting a stunning new Premier League record just 31 minutes into his debut.

The £123million summer signing clocked a top speed of 35.9km/h during the Reds’ 2-0 victory over Ipswich.



That made the French winger the fastest player recorded in the Premier League this season, according to FotMob.

Barcola was handed his Liverpool debut in the 64th minute, replacing Victor Munoz as boss Andoni Iraola introduced his blockbuster new arrival.



And it did not take long for the 24-year-old to showcase exactly what Liverpool have paid so heavily for.

The former Paris Saint-Germain star’s blistering pace immediately gave Ipswich’s defence another problem to deal with.

Liverpool fans had endured a lengthy transfer saga before finally seeing Barcola arrive at Anfield.

But the Frenchman’s first appearance suggests the wait could be worth it.

Barcola was pleased with the win and boss Iraola was also impressed by his cameo.

The Liverpool boss said: “I think he had good minutes. I think he has a very good pass.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

He added: “In a counter, a couple of times we didn’t find him, so we will have to learn these kinds of movements because he will be in behind, threatening all the time.”

Iraola also admitted Liverpool would need to manage Barcola carefully after his lack of competitive action.

He said: “He hasn’t played any competitive minutes since the World Cup, so we have to be a little bit more careful, but I think he has been very good.”

Barcola could now be handed his first Liverpool start when Atletico Madrid visit Anfield for their Champions League opener on Wednesday.

The France international had made it clear he wanted to leave PSG, informing the French giants that he would not sign a new contract.



Despite interest from a number of clubs, Barcola’s preference was to join Liverpool and the Reds eventually got their man.

However, he could face a battle to secure a regular starting spot.

Cody Gakpo‘s proposed move to Manchester City failed to materialise, leaving the Dutchman firmly in the Liverpool squad.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And Gakpo has already laid down a marker, setting up both of Liverpool’s goals in the win at Ipswich.

Barcola may have the speed record, but his next challenge will be proving he can turn that frightening pace into regular goals and assists for the Premier League champions.

Sports.title: Brighton 1 Leeds 1: Luka Vuskovic steps up for hosts to deny Daniel Farke after classy Jayden Bogle opener
Sports.content:
LEEDS’ unbeaten start to the season continued, but they might have been celebrating their first Premier League win at the Amex Stadium in five attempts.

Daniel Farke’s side dominated the first hour and went ahead after 14 minutes when Jayden Bogle became the first Leeds player to score at the Amex since 2012.



But they missed a host of chances to score a second. Or a third. Or even a fourth.

And they were kicking themselves when Brighton’s record signing Luka Vuskovic levelled after 71 minutes with his first goal for the club.





Leeds looked up for the fight from the first kick. Dominic Calvert-Lewin earned a talking-to from referee Stuart Attwell for laying Vuskovic out.

But Leeds were being aggressive with the ball as well. Noah Okafor dribbled through only to overrun the ball.

Then left-back Gabriel Gudmundsson outran Ferdi Kadioglu befoe Lewis Dunk rescued his team with an interception right in front of goal.

And they were ahead after 14 minutes. Calvert-Lewin was left unmarked to power in a header that Bart Verbruggen could only parry.



Ao Takana got to the loose ball first and directed it across goal for Jayden Bogle to score from point-blank.

Was Tanaka’s effort a shot or a pass? Leeds did not care.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Injury-hit Brighton looked stunned and only a superb recovery and clearance by skipper Dunk prevented Leeds going two up.

Calvert-Lewin, looking miles offside but played through by Brighton’s Babis Kostoulas, went round Verbruggen and shot at the empty net until

Dunk slid across to block.

Then Ao Tanaka’s shot hit the bar. Brighton were struggling to find any rhythm at all, their passing lacking its usual zip.



Their best effort of the first half came from Diego Gomez after 29 minutes but the Paraguayan’s powerfully-hit volley was easily dealt with by James Trafford.

Leeds should have doubled their lead three minutes into the second half when Brighton made a mess of clearing an Ethan Ampadu long throw-in.

The ball ran loose to Anton Stach but Verbruggen stuck out a leg to divert the ball to safety.

And Brighton had another let off within seconds as Tanaka netted following a free-kick only to be given offside by the narrowest of margins.

Next, Verbruggen saved from James Justin as Leeds continued to dominate.



But while Brighton were somehow only one goal behind, they were still in with a chance if they could find a moment of inspiration.

Kostoulas almost provided it after 68 minutes with a dribble past three defenders. But he ended it with a powder-puff finish straight into the arms of Trafford. But it woke the Amex crowd up and lifted the team.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And when the equaliser came, it was as simple as you like. Max De Kuyper floated a corner to the far post and Vuskovic leapt unchallenged to head in.

Now it looked like Brighton’s game to win but Pascal Gross scooped a great chance over the bar after the ball had come off Nico Elvedi’s back.

Sports.title: Man City 1 Coventry 0: Erling Haaland sinks Frank Lampard’s Sky Blues as Enzo Fernandez forced into surprise debut
Sports.content:
ENZO FERNANDEZ may be the joint most expensive player in British football history.

But the £125 million ace will have to go some to upstage Erling Haaland at his new home, the Etihad.



The Argentina World Cup star was pressed into an emergency full debut after initially being named on the bench on his first day.

And it went as well as he could have hoped – catching the eye in the first half and also having a hand in the only goal of the game.



However, as usual, it was the main man Haaland who scored it, nodding in a delicious cross by Antoine Semenyo in the first half.

You don’t take the headlines off the big guy in this part of town no matter how much you cost.



Haaland has picked up where he left off in his first World Cup, scoring three times in his club’s first three games of the season.

The Norwegian should have had more too – and could have made it much easier for his team who became increasingly ragged as the game wore on.

And against a team more clinical than Frank Lampard’s Prem new boys, they could easily have dropped points for the first time this season.

Fernandez said he has always dreamed of joining a ‘big club’ like City, and their record of winning trophies recently backs that up.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But there is no doubt they are a club in transition following the departure of Pep Guardiola after ten years at the helm in the summer.

His old assistant Enzo Maresca has won his first three Prem matches in charge and sits on top of the table – you can’t say fairer than that.

However in two of the matches so far, they have looked more like a work in progress than a team with title pedigree.

So Fernandez will know he will have to justify some of that huge transfer fee if they are to challenge this season.

Former Chelsea skipper Fernandez was initially named on the bench by his boss Maresca.



However, England ace Nico O’Reilly was injured in thewarmrup, – forcing a late rethink by the Etihad chief.

It was so late that O’Reilly was even announced in the starting line-up as the two teams warmed up ahead of kick-off.

However it soon became clear that Fernandez – wearing his new number 17 shirt – would be in from the first whistle.



Fellow new boy Iliman Ndiaye was named in the XI by Maresca and was used out on the left hand side against Frank Lampard’s men.

Coventry were still searching for their first goal since returning to the top flight – yet the hosts did their best to gift them one.

First, Gianluigi Donnarumma struggled to bring a routine pass from Abdukodir Khuasnov under control and only just prevented an embarrassing own goal.

Then Semenyo’s stray pass allowed Taiwo Awoniyi to go clean through but he pulled his shot wide.

At the other end, Rayan Cherki slipped a pass to Haaland after quickly taken free-kick but Carl Rushworth got down to make the save.



Fernandez was starting to have an impact and slipped a pass to Cherki who took a touch before firing a low shot against the post.

While City were looking good going forward, they were open at the back and Jack Rudoni got on the end of a long throw but Donnarumma got down to save.

Fernandez’s pass reached Semenyo, who whipped a cross over Rushworth’s head for Haaland to head into the unguarded net.



Barely a game goes by without the Norwegian breaking some kind of record, and here is this week’s.

This was a 20th headed goal in the Prem for Haaland – more than any other City player in the history of the competition.

Fernandez was again involved just before the break, linking up with Elliot Anderson and Cherki to tee up Haaland, who was again denied by Rushworth.

Lampard has been back here as a coach plenty of times since his brief spell as a City player ended in 2015.

So he would not have been too disheartened that his team were only one goal down at the break and still in with a shout.



But the home side looked to kill the game off with Fernandez producing a clever flick to tee up Haaland for a tap in – only for the offside flag to cut short the celebrations.

And the newly-promoted visitors took heart from that – going close to pulling level on a couple of occasions.

First sub Loum Tchaouna pounced on a mis-hit City pass and forced a smart save out of Donnarumma, with Marc Guehi thumping away the loose ball.

From the resulting throw in, it dropped nicely for Matt Grimes whose thumping low shot went the wrong side of the post with the Italian beaten.

With the visitors becoming more ambitious, they left gaps at the back and Haaland could not quite get on the end of another Semenyo cross.



Fernandez was withdrawn 15 minutes from time with the game still in the balance, making way for another big- money arrival Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Needless to say, the Argentine World Cup ace was roundly booed by the visitingfans ;– he might have to get used to that.

But still the plucky visitors pushed forward with Caleb Yirenkyi’s cross reaching Ellis Simms at the back post.

The sub tried to lift the ball over Donnarumma but it hit the Italian – who knew little about it – flush in the face.

City held on – but it was far from convincing from Maresca’s new look team.

Sports.title: Cardiff star Krystian Bielik appears to grab young fan by NECK before supporter ‘slaps’ him in shocking scenes
Sports.content:
CARDIFF midfielder Krystian Bielik appeared to grab a young fan by the THROAT in a shocking bust-up.

The Championship showdown between Portsmouth and Cardiff came to a halt in the 70th minute.



The altercation started when Bielik was trying to retrieve the ball for a throw-in in front of the home fans.

The former Arsenal youngster then appeared to grab the fan by the neck in unsavoury scenes.



The supporter in question was then seen escorted out by stewards shortly alongside his family.

Portsmouth won the game 2-0, making it a doubly poor day for Bielik.

Goals from Conor Shaughnessy and Marezi Marezi got the job done for the home side.

Bielik was not punished for the incident, though he did pick up a booking in the ninth minute of the contest.



It remains to be seen whether or not retrospective action will be taken against the Pole once the incident is reviewed.

But it’s quite incredible he wasn’t shown a second yellow card at the very least.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Social media has been in uproar over what many perceive to be a gross over-reaction from the player.

One fan wrote: “I hope the Bielik gets some punishment for this. You cannot do this just for not giving him the ball!”



Another posted: “Amazed that the kid got thrown out here and not Bielik, he should be banned for the season.”

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest 0 Tottenham 0: Spurs’ search for Prem goal goes on as hosts have strike controversially ruled out
Sports.content:
MAYBE Sandro Tonali’s Tottenham luck is turning – even if it will not have felt like it at the time.

Spurs’ £100million man was having another underwhelming game which looked set to get a whole lot worse midway through the second half.



The Italian had somehow missed his clearance from a Morgan Gibbs-White shot which then bobbled over the line, with the help of Neco Williams who bravely dived headfirst towards the ball as a desperate Tonali tried to hack it away.

Tonali lay in the net as the City Ground erupted, no doubt thinking of the flak set to come his way yet again since joining Spurs for a record fee.



But then came a massive stroke of fortune for the 26-year-old as the goal was chalked off by VAR which had spotted Williams touching the ball with his hand as it crept over the line.

It felt harsh because the Welshman was only putting his hands up to protect himself from being kicked in the face by Tonali but, the officials will argue, rules is rules.

Cue massive relief from Tonali and his boss Roberto De Zerbi, who had been bracing himself for three straight league defeats to kick off the campaign after splashing more than £300m.

In the end his Spurs side – which included Mykhailo Mudryk as a late sub – did grind out their first point of the season, even if they are still goal-less in three.

It did not mask another disjointed display lacking in creativity and dynamism, but given the circumstances, De Zerbi and Tonali will certainly take it.

Mudryk’s heart must have been racing as he took his place on the bench before the game for his first competitive match since November 2024.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Spurs’ Hail Mary deadline day signing, brought in on loan from Chelsea, has not been allowed to play in that time due to a doping ban which was resolved in July.

Sporting the exact same get-up of black jumper, black trousers and white trainers, rival bosses Roberto De Zerbi and Oliver Glasner coached their new sides from the edge of their technical areas throughout the game.

They watched what could certainly be described as a competitive game – but also a dull one.

There were plenty of robust challenges, a few which left Spurs stars Sandro Tonali and Micky van de Ven on the floor, only for ref Craig Pawson to tell them to get up.

Savio, the £85m capture from Manchester City as part of Spurs’ massive spend, made his league debut here and showed some flashes of skill down the right-hand side.



Tottenham’s fans serenaded the Brazilian and his dancing feet with a new chant to the tune of ‘Gold’ by Spandau Ballet.

But it was his fellow arrival from City, Omar Marmoush, who really should have put Tottenham ahead on 17 minutes.

Holding off Neco Williams, loan star Marmoush raced onto a ball over the top from Pedro Porro, controlled it but then fired wide of the far post.

That was about it from Spurs in the first half, but it was hardly like Forest were creating anything either.



The best they could conjure up was a Jair Cunha drive which fizzed over, while James McAtee’s awful free-kick in stoppage time summed up the opening period.

That made it five straight halves of Premier League football this term for Spurs without a goal and you could sense them upping the ante after the break.

They almost had the breakthrough too ten minutes into the second period when Micky van de Ven got in front of Matz Sels to divert Savio’s corner just the wrong side of the post.

Sensing his side losing momentum, Glasner introduced £22m new-boy Daniel Munoz to a standing ovation.

And it was then Forest who had the big moments, both involving Williams.



First the Welshman was crashed into in the box by Mohammed Kudus, but nothing was given.

Then came the game’s main flashpoint.

McAtee rolled a neat ball through to Gibbs-White who clips it over Kinsky goal-bound.



Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke were both in a position to clear it but the latter left it to the Italian, who missed with his attempt.

The ball appeared to be bouncing in but brave Williams was there to make sure of it as Tonali desperately tried to get back to hack it away.

Forest were celebrating what they thought was the opener – only to find out that VAR had ruled it out for handball against Williams.

It left the player and all observers wondering what he was supposed to do, given he would have been kicked in the face had he not put his hands up.

Spurs responded to their let-off by bringing on Mudryk, while Marmoush was barracked with taunts of “What a waste of money” as he smashed a shot well wide.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

It ended a stalemate which, given Spurs’ results, represents progress for De Zerbi.

But it is the first time since 1974-75 they have failed to net in their opening three league games.

Sports.title: Why is Nottingham Forest star Daniel Munoz wearing a mask?
Sports.content:
NOTTINGHAM FOREST are taking on Tottenham at the City Ground – and Daniel Munoz has made his debut.

The flying wing-back has come on in the second half to a standing ovation and fans have spotted that he is wearing a protective mask.



SunSport brings you the reason why.

Why is Nottingham Forest star Daniel Munoz wearing a mask?

Munoz is wearing a protective mask while playing for Nottingham Forest after the Colombian had nose surgery in the summer.



Forest boss Oliver Glasner confirmed: “He played in a mask at Everton because he had surgery on his nose for his breathing.”

The wing-back was an ever-present under Glasner during his Crystal Palace tenure.

The Austrian manager will be hoping Munoz can hit the same heights at the City Ground.

He made the £22million move north of the country just days before the transfer window slammed shut.

On the switch, Munoz said: “I’m really excited because I can see so much talent, Forest is a team with great players, great qualities and great skills on the pitch, I can’t wait to get out there so I can help my new team-mates and I think that we’re going to do great things.

“It is a club that’s fought hard in recent years, it has competed hard, it got to the semi-finals of the Europa League and I think it has even greater objectives for the future, and really this is what I like about Forest, and that’s why I decided to come here.”

Sports.title: Le Fee penalty rescues draw for Sunderland at Brentford
Sports.content:
Enzo Le Fee rescued a point for Sunderland after dispatching his late penalty to secure a 1-1 draw at Brentford.

The Bees broke the deadlock just before the hour mark thanks to Vitaly Janelt's well-taken effort into the top left corner, only for referee Thomas Bramall to point to the spot in the 82nd minute to penalise Keane Lewis-Potter for holding Wilson Isidor inside the box.

The full-back did not have eyes on the ball while making contact and after being confirmed by VAR, Le Fee stepped up to dispatch it into the bottom right corner.

"We can do better, I always look at us," Brentford boss Keith Andrews said in his post-match press conference.

"I wasn't bowled over with the officiating today, though, which I rarely say.

"I don't tend to go on about officials too much. I will talk myself into trouble but I didn't like the flow of the game; there were incidents where it was not under control."

A point marked a fair return for both sides in a game where momentum swung in favour of both teams at different stages of the contest.

Sunderland, who switched to a back five for this fixture, had started the better side and came close to an opener in the first half after Dan Ballard's goal was disallowed following a lengthy VAR review and Le Fee hit the post with a fierce strike from range.

"It is a shame," Regis Le Bris said after the game regarding Ballard's goal, which was ruled out due to debutant Kevin Danso being offside. "If you need four and a half minutes to make a decision, it means you are hesitating."

Half-time changes from Keith Andrews - replacing Michael Kayode, Mamadou Sangare and Dango Ouattara with Aaron Hickey, Yehor Yarmoliuk and Anthony - inspired fresh impetus going forward.

Their unbeaten start to the season continues but marks the second consecutive week the Bees have squandered a lead late on and were forced to settle for a point following the 1-1 at Leeds United last time out.

Andrews: We were off our usual levels

Brentford boss Keith Andrews:

"It had a lot in it, the game. In the first half, we didn't hit the levels we had. The way they played was very good.

"We were a little bit off it and in the second half we did the basics very well. It allowed us to have control and more territory; we looked more like us and got ourselves in front.

"There were then decisions that went for us and did not go for us.

"I knew it would be a very difficult game today. It was a proper game. If I am in the stand and watching from afar, it is what the Premier League is all about. Going toe-to-toe with a good team and good coach."

Le Bris: We dominated but Brentford switched the momentum

Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris:

"First half, we were dominant and created four big chances in the first 30 minutes.

"We managed this part of the game but didn't score. It is always a big shame.

"They changed three players and it switched the momentum. They scored but the lads were still in the game.

"We know we are good when we are behind. The subs helped."

Sports.title: Aberdeen and Kilmarnock end losing streaks with draw
Sports.content:
Aberdeen and 10-man Kilmarnock battled out a tetchy 0-0 Premiership draw at Pittodrie as both sides brought their losing streaks to an end.

Quality chances were at a premium with Aberdeen's Tony Yogane hitting the inside of the post in the first half but Dons goalkeeper Marius Muller was the busier goalkeeper throughout.

Aaron Tshibola saw red for the visitors for a second booking with eight minutes remaining but Aberdeen were unable to capitalise on the extra man.

In the first of a double-header between the sides, they meet again at Rugby Park in the Premier Sports Cup next weekend, both were looking to arrest poor league form.

Aberdeen had not scored in their previous three league games, having only taken points from their opening day win over Hearts at Pittodrie.

Killie had lost all four of their Premiership matches so far, and were keen to avoid becoming the first side to lose their first five of the season - the last having been current Killie boss Neil McCann's Dundee side in 2018.

Both managers made changes, with Aberdeen making four after the defeat at Celtic in midweek, and McCall swapping three after the loss to St Mirren.

The home side showed some smart early initiative as Stuart Armstrong and Kevin Nisbet combined to create an opening after just two minutes, but Armstrong opted for an extra pass and the chance was gone.

Killie captain Greg Kiltie flashed wide of the left-hand upright from 20 yards, before, midway through the first half, Aberdeen's Nesta Guinness-Walker threw himself in front of a Jamie Brandon effort after Mitchy Ntelo gave away possession cheaply in midfield.

Aberdeen moved Lewis Smith infield and he flashed an effort over the bar, before Yogane curled an effort off the inside of the far post after cutting inside from a Smith pass.

Muller pushed another Kiltie effort past the far post and Aberdeen's Dan Happe saw a header held by Max Stryjek as the first half drew to a close.

The home side made a triple change at the interval, switching to a 3-4-1-2 formation, and soon after sub Toyosi Olusanya just failed to connect with a ball across goal which was put wide by Smith at the back post.

That sparked a period of pressure that saw an Ayoub Mouloua header held by Stryjek, after McCann had been booked following a VAR review of a potential handball in the Killie box.

Armstrong saw an effort from distance held, before Muller pushed a Cathal McCarthy header over and then impressively denied Kiltie from point-blank range.

Image: Referee John Beaton shows Kilmarnock's Aaron Tshibola a red card

Tshibola was denied by the masked Muller, the goalkeeper diving high to his left to push a 25-yard free-kick over.

Ten minutes from time, good hold-up play from Mouloua created an opening for Chris Cadden, his effort blocked by a sliding challenge from George Stanger.

Killie were reduced to 10 men when Tshibola was dismissed for a challenge on Mats Knoester, having been booked for a first-half foul on Smith.

Sports.title: Norwich ease to win at Sheff Utd
Sports.content:
Norwich secured a first away victory of the Sky Bet Championship season with a strong performance in a 3-1 win at Sheffield United.

Goals from Anthony Musaba, Mohamed Toure and Mathias Kvistgaarden earned them the three points, with Patrick Bamford scoring for the hosts.

Musaba struck in the eighth minute with a curling effort. Goalkeeper Michael Cooper got a hand to the ball but could not keep it out.

The visitors maintained their early pressure with Andre Brooks screwing a shot wide and then putting another straight at Cooper. Playing against the team he left this summer, the lively Brooks also fired wide from a corner.

The Blades began to pose more of an attacking threat, with Sydie Peck forcing a save from Vladan Kovacevic at his near post and the keeper turning a Romelle Donovan shot wide.

The equaliser came in the 23rd minute when Ben Brereton Diaz found Tyrese Campbell and he laid the ball off to Bamford who beat Kovacevic with a curling effort from just outside the area.

Brereton Diaz shot wide and Campbell had a low shot saved before Norwich regained the lead a minute before the break. Anis Slimane sent Toure clear and the striker slipped the ball past Cooper one-on-one.

Cooper had to stand up well to Musaba, making an important save at his near post, while Toure failed to direct a header on target when the ball was whipped in from the left.

The fourth goal of the game came in the 62nd minute, with substitute Kvistgaarden finding the net with a low shot shortly after joining the action.

Hamza Choudhury appeared to have made a second goal-line clearance in rapid succession, but the referee ruled that the ball had crossed the line.

Sheffield United never looked likely to stage a comeback, with their attack lacklustre. Their best effort of the second half was a firm drive from substitute Kalvin Phillips which flew wide.

Ben Chrisene made a vital challenge to nick the ball away from Bamford in the area in the closing stages as Norwich defended resolutely.

The defeat was Sheffield United's first of the season in any competition.

Sports.title: Portsmouth see off Cardiff
Sports.content:
Goals from defender Conor Shaughnessy and Marezi earned Portsmouth their first home win of the season as they beat Cardiff 2-0 on an emotional afternoon at Fratton Park.

The south-coast side paid a poignant pre-match tribute to former goalkeeper Alan Knight, who sadly passed away this week aged 65.

Knight played 801 games for Pompey and also served them as coach and ambassador, and both sets of players lined up around the centre circle for an impeccably-observed minute's silence.

The hosts handed debuts to transfer deadline-day signings Tyrese Shade and Jayden Meghoma.

Cardiff could have opened the scoring after only three minutes when Krystian Bielik headed wide from a Joel Bagan free-kick.

Adrian Segecic had Pompey's first clear chance when his long-range effort was tipped wide by Nathan Trott following an initial poor clearance from the Cardiff goalkeeper.

Portsmouth should have taken the lead after 23 minutes when Marezi headed wide from close range.

A minute later Terry Devlin also failed to keep his header on target from Segecic's low free-kick.

The home side broke the deadlock 14 minutes before half-time when Shaughnessy sent a looping header into the net from new boy Shade's long throw.

Marezi then shanked another presentable chance wide from a tight angle after John Mousinho's men had hit Cardiff on the counter-attack.

Serbian Marezi made amends for his first-half misses by doubling Pompey's lead seven minutes after the re-start.

Segecic picked out Marezi with a pin-point cross and the big striker swept the ball past the helpless Trott.

Marezi thought he had scored his second and Pompey's third when he nodded in Meghoma's cross, only for the goal to be ruled out for offside.

Pompey looked vulnerable defensively, but Cardiff lacked the killer edge to ever look like taking full advantage.

The second from bottom Bluebirds are still waiting for their first Championship win since last season's promotion from League One.

Frustrations boiled over in the final 15 minutes when Cardiff defender Bielik appeared to grab a home fan around the throat.

Pompey almost added a third when Abu Kamara was denied by the crossbar while captain Marlon Pack also had a header from a tight angle blocked.

Cian Ashford almost reduced the deficit in the last minute of the 90 but his shot from the edge of the penalty area proved no match for Pompey goalkeeper Daniel Bielica.
