Sports.title: West Brom edge past Watford
Sports.content:
Jimmy-Jay Morgan's fifth goal of the season extended West Brom's bright start with a 1-0 home win over Watford in the Championship.

The 20-year-old, a £1.3million summer signing, scored in the 36th minute for his third Championship strike and first at The Hawthorns to extend Albion's unbeaten home record to 10 matches.

It was a game of two halves, with Morgan denied twice and Aune Heggebo once in the first half, while Watford missed two chances after the break.

Watford are now winless away from home in their last nine trips, since February.

Intense pressing on Albion's midfield saw Watford threaten first when Othmane Maamma forced goalkeeper Max O'Leary into a vital block with his leg.

Maamma's opportunity came when Hector Kyprianou dispossessed Ousmane Diakite and Martin Payero ran from deep before slipping in the Moroccan forward to his right.

Albion responded when Morgan's low shot was blocked by goalkeeper Federico Ravaglia after Chris Mepham's long pass into the striker.

Albion had the ball in the net in the 34th minute, but Morgan appeared to head the ball out of Ravaglia's hands from Nolan Galves' deflected cross and it was disallowed for a foul.

The cheers were somewhat muted but the booking for Morgan seemed harsh.

But the hosts did not have long to wait to break the deadlock.

Morgan tapped home Harry Whitwell's cutback after the latter burst into the box from Isaac Price's cross in the 36th minute.

Watford, who introduced Edo Kayembe for left-back Jordan Zemura at half-time, twice threatened soon after the restart.

Spaniard Iker Bravo's first-time shot was blocked from Luca Kjerrumgaard's cross.

Then Payero hooked over the bar from close range after Maamma headed down Edoardo Bove's deep cross at the far post.

Whitwell was showing his potential and Kayembe was booked for wrestling him to the ground as he charged down the right in the 63rd minute.

Watford threatened again when Bravo could only glance weakly straight at O'Leary from Keben's inviting centre.

But Albion missed the chance to double their lead in the 71st minute.

Whitwell slid Heggebo clean through with a lovely reverse pass and the Norway striker tried to lift his shot over Ravaglia only for the keeper to smuggle it behind for a corner.

Substitute Stephy Mavididi had the chance to level it but the forward blazed high over the bar after twisting inside his marker on the angle.

Albion appeared to be denied a penalty at the death when substitute Felix Horn Myhre seemed to be pushed over on the ball from Keben.

In a melee seconds later, Bravo was booked after pushing substitute Jayson Molumby in the corner.

Sports.title: Millwall thump four past Bolton
Sports.content:
Lyndon Dykes scored his first two goals for injury-hit Millwall as they returned to winning ways in the Sky Bet Championship in some style with a 4-0 victory over Bolton at The Den.

The Lions made light of the fact they have 11 first team players currently unavailable - and that their last two games ended in heavy defeat - as they inflicted a third loss in a row on the Trotters.

A late burst of three goals in nine minutes gave the final score an emphatic look, while both teams finished with 10 men after Millwall midfielder Jenson Metcalfe and Bolton captain Josh Sheehan were sent off for violent conduct.

Bolton had a big chance to grab an early lead when Sam Dalby played a one-two with Sheehan before scuffing wide from inside the box.

The away side were growing in confidence as Sheehan had time to control before getting away a shot that was held by Millwall goalkeeper Max Crocombe.

But it was Millwall who claimed a much-needed lead in the 38th minute when Metcalfe hung up a corner to the back post where Caleb Taylor rose highest to head in.

Dykes almost doubled the advantage early in the second half with an audacious lob from 40 yards that Bolton goalkeeper Jack Bonham was relieved to see drop over his crossbar.

The Trotters then came close to an equaliser twice in the space of a minute, with Crocombe first having to make a good save to turn an effort from half-time substitute Ruben Rodrigues behind.

The resulting corner was then cleared as far as Xavier Simons who crashed a tremendous first-time strike from just outside the box against the bar.

Millwall then had a big chance to make the game safe when debutant Yanis Issoufou's backheel put Jordi Osei-Tutu through, but Bonham stood tall to make an important save.

Taylor then fluffed an opportunity to score his second after Metcalfe's free-kick was allowed to run through to him before Gale's shot across goal needed tipping behind by Crocombe at the other end.

The Lions then made the game safe in the 83rd minute when Bonham allowed Dykes to nick a harmless-looking Camiel Neghli long ball off his toes and walk the ball into the net.

There were then a pair of red cards three minutes later when Metcalfe and Sheehan were both sent off after getting into a fight.

Dykes added his second in the 88th minute when he beat Bonham at his near post after Zak Sturge had nipped in ahead of Max Conway in the Bolton area.

And there was still time for the Lions to score a fourth in stoppage time when Issoufou played the ball through for Neghli to apply a composed finish.

The managers

Millwall's Alex Neil:

"As far as I'm concerned, the kid dragged his boot over the top of Jenson's head.

"I think Jenson thought he tried to kick him in the head - whether he did or not, the lad (Sheehan) can only answer that himself.

"After that, it was handbags, everybody starts coming in and it's just a kerfuffle.

"A week's a long time in football, isn't it? A week ago, we'd just come off the back of Bristol [City] and Norwich and we're all thinking 'here we go.'

"Then we lose a couple of games, we sell Femi [Azeez, to Brighton] at the end of the window, then we lose 10 or 12 players [to injury].

"So, it's been a testing week, and there's been a bit of frustration in that we can't put our best foot forward, in terms of competing and trying to win games.

"But I thought today was really important for us to have a good reaction."

Bolton's Steven Schumacher:

"I think it's an unnecessary red card, on our point, because when Josh falls on top of Metcalfe and drags him on top of him, I was right in front of it.

"He hasn't made any movement to move his leg towards the player's head, it was just a natural sort of momentum, the way he falls on top of him.

"Then I think because of Metcalfe's reaction, and the way the melee happened, with so many players involved in it, the referee thinks it's more of an issue than it actually was.

"If they just zoom in and have a look at it, they'll see it, so hopefully that'll get rescinded.

"We lost a man to injury after we made all our subs, so that gave them a numerical advantage when we were chasing the game.

"Up until the 83rd minute, when Lewis Brunt went off [injured], we were more than a match for Millwall."

Sports.title: Hull City v Aston Villa: Premier League – live
Sports.content:
7m ago 13.17 EDT Half-time: Hull 0-0 Aston Villa After some appeals for a Villa penalty as Mendy nudges Jackson out of the way of Maatsen’s cross and Belloumi wastes a delivery at the other end, Michael Oliver blows for the break. Jackson had the best chance, with his head, inside two minutes. Barkley has tested Tzolakis as well, but Hull look good for at least a point so far. Share

9m ago 13.15 EDT 45 min: Cash can’t keep a Jackson pass from rolling out for a goal-kick. One minute added. Share

10m ago 13.14 EDT 44 min: Hull’s cautious press keeps Villa in their own third for a bit. Share Updated at 13.15 EDT

12m ago 13.12 EDT 42 min: Giles wins a Hull corner off a sliding Cash. Belloumi’s delivery is headed out by Barkley and then the flag goes up for the cross back into the box. Villa are dealing with Hull’s set pieces a bit better than Manchester United on the opening weekend. Share

14m ago 13.10 EDT 40 min: Michael Oliver’s yellow card comes out as Jackson rolls Ajayi and the Hull defender brings him down. Buendía stands over the free-kick, some 25 yards out and left of centre … and the Hull fans wave it on its way, some distance over the bar. Share

16m ago 13.08 EDT 38 min: Belloumi drops a shoulder, shifts the ball on to his left and hits a tame shot bouncing into Suzuki’s grasp. The Villa keeper is tested again as Giles bounds through a couple of flimsy challenges and lays it off for Slater to strike. The midfielder’s effort is low and easily gathered by Suzuki down to his right. View image in fullscreen Regan Slater arrows a shot towards goal. Photograph: Ian Hodgson/Reuters Share Updated at 13.16 EDT

18m ago 13.06 EDT 36 min: McBurnie caught Cash in the face with an elbow as they challenged for the Tzolakis free-kick forward. The Villa right-back is receiving treatment and just checks all his teeth are still intact before returning to the field. Share

20m ago 13.04 EDT 34 min: Jackson comes short for a ball that has eluded him since his early chance. The flag goes up as he collects it. Hull launch the free-kick forward and Slater’s drive from the edge of the box is well struck but flies over. Share

22m ago 13.02 EDT 32 min: Stroud forces a throw-in off Maatsen for Hull near the corner flag. Mings miscues a header and sends the ball spinning out for a corner – Suzuki gets his fists to it in a crowded six-yard box. Share

24m ago 13.00 EDT 30 min: Hull are happy to sit in for a little bit. Villa knock it from side to side. Mendy charges forward from centre-back and clatters into Mings on halfway. He’s providing a bit of entertainment, for sure. Share

26m ago 12.58 EDT 28 min: Villa’s spell of pressure ends with Mings shooting high and wide from distance. Share

28m ago 12.56 EDT 26 min: Tzolakis saves from Barkley! McGinn dummies the low ball into the box and Barkley meets it about 15 yards out. He scuffs his shot low and Tzolakis gets his fingertips to it to touch it past the post. The corner comes to nothing. Share

30m ago 12.54 EDT 24 min: McGinn’s inswinging corner breaks to Maatsen on the left of the penalty area. Villa go all the way back to Suzuki before McGinn’s low cross is punted clear by Mendy. Where’s Austin MacPhee when you need him? Share

32m ago 12.52 EDT 22 min: Mendy shows his defensive qualities by stopping Cash’s surge into the box and conceding a corner … Share

34m ago 12.50 EDT 20 min: Belloumi is a lovely player to watch. He glides inside again from the Hull right, lays the ball off to Mendy and the defender whacks a speculative effort well wide. Villa then beat the press but Buendía can’t find the right pass when approaching the final third and a dangerous move ends there. Share

36m ago 12.48 EDT 18 min: McGinn finds Buendía in a pocket of space with a cute pass. Buendia shifts it to Jackson, who is forced wide and whose cross is hopeful if nothing else. Emery looks pleased with what he’s seeing on the touchline. Share

38m ago 12.46 EDT 16 min: Villa enjoy a fair bit of the ball in the Hull half. A fast break for the hosts is stunted by midfielder Gourna-Douath’s inability to get a quick pass away. Share

40m ago 12.44 EDT 14 min: Hemmings comes close to his first senior goal – the 19-year-old is fed in the box by Barkley but his left-footed shot is kept out by Tzolakis, who closes his legs just in time. There’s a good pace to this. Share

42m ago 12.42 EDT 12 min: Belloumi jinks past Barkley and gives Villa a scare down the Hull right. His ball into the box is cut out and Villa try to settle into a rhythm. Share Updated at 12.42 EDT

44m ago 12.41 EDT “Afternoon, Billy,” writes Benjamin on email. “Was at a loose end so went to Whaddon Road to see Cheltenham Town contrive to draw from 2-0 ahead with Grimsby, and an unexpected encounter with Villa alum Andreas Weimann leading the line and scoring for the Robins. “Now settled in the pub and hoping to see some new faces gelling quickly for current Villa - which we’re apparently obliged to call ‘Emery’s Villa 2.0’. With all due respect to Hull’s performances so far, I’d really hope that Villa can put something together today to show that the wheels are still somewhere in the vicinity of being on.” Whaddon Road – nice little ground, I lived down the road for a few months. Share Updated at 12.42 EDT

46m ago 12.38 EDT 8 min: Centre-back Mendy goes for goal from the, erm, halfway line. It bounces well short of Suzuki, who might feel a bit offended as he picks up the ball. Hull’s tails are up though. They are getting some joy down the left. Share

48m ago 12.36 EDT 6 min: Giles gets into good space down the Hull left, arrives at the byline and crosses low for McBurnie. The striker can’t quite get a toe on the ball as Suzuki comes out to collect. Share

50m ago 12.34 EDT 4 min: Hull settle into some possession. The place is bouncing. View image in fullscreen Hull’s Elliot Stroud on the move. Photograph: Bruce Rollinson/PA Share Updated at 12.40 EDT

52m ago 12.32 EDT 2 min: Jackson heads wide! Early chance for Villa as Maatsen crosses from the left, Jackson rises between the Hull centre-backs and heads it back beyond the near post. Share Updated at 12.33 EDT

54m ago 12.30 EDT Kick-off After the PR announcer says a very boisterous hello to all four stands of the MKM Stadium in turn, the football mercifully comes to our rescue. Villa get us under way in sky blue and claret. Hull would go top of the Premier League with a healthy win … Share

1h ago 12.26 EDT Here come the teams. Hull have won two, Villa have lost two – but I’d say it’s pretty tough to call. Share

1h ago 12.18 EDT “I am looking forward to watching how we will respond,” says Unai Emery as his Aston Villa team come into this off the back of two opening defeats and a tumultuous transfer window. double quotation mark We are trying to build again our structure as strong as possible. Today is a new opportunity to try to get better. Our preparation was good last week. We were close, more or less, to be in a good shape with the players [against Arsenal]. Today is a new challenge against Hull City, who are performing fantastically. Already they are confident. This is our challenge. The last Villa manager to come here in the Premier League was Paul Lambert, who was sacked the day after a 2-0 defeat in February 2015. View image in fullscreen Unai is here. Photograph: Richard Sellers/PA Share Updated at 12.25 EDT

1h ago 12.11 EDT “Easy to say, three in a row,” smiles Hull Sergej Jakirovic in his pre-match interview, playing down the significance of a possible third win out of three since promotion for Hull. double quotation mark I know Aston Villa had a lot of changes. They sold a lot of players – a lot of good players. This is also our chance today to push them. Maybe there is pressure on them but they are used to this. Share

1h ago 12.04 EDT Hull’s Lucas Herrington: ‘Zlatan told me not to fear anyone in the Premier League’ Herrington made the headlines this summer with his impressive displays as an 18-year-old centre-back for Australia at the World Cup – before missing a decisive penalty in their shootout exit to Egypt in the last 32. Zlatan Ibrahimovic offered to have a chat with the Colorado Rapids defender after that penalty miss. Herrington, who turns 19 today, has since sealed a move to the Premier League and sat down for an interview with Joey Lynch this week … double quotation mark Zlatan said: ‘Really, don’t fear anyone; I’m here for a reason, so just go enjoy it.’ It’s a great league; he played in it. His message was just to go have fun, and don’t fear anything. Go, work hard, be yourself … because it’s a great experience to play in the Premier League. Read more … Lucas Herrington staying grounded at Hull City despite meteoric rise: ‘It’s pretty crazy’ Read more Share

1h ago 11.55 EDT It’s fair to say Aston Villa are have operated in a totally different transfer market to Hull this summer – they’ve spent over £250m and still made a healthy profit after the sales of Morgan Rogers and Ollie Watkins. Hull have shelled out over £150m on virtually an entire other team but not recouped nearly as much. Hull arrivals: Nobel Mendy (£20m), Konstantinos Tzolakis (£20m), Lucas Herrington (£17.1m), Ilyas Ansah (£14.5m), Tim Iroegbunam (£13m), Mohamed-Ali Cho (£13m), Christos Mouzakitis (£12.9m), Brooke Norton-Cuffy (£12m), Jens Hjertø-Dahl (£10m), Sorba Thomas (£7.5m), Joe Gelhardt (£6.5m), Jack Butland (£3.5m), Lucas Gourna-Douath (£3.4m), Elliot Stroud (£3m), Robinio Vaz (loan), Hidemasa Morita (free), Matt Targett (free), Oscar Zambrano (undisc.)

Total spend: £156.4m

Transfer balance: -£141.6m Aston Villa arrivals: Johan Mamzambi (£51m), Nicolas Jackson (£47.5m), Ibrahim Mbaye (£47m), João Gomes (£34m), Zion Suzuki (£30m), Taylor Harwood-Bellis (£25m), Matteo Ruggeri (£21.4m), Leon Goretzka (free), Aaron Wan-Bissaka (loan), Alejandro Garnacho (loan)

Total spend: £255.9m

Transfer balance: +£60.7m Share

2h ago 11.42 EDT Starting lineups Hull make one change from their 1-0 win against Coventry last Saturday as Lucas Gourna-Douath replaces Hidemasa Morita in midfield. The scorer of the winner at Coventry, Liam Millar, has since joined Birmingham. There are four deadline-day signings on the bench. Hull (3-4-3): Tzolakis; Ajayi, Egan, Mendy; Coyle, Slater, Gourna-Douath, Giles; Belloumi, McBurnie, Stroud

Subs: Phillips, Thomas, Hjertø-Dahl, Norton-Cuffy, Herrington, Targett, Mouzakitis, Vaz, Cho Tyrone Mings for Pau Torres at centre-back is Villa’s only change from their 1-0 defeat to Arsenal last Monday. Ibrahim Mbaye is on the bench after his £47m move from PSG. Aston Villa (4-2-3-1): Suzuki; Cash, Lindelöf, Mings, Maatsen; Kamara, Barkley; McGinn, Buendía, Hemmings; Jackson

Subs: Bizot, Ruggeri, Torres, Garnacho, Abraham, Mbaye, Bogarde, Wan-Bissaka, Alysson The referee is Michael Oliver – the best in the country. Share Updated at 11.43 EDT

Sports.title: Haaland edges Manchester City past Coventry as Fernández sparkles on debut
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernández started for Manchester City after Nico O’Reilly’s back injury during the warm-up and sparkled to show why the club paid a British record-equalling £125m for the midfielder.

The winner, for a stuttering home team, came courtesy of Erling Haaland’s 300th club goal and Fernández had a key cameo, feeding Antoine Semenyo, whose cross from the right was crashed home.

In the second half, particularly, Coventry hammered away, but their wait for a first top-flight goal since Mustapha Hadji’s on 5 May 2001 goes on.

The visitors will not like losing, but can be heartened by holding the star-studded hosts to a slender win, though the bottom line is all three of their Premier League outings on their return have been defeats. Enzo Maresca’s men have a maximum nine points so can be supremely satisfied at the start under the Italian.

Ayoubb Bouaddi, bought for £85m, was on the bench for those in blue, as Fernández lined up alongside Rayan Cherki in a 4-1-2–2-1 that had Semenyo and Iliman Ndiaye, another new home signing, stationed behind Haaland.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Fernández shoots at goal on his Manchester City debut. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

Coventry, arriving having lost 4-0 on aggregate so far in the league, changed Caleb Yirenkyi and Loum Tchaouna for Ethan Pinnock and Frank Onyeka, and Taiwo Awoniyi should have bridged the 25 years to Hadji when a too-short Semenyo pass meant for Rúben Dias was intercepted.

But when the striker ran in on goal his radar failed, and the shot was pulled wide. A second scare came after Abdukodir Khusanov fed the ball to Gianluigi Donnarumma, it slipped under his boot, and the goalkeeper scrambled – just – to prevent the goal

The longer Coventry stayed level the far better their prospects. So when Cherki fed a galloping Haaland and he twisted and let fly, Carl Rushworth’s save was priceless. Then Dazzling Cherki footwork – after Fernández’s ball – was followed by a shot which struck a post.

The frame of the goal and Rushworth could do nothing to stop Haaland’s opener, though. This time Fernández curved a pass in behind for Semenyo, the right winger spun the ball over, and Haaland did the rest.

This was 25 minutes in and Coventry were under siege – as those in blue would be after the break.

Fernández collected along the right, looked up, and flipped over a cross aimed for Haaland but it failed to beat the first man. Then Cherki, again in Fred Astaire mode, made space and saw an effort blocked.

Maresca wants his wingers to be more direct – utilising the pace of Ndiaye and Semenyo – and the tactic continually spun Coventry. So, too, did an impish Cherki flick which put Haaland careering in again: he rode a challenge when going down might have brought a penalty, before shooting. Rushworth once more thwarted the Norwegian.

View image in fullscreen Frank Lampard and the Coventry players applaud the away fans but their wait for a Premier League goal goes on. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

After Awoniyi’s early miss, Jack Rudoni did far better with a header – at close-range he had Donnarumma flying left to prevent the equaliser. This showed the hope Frank Lampard’s men carried but they had to finish any chance fashioned as these were scarce.

Ndiaye was quietish on debut and when Cherki’s work took the ball to him in the area he should have pulled the trigger but refused. Coventry came close to punishing this at a free-kick that bounced about the area and Maresca, seeing enough, replaced Cherki with Foden.

Still Coventry threatened. Tchaouna, on as a replacement, skated forward and drew a Donnarumma save and from the resulting corner Matt Grimes sprayed wide. Now came Bouaddi’s debut, on for Fernández after 75 minutes – Maresca asking the 18-year-old No 6 to steady a wobbly Manchester City ship – and he showed composure and class.

When Ndiaye found Haaland, the ball was turned to Foden and his attempt went close to a second for Maresca’s side. As did Ellis Sims for Coventry. Donnarumma beat a point-blank effort out as those in blue suffered a late-game bombardment.

Sports.title: Tottenham fire blanks in draw at Nottingham Forest after Williams goal ruled out
Sports.content:
For the third successive league match, Tottenham failed to score and this time they did not even muster a shot on target. Excluding a 5-1 win against a Charlton B team in the Carabao Cup, their season so far reads: five goals against and none scored. For a couple of minutes Nottingham Forest thought they had added to that goals-against tally but Neco Williams was adjudged to have handled when stooping to head in on the goalline as Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke attempted to prevent Morgan Gibbs-White’s deflected effort bobbling into the net.

The mood music surrounding Roberto De Zerbi has been overwhelmingly positive since the Italian arrived at the end of March and led the rescue mission; see the Birra Moretti-themed flag on show in the away end here. But Spurs, for whom Mykhailo Mudryk arrived as a late substitute for his first competitive appearance for 645 days, still struggled in front of goal. Dominic Solanke, another late sub, headed on to the roof of Matz Sels’s net on 88 minutes and that was as good as things got for the visitors. Where was all the firepower? Last season’s top goalscorer, Richarlison, is training separately from De Zerbi’s first team after rejecting an offer from Everton and was not in Spurs’ 25-man squad.

There were glimpses of quality from the Spurs debutant Savio, a £75m arrival from Manchester City, but they were just that. Tonali, a £92.5m buy from Newcastle, impressed defensively more than anything else. Apart from Gibbs-White’s effort in the buildup to Williams’ disallowed goal, Forest’s sole shot on target was a 30-yard daisy-cutter from James McAtee. No wonder both teams remain winless. Spurs’s home game with Everton next weekend has just taken on another layer of significance and the same applies for Forest and their trip to Aston Villa.

The moment that will dominate the discourse will be Williams’ disallowed goal. Liam Delap, on his first Forest start, released Gibbs-White with a cute pass and while the Forest captain could not trap the ball, he got a shot away. Tonali recorded a swing and a miss as he attempted to clear on the goalline and Williams was hungrier than Van Hecke. But the video assistant referee, Peter Bankes, checked the goal and then the referee, Craig Pawson, took to the mic before awarding a Spurs free-kick amid a chorus of boos from the home support: “After review, the ball touches the hand of Nottingham Forest’s No 3 before the goal is scored.”

View image in fullscreen Spurs’ Mykhailo Mudryk came on as a late substitute for his first competitive appearance for 645 days. Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters

For so long, the teams’ stubborn three-man defences seemed to neutralise each other. It was hard to escape the sense there was always an extra defender on hand to extinguish even the tamest of attacks – and there were plenty of those. The Forest centre-back Murillo took matters into his own hands in the first half, his spectacular overhead-kick flying over the bar after a recycled corner.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Vinai Venkatesham, the Tottenham chief executive in attendance, could be forgiven for wondering when Spurs will see the fruits of their aggressive £300m-plus recruitment drive. Much of the focus had centred on strengthening the Spurs attack. They turned to Mudryk, who replaced Mathys Tel with 16 minutes of normal time remaining, after the failure to sell Richarlison halted moves for preferred targets Cody Gakpo and Iliman Ndiaye. This was not the desired result.

Sports.title: Chilwell seals Crystal Palace comeback win after Mitchell double at Fulham
Sports.content:
The managers may have changed but the result stays the same. For the fourth successive trip to this part of west London, Crystal Palace returned to south London with all three points in the bag as Pierre Sage got his reign off the mark in dramatic style. Their hero was Ben Chilwell, the former England left-back who was signed on deadline day from Strasbourg – this time permanently after he spent the second half of 2024-25 on loan and helped Palace win the FA Cup – and who came off the bench to volley home the winner.

It was a bitter blow for Fulham’s new manager Álvaro Arbeloa, who had seen his side lead twice through the impressive Josh King – showing his real potential in front of the watching England manager, Thomas Tuchel – and César Palacios before being pegged back twice by Tyrick Mitchell, the second in bizarre circumstances. They left the pitch to boos from some supporters and remain pointless in the league after three matches.

But having won here three times in 2025 under Oliver Glasner, this has been a happy hunting ground for Palace and Chilwell could not contain his delight as he celebrated with the travelling fans at the full-time whistle.

Like Palace, Fulham have made a habit of doing their business late in the window. But there was no place in the starting lineup for any of the three deadline day arrivals, with Hugo Larsson, David Affengruber and Manuel Ángel – the third player signed by Arbeloa from his former club, Real Madrid – all on the bench. It did not take long for Alex Iwobi – the 30-year-old who has now become only the fifth player in Premier League history to reach 100 or more appearances for three clubs – to start pulling the strings in midfield alongside the new £3om signing from Southampton, Shea Charles.

View image in fullscreen Tyrick Mitchell equalised twice for Palace. Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters

A sloppy early pass from Jaydee Canvot inside the first minute that almost gifted Palacios an opportunity betrayed the nerves of a Palace defence that had the Chelsea loanee, Axel Disasi, in the centre of the back three also favoured by Sage’s predecessor. When Timothy Castagne waltzed through and shot wide not long after it looked like being a long afternoon, and on 11 minutes Palace fell behind. Adam Wharton failed to clear a cross from Oscar Bobb and it fell straight into the path of King, whose shot took a big deflection to deceive Dean Henderson.

It was typical of Sage’s luck so far that a superb apparent equaliser less than two minutes later was chalked off. Daichi Kamada had strayed millimetres offside before volleying in a brilliant cross with the outside of his boot from Yéremy Pino. Palace were indebted to Disasi for blocking Bobb’s goalbound shot at the other end after Chris Richards had forced Bernd Leno into a full-length save. The visitors could have found themselves 2-0 down when Henderson saved a Castagne shot from close range, but Mitchell beat Leno at his near post to equalise against the run of play after being set up by Eddie Nketiah.

Palace’s joy was shortlived, however. Richards – being watched by his USA manager Mauricio Pochettino – was fooled by King’s clever dummy and the England Under-21 midfielder accepted the invitation to burst into the box. His cross would have been diverted into his own net by Canvot had it not been for an excellent save from Henderson, but Palacios put the ball into the empty net.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen César Palacios scored his first goal for Fulham to put them back in front before half-time. Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters

Of the two managers dressed all in black, it was no wonder that Sage looked much more concerned than his Spanish counterpart as they headed down the tunnel for the break. Things had not seemed to have improved much at the start of the second half when Palacios fired just wide following a corner and then Quinten Timber, starting as Wharton’s midfield partner on his Palace debut, had to block another shot from King after a flowing move.

But Palace’s luck suddenly changed for the better when they scored a comical second equaliser. Mitchell’s initial effort was cleared by García as the striker charged back into the area, but the Palace defender volleyed hopefully towards goal as he fell and García somehow managed to miss the ball altogether as it trickled over the line.

Fulham seemed to shrink after conceding and Palace sensed an opportunity. The comeback was complete when Chilwell volleyed in after Anan Khalaili’s effort had been blocked, and Fulham were forced to accept their fate once their own substitute left-back, Ryan Sessegnon, found the sidenetting in stoppage time.

Sports.title: European football: Nwaneri forces late own goal to cap dramatic Dortmund comeback
Sports.content:
Arsenal loanee Ethan Nwaneri caused a late own goal in Borussia Dortmund’s favour, as his side came from two down to win 3-2 at Hoffenheim in a topsy-turvy Bundesliga clash.

Hoffenheim were the better team for the opening hour but lost their way as Dortmund clicked into gear and romped to victory with three goals in the final 30 minutes.

Hoffenheim were two up with 54 minutes played thanks to goals from Leon Avdullahu and Tim Lemperle.

Nwaneri, who became the youngest player in Premier League history in 2024, arrived on a season-long loan from Arsenal on deadline day and came on with half an hour played after an injury for Filippo Mane.

Striker Serhou Guirassy gave the hosts hope when he scored just after the hour mark and then set up Fabio Silva five minutes later.

With just four minutes of regular time remaining, Nwaneri cut down the left and shot centrally, but his effort took a big deflection off home defender Albian Hajdari and into the goal.

Bundesliga newcomers Elversberg continued their excellent top-flight arrival with a 4-3 win at Borussia Mönchengladbach, making it two wins from two this season.

Gladbach took the lead twice and were 3-1 up midway through the second-half, but Elversberg fought back despite losing manager Vincent Wagner to a second yellow card just before the break.

With 10 minutes left, Felix Keidel levelled the scores at 3-3 and Maurice Krattenmacher put the visitors in front in stoppage time with his second goal of the match.

Bayer Leverkusen rebounded from their loss to Elversberg last Saturday by putting sorry Union Berlin to the sword in a 4-0 home victory.

Argentina internationals Equi Fernández and Facundo Medina had Leverkusen 2-0 up at half-time. England centre-back Jarell Quansah set up Patrik Schick for Leverkusen’s third before Ibrahim Maza added a stylish fourth late on.

West Ham loanee Niclas Füllkrug scored his second goal in three games since returning to Germany to help Werder Bremen win at home 3-1 against RB Leipzig. The Germany striker scored a long-range header, with Eren Dinkci and Marco Grüll also getting on the scoresheet.

Europa League finalists Freiburg continued their perfect start to the season with a solid 1-0 win away at promoted Paderborn.

Defending champions Bayern Munich face promoted Schalke later on Saturday.

View image in fullscreen Oihan Sancet roars with delight after scoring Bilbao’s third goal. Photograph: Vincent West/Reuters

In Spain, Athletic Bilbao thumped Atlético Madrid 3-0 on a miserable afternoon for Diego Simeone’s side. Nico Williams, Robert Navarro and Oihan Sancet’s goals gave the Basque hosts a resounding victory at San Mames.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Athletic secured back-to-back wins under former Borussia Dortmund coach Edin Terzic, after losing their first two matches of the campaign.

Striker Julián Álvarez, who tried to leave the club to join Barcelona this summer, returned as a substitute after illness but was ineffective in his second-half appearance.

On Sunday La Liga leaders Barcelona visit Valencia looking to move clear of Real Madrid, who lost 1-0 at Real Betis on Friday.

A late Ché Adams strike sealed a 2-1 comeback win for Torino over Fiorentina as the Florence club’s nightmare start to the Serie A season continued.

Mateo Pellegrino’s long-range strike put Fiorentina in front early in the second half, but a pile-driver from Rolando Mandragora – who had only joined Torino from La Viola four days earlier – drew the scores level.

Scotland international Adams sealed his side’s first points of the season in the 82nd minute, plucking a cross out of the air and flicking it in from close range to stun the Stadio Artemio Franchi crowd.

Fiorentina, the two-time Italian champions, have lost their first three games by an aggregate score of 9-1, and were booed off by their own fans following a performance that left them in last place.

Inter host Napoli in the early evening in a meeting between last season’s top two sides, before Gian Piero Gasperini faces his former club when Roma host Atalanta.

Sports.title: Luka Vuskovic rides to the rescue for Brighton as Leeds fail to take chances
Sports.content:
What might have been; what should have been. Leeds remain unbeaten three games into the season, but they will rue not departing the south coast with another win to add to their impressive start to the Premier League campaign.

They certainly had chances. By the time Brighton finally woke up with around half an hour remaining, Bart Verbruggen would have been wondering how on earth his goal had only once been breached, so great was Leeds’ dominance and so bullied had his side been. Yet, aside from Jayden Bogle’s early tap-in, the visitors just could not put the game to bed.

Their profligacy proved costly when Luka Vuskovic headed in with 19 minutes remaining to set up an unlikely thunderous conclusion from the hosts, which left Leeds clinging on to a point. Not since 2009, at the Withdean Stadium, have Leeds won a game at Brighton.

Having averaged more than 70% possession in their opening two league games, Brighton again had the lion’s share here, but rarely came close to doing anything with it. Perversely, in spite of the numbers, they also seemed incapable of retaining the ball in key positions for much of this match.

Had Dominic Calvert-Lewin – whose movement habitually caused issues – had his shooting radar properly calibrated, Leeds might have found themselves out of sight within the opening half hour. As it was, the visitors had only one goal to show for their far greater threat.

That came courtesy of Bogle, who was the beneficiary after Calvert-Lewin’s header was palmed out to Ao Tanaka, who squared across the face of goal for Leeds’ wing-back to complete the job by tapping in from a yard. Oddly, it was the first Leeds goal in nine away trips to Brighton, stretching all the way back to November 2012.

Calvert-Lewin had earlier been mightily relieved to see the offside flag belatedly raised after sticking an effort well wide when put clear through on goal, and the feeling that it was not his day only strengthened when he failed to convert a similar opportunity soon after Leeds had taken the lead. Unintentionally released by a stray Brighton pass, the England striker rounded Verbruggen and passed into an empty net only for Lewis Dunk to slide on the goalline and turn it wide. Tanaka promptly smashed against the crossbar from the resulting corner.

The home fans produced a smattering of boos at the half-time whistle, prompted more so at the ease with which their side was being frequently cut apart than their lack of cutting edge in an attack shorn of injured trio Georginio Rutter, Yankuba Minteh and Kaoru Mitoma.

Much has been said about Brighton’s decision not to recruit a senior striker to replace the departed Danny Welbeck but, for the concern about where their goals might come from, they came into this game as the Premier League’s top scorers with seven from their first two games.

There was little to quell the Amex’s disgruntlement immediately after the break when Anton Stach almost scored from close range and then delivered a wonderful cross that Tanaka turned past Verbruggen. Thankfully, for the hosts, the goal was ruled out with the Japanese midfielder straying a couple of inches offside.
