Only on the hour – with Leeds’ xG sitting at 2.5 and Brighton’s languishing just above 0.1 – did the hosts begin to play. Charalampos Kostoulas produced a wonderful jinking solo run, weaving his way past four men before sticking a weak effort into the hands of James Trafford, who had to hastily be at full stretch to turn a Malick Yalcouye curling shot round the upright. Vuskovic then nodded in Maxim De Cuyper’s corner at the far post for the equaliser.

View image in fullscreen Jayden Bogle scores with a tap-in to put Leeds 1-0 ahead in the first half. Photograph: Dylan Martinez/Reuters

Suddenly it was a different game. Yasin Ayari curled into Trafford’s hands, Promise David turned an effort over the bar, and Pascal Gross then smashed too high when gifted a prime opportunity from six yards out.

In all, Brighton managed an astonishing 17 shots in the second half. They probably should have scored another. What might have been; what should have been.

Sports.title: Enzo Le Fée penalty redemption rescues point for Sunderland at Brentford
Sports.content:
True redemption, perhaps, would have been to score with a Panenka, but Enzo Le Fée didn’t quite have the chutzpah for that. His duffed dink at Brentford in January was the low point of one of Sunderland’s two worst performances of the season, but he converted from the spot with eight minutes remaining to earn a draw in a battle of two physically aggressive and well-drilled teams who must both look at the chaos elsewhere and be thinking again of top-half finishes.

It had seemed that it would be a tale of Brentford’s newfound strength in depth and a second-half turnaround as they overcame a rocky first period to have the better of the second after a triple change at half-time, having already lost their captain Nathan Collins to a calf strain. But instead it was a Sunderland substitute who made the key contribution, Wilson Isidor being held by Keane Lewis-Potter at the back post to earn the penalty.

“The first half we didn’t hit the levels we have,” said the Brentford manager, Keith Andrews. “Second half I thought we did the basics very well, allowed us control and a little bit more territory. I think if we’d played the same XI second half there would have been a reaction, but we needed that chance for renewed energy and new personality. We need to constantly evolve and adapt according to what teams do against us. We feel confident we can fix different problems with the personnel we have.”

These are not normal times. Clubs up and down the Premier League are in flux, undercooked and struggling to deal with a flurry of late signings. In that context, it’s reasonable to wonder what the ceiling for Brentford might be. They narrowly missed out on Europe last season, but with this squad and rivals wobbling, a first qualification has to be the target this time round. Business done early and wisely, Brentford are the poster club for what now seems an old-fashioned model of team-building, one that doesn’t lead to flustered final day sprees or competing private jets on the runway at Lyon airport. They may rely on algorithms and the data-led unearthing of hidden gems, but there is at least a sense of a squad being built for footballing rather than financial reasons.

View image in fullscreen Vitaly Janelt controlled a bouncing ball well to give Brentford the lead. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters

The feeling with Sunderland is always that they’re rather more effective when there is no expectation that they will make the play. Countering dangerously, often through the erratic and unpredictable stylings of Nilson Angulo, they had the four best opportunities before the break: a Dan Ballard volley was ruled out because the debutant Kevin Danso was offside and in the goalkeeper’s eyeline, Le Fée smacked a shot against the post and, twice, goalbound efforts were blocked in the six-yard box, once by Jannik Schuster, who impressed after replacing Collins, and once inadvertently by Brian Brobbey, who got in the way of that rarest of things, an on-target effort from Noah Sadiki.

Sunderland’s manager, Régis Le Bris, said: “We were dominant but didn’t score, which is a shame when you come away somewhere like this. We still have this character. We are good when we are behind and we are still able to change the dynamic.”

Andrews called it a “proper game” and said tactical battles like that “make me feel alive”. And his half-time shake-up worked. Brentford looked far more comfortable after the break, and Igor Thiago had already headed a close-range chance straight at Robin Roefs when Vitaly Janelt put Brentford ahead after 57 minutes, meeting Nordi Mukiele’s diving headed clearance at the top of the bounce and steering a controlled slice into the top corner.

As Aaron Hickey, one of those three half-time changes, got much tighter to Angulo than Michael Kayode had, the Sunderland threat down the left diminished. Mamadou Sangaré, having dominated the 3-0 win over Spurs, found life rather harder against Granit Xhaka and Sadiki, but Brentford now have options on the bench. Yehor Yarmolyuk came on and imposed himself far more. Jaidon Antony, similarly, offered fresh impetus in replacing Dango Ouattara.

But while Sunderland’s lack of incision remains an area obviously in need of improvement, they had just about enough to haul themselves back into the game; those spurned first-half opportunities will not be rued too much.

Sports.title: Own goal and inspired debut from keeper Akane Okuma earn Villa point at Chelsea
Sports.content:
A Veerle Buurman own goal punished a profligate Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, securing a point for Aston Villa in a frustrating start to the hosts’ push to win back the WSL title.

How Villa came away with a point having conceded 65% possession and having amassed just seven shots to Chelsea’s 34 and five touches in the opposition box to the home team’s 57 is somewhat inexplicable.

Chelsea were creative and Lauren James was at her free-flowing best, but they could not convert their many chances, and the new Villa goalkeeper Akane Okuma’s monumental performance was a big part of that.

“If you analyse the performance today and the statistics of the game you can say that’s crazy we couldn’t win the game,” said the Chelsea manager, Sonia Bompastor. “You need to make sure you kill the game because when you are only one-nil up, you are always exposed. That’s what happened today and I think at the end of the game we are all frustrated because it’s not a good result.”

View image in fullscreen Almost every Villa outfield player joined the celebrations for their equaliser. Photograph: Katie Chan/Action Plus/Shutterstock

Chelsea’s summer has been one of change after a somewhat transitional season that broke a run of six consecutive WSL titles, and spirits have been high about their potential. However, they have a problem up front: with the new signing Melvine Malard, who came off the bench and scored two in their Champions League qualifier home leg against Real Sociedad, out with an injury, and Mayra Ramírez yet to make her return from a long lay-off, Aggie Beever-Jones failed to make the most of the opportunity to lead the line.

“In football, some of these things are also about mentality and mindset when it comes to being ruthless, being critical in the box,” said Bompastor. “The best teams don’t need to have many opportunities. So, that’s something we need to work on and find solutions for.”

Ushering in a new era in front of 7,900 fans at Stamford Bridge, where they will play all their WSL home games for the first time, Chelsea’s aggressive and relentless pressing in the opening half-hour caused all sorts of problems for Natalia Arroyo’s team, forcing error after error.

View image in fullscreen Lauren James gave an early sign of what she is capable of with a finish that left the Villa keeper helpless. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters

It was no surprise when that physical effort yielded results. In the 11th minute when pressure caused confusion between Okuma and the target of her pass out from the back, the loose ball was worked to James who glided into the box, shifting her weight as she went, before lashing the ball into the roof of the net. It was a statement goal from a statement player.

This was always going to be a tough opening game for Villa, who had lost all 12 of their previous WSL games against Chelsea and were starting five of their eight summer signings,. They only began to look a little more comfortable and structured as the home team’s pressure eased off towards the end of the first half.

“We just need to go through that and understand that when you’re in the middle of the jungle or whatever, at some point, you arrive at a point where there’s no more trees and I think that’s what we do at the end of the first half,” said Arroyo. “We get the energy back in the changing room and we talk about how to avoid these moments.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Chelsea’s profligacy in front of goal was the big frustration for Bompastor, and Villa were clinging on for large swathes of the game with Okuma, signed from the Japanese champions INAC Kobe Leonessa, key to keeping the margin to one goal.

View image in fullscreen Noelle Maritz’s (centre) shot led to Veerle Buurman’s own goal. Photograph: Katie Chan/Action Plus/Shutterstock

At no stage had it felt like the visiting team would be able to take something from the game. They were patient, but Chelsea were the masters of their own downfall, and in the 79th minute the ground was silenced when they failed to clear Lynn Wilms’ cross, Noelle Maritz swiped it goalwards from eight yards out, and Hannah Hampton’s block sent the ball bouncing off Buurman and over the line.

The home side pushed hard for the winner but Okuma was equal to every attempt. “We gave her some nice tests this week trying to know where she was at, if she was nervous, if she had any doubt and in which ways we could help her,” said Arroyo. “She’s still settling in here, she’s still trying to learn the language to be able to communicate with all the players, but we were surprised to see that she was safe in some of the actions, she read the game really well.”

On the final whistle the Japanese goalkeeper was enveloped in the hugs of her teammates as the players in blue digested how they had ended up with only a point from such a dominant performance.

Sports.title: Cardiff's former Arsenal star Krystian Bielik grabs young fan by the throat - before being slapped back - and gets away without any punishment in bizarre incident
Sports.content:
Cardiff's Krystian Bielik appeared to grab a supporter by the throat during a bizarre confrontation during their Championship match against Portsmouth.

The incident occurred in the 70th minute at Fratton Park, with Cardiff trailing 2-0 to the hosts.

Bielik, a former Arsenal youth product, had attempted to gather the ball from the stands.

Footage showed a young fan throwing the ball away from the Cardiff midfielder.

The act prompted a reaction from Bielik, who could be seen reaching out towards the fan's throat and pushing them away.

The fan responded by standing up and appearing to try to push Bielik in retaliation.

So Bielek grabs a kids throat, kid defends himself, and kid gets thrown out. Portsmouth FC should give off about this and Bielek needs suspending! pic.twitter.com/9Np1k8Xl3i — Charlie Barnes (@ChaltJames) September 5, 2026

Cardiff's Krystian Bielik appeared to grab the throat of a young Portsmouth fan after they threw the ball away from him

The fan responded by standing up and appearing to try to push Bielik in retaliation

The fan was ejected from the stadium following the incident, while Bielik avoided punishment

Another supporter could also be seen throwing the ball at Bielik in the aftermath but struck his Cardiff team-mate Perry Ng.

Following a delay, the supporter involved in the initial incident was ejected from the stadium for their part in the incident while Bielik avoided punishment.

Both Portsmouth manager John Mousinho and his Cardiff counterpart Brian Barry-Murphy were spoken to by the referee, as well as captains from both teams.

Portsmouth would ultimately go on to secure a 2-0 victory over their newly promoted opponents.

Bielik, 28, was making just his fourth appearance for Cardiff after joining the Bluebirds last month.

Sports.title: Man City 1-0 Coventry: New £125m man Enzo Fernandez takes first step towards paying off his price tag, Rayan Cherki strengthens his claim to be Enzo Maresca's key creative spark - and the flaws the narrow win exposed
Sports.content:
Man City 1-0 Coventry: New £125m man Enzo Fernandez takes first step towards paying off his price tag, Rayan Cherki strengthens his claim to be Enzo Maresca's key creative spark - and the flaws the narrow win exposed

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A late call, a great ball, and one small step towards paying off the most baffling transfer fee of the window. Those hoping for Enzo Fernandez to fall flat at Manchester City will have to wait a while longer to land their punches.

We can state at the outset that the Argentine did not settle this game – that was achieved by the more conventional route of Erling Haaland.

Nor was Fernandez the best player, because Rayan Cherki seems to hold a standing reservation on that status.

But in a game that lacked any sustained periods of class from City, Fernandez, the £125million riddle, bedded himself in with a solid contribution and one sublime delivery.

Relevantly, it was the ball that orchestrated the winning moment after 26 minutes, when he spotted the run of Antoine Semenyo, processed the space behind Jay Dasilva, and through a split-second judgement was able to shape the two factors into a high-quality, game-changing pass.

From there, Semenyo nailed the cross and Haaland did what Haaland does, but the art had been supplied by a man who most neutrals might prefer to despise. Presumably, he won’t wait too long to offer a reminder of the infuriating aspects he showed at Chelsea, and at the World Cup, but this was a strong start.

Erling Haaland celebrates scoring the only goal of the game for Man City against Coventry

Enzo Fernandez was listed among Enzo Maresca’s substitutes, only to be promoted to the XI when Nico O’Reilly tweaked his back

And a strange one, too, given Fernandez was listed among Enzo Maresca’s substitutes, only to be promoted to the XI when Nico O’Reilly tweaked his back in the warm-up.

In truth, that setback wasn’t the only hurdle Maresca faced. Sure, this was City’s third win in three, but it was also messy, wasteful, and far closer than anyone expected. Coventry had good chances in both halves.

Credit there to Frank Lampard – each of his substitutions after the break enhanced Coventry’s side, which might have been worth something had Gianluigi Donnarumma not made a string of saves, but it is hard to escape their record. At three defeats from three, they are the mirror to City in every way.

Maresca, therefore, won’t read volumes into this beyond the result, and the broader excitement elicited whenever Cherki takes possession. He neither scored nor assisted here, but with two of each preceding another menacing contribution, his confidence is glowing in fluorescent shades, especially when he is permitted to play that advanced role behind Haaland.

To that end, Fernandez’s arrival ought to help. The risk is that they might clog each other’s space around the box, but the early signs in this fixtures was of a fast-settling relationship. They worked well together.

Other praise might be hard to find for Maresca. Indeed, the O’Reilly scenario was a prelude to 10 minutes of sheer calamity at the start of the game.

That messy little stretch commenced when Donnarumma was forced to hack a clearance off the line after allowing an Abdukodir Khusanov backpass to squirm under his boot. Tone set, Semenyo then day-dreamed into a square ball across goal that was cut out by Taiwo Awoniyi and offered a one-on-one.

Fortuitously for Semenyo, Awoniyi dragged his finish wide, but City were nervy, uneasy, unsure, which carried into the final act of the sequence, when Marc Guehi attempted a basic header back to Donnarumma and bobbled it straight out for a corner. Ugly stuff.

But it’s City. And it’s Coventry. All of which meant it stabilised. The corrections started with Haaland, who had a snapshot saved by Carl Rushworth, and then Cherki, who bluffed Bobby Thomas into a lunge and then fired against the post.

Cherki’s confidence in those tight spaces has been a theme of these opening games, but it is worth noting that it was Fernandez who gave him the opportunity. The Argentine’s next spell was to set Semenyo loose to assist Haaland’s header for 1-0.

This being Fernandez, we should also state there had already been one entirely unnecessary shoulder barge on Rushworth inside the first two minutes and he was later bullied to the ground by Ephron Mason-Clark after over-elaborating in midfield - as ever, he brings the good and bad.

MATCH FACTS Manchester City (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 7; Khusanov 6.5, Dias 7, Guehi 6, Gvardiol 6.5; Fernandez 7.5 (Bouaddi 76), Anderson 7; Ndiaye 5.5 (McAidoo 86), Semenyo 7, Cherki 8 (Foden 66, 6); Haaland 7. Subs not used: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Nunes, Lewis, Samba Booked: Khusanov Enzo Maresca 7 Coventry (3-4-2-1: Rushworth 7.5; Thomas 7.5, Amenda 6, Pinnock 6.5; Van Ewijk 7, Grimes 6.5, Onyeka 6.5 (Yirenkyi 63, 6.5), Dasilva 6 (Hamer 85); Rudoni 6 (Tachaouna 63, 6.5), Mason-Clark 6.5 (Thomas-Asante 71, 6); Awoniyi 6 (Simms 71, 7). Subs not used: Bentley, Sakamoto, Latibeaudiere, Torp Booked: Van Ewijk, Pinnock Frank Lampard 7 Ref: Paul Tierney 7

But that applied to City as a whole - their fluctuations across the first half were wild and only marginally less of a concern in the second.

That period started well for Maresca, albeit with a Haaland goal correctly disallowed for offside by Fernandez. The shame in that instance was the nullification of Ferandez’s assist, crafted by a hooked volley across goal, because the technique was sublime.

From there, City invited trouble. The short passes, the urges to go sideways and backwards, are staples of Maresca’s football but also allowed Coventry time to set a shape. Urgency might have killed their threat and yet there was precious little - Iliman Ndiaye had a particularly quiet debut in place of Phil Foden.

Against that inertia, Coventry had scope to push back. When Loum Tchaouna broke clear, they had such a chance, but Donnarumma made the save, and the goalkeeper did so again when Ellis Simms pounced on City’s failure to handle a cross. High balls regularly unsettled Maresca’s defence, but Coventry have not yet scored in the league, so no punishment was forthcoming.

Sports.title: Leeds United blow golden chance after dominating in 1-1 draw at Brighton as Daniel Farke's men miss openings and Luka Vuskovic levels for Albion
Sports.content:
Leeds United blow golden chance after dominating in 1-1 draw at Brighton as Daniel Farke's men miss openings and Luka Vuskovic levels for Albion

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Leeds United stay unbeaten this season but will be kicking themselves for not recording a first-ever win at the Amex after dominating the first hour of this game. Jayden Bogle became the first Leeds player to score at the Amex since 2012 after 14 minutes but Daniel Farke’s side missed a host of chances to add to their lead.

And after Brighton’s record signing, Luka Vuskovic, levelled after 71 minutes with his first goal for the club, the game swung entirely in the home side’s favour.

Where are Brighton’s goals coming from without Danny Welbeck?

Welbeck was last season’s top scorer with 13 goals and there were pre-season concerns that Brighton would struggle up top without him. Seven in opponents’ nets in the first two Premier League games, against Villa and Chelsea, appeared to allay those fears – but two of them were scored by opponents.

Canada striker Promise David, signed on loan from Union St Gilloise, is the nearest thing to a Welbeck replacement, but so far head coach Fabian Hurzeler has trusted either ex-Leeds man Georginio Rutter – injured today – or Greek teenager Babis Kostoulas, neither of whom is an out-and-out number nine.

Kostoulas produced one memorable dribble through the packed Leeds defence, only to spoil it with a weak finish, while David looked clumsy in a brief cameo.

Horses for courses?

Leeds had not won a Premier League game at the Amex in four previous attempts, nor scored on Brighton turf since November 2012. They had played more matches there without winning than at any other stadium in their history (P10 D 3 L 7). 34 different Leeds players had had shots at goal in eight visits since the 2013-14 season without scoring.

Bogle broke that duck after 14 minutes from just a few inches out and plenty about the rest of their performance suggested that this Leeds side has more about them than some previous versions.

Jayden Bogle became the first Leeds United player to score at the Amex since 2012

Brighton’s record signing, Luka Vuskovic, levelled after 71 minutes with his first goal

James Trafford for England?

Leeds’ £40m outlay on Trafford makes the England hopeful the fourth-most expensive goalkeeper in history. The Leeds fans’ chant of “England’s number one” presumably matches his own ambitions.

An early punch when a catch looked on was unconvincing, but his parry of Diego Gomez’ powerful volley was safe enough and his distribution was eye-catching at times, one long pass sending Dominic Calvert-Lewin racing into space down the left.

But he is not the finished article; he was left looking for defenders to blame when Brighton’s Luka Vuskovic headed in a corner from a yard out.

Malick magic

The Ivorian made a sensational full Premier League debut for Brighton at Chelsea last weekend after loan spells at Sturm Graz and Swansea City, scoring with a sensational volley.

The 20-year-old midfielder has been compared to N’golo Kante and was voted man of the match against Leeds but was a surprise omission from Brighton’s 25-man UEFA Conference League squad on Friday. Boss Fabian Hurzeler has hinted that there might be ways that the neat and dynamic Yalcouye could still be squeezed in and on the evidence so far he must be hoping so.

Sports.title: Pierre Sage's supersubs prove the difference as unlikely heroes Tyrick Mitchell and Ben Chilwell pile pressure on Alvaro Arbeloa: Fulham 2-3 Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
Pierre Sage's supersubs prove the difference as unlikely heroes Tyrick Mitchell and Ben Chilwell pile pressure on Alvaro Arbeloa: Fulham 2-3 Crystal Palace

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Pierre Sage and Alvaro Arbeloa began their Saturday in much the same place.

Winless, pointless, and just beginning to wonder if they had made a mistake in taking a long-term lease on a London flat.

'El Sackico' in the first weekend of September? Not quite. Not yet.

But Sage and Arbeloa will both have been desperate for a win to give them lift-off, after inauspicious starts to daunting tasks in following Oliver Glasner and Marco Silva at Crystal Palace and Fulham respectively.

In the end it was Sage who got his wish. And through the unlikeliest of sources.

Fulham had taken the lead twice – through Josh King and Cesar Palacios – but both times saw it cancelled out by Tyrick Mitchell. The full back had managed just four goals from his first 209 Premier League games, then came up with two in 54 minutes.

The second was a shambles of a goal to concede from Fulham's perspective, a Gonzalo Garcia clearance going only as far as Mitchell's boot, then the Spaniard failing to deal with the danger again as the ball travelled sedately towards goal.

With both teams chasing a win, Ben Chilwell delivered it. The former Chelsea and England man had only been on the pitch for a few minutes when the ball rebounded to him in the box and he volleyed accurately into the far corner.

Some way to reintroduce yourself to the Palace faithful, days after the former loanee rejoined the club from Strasbourg.

This was an entertaining game, end-to-end from start to finish and with both goalkeepers called into action relentlessly. It could have gone either side's way.

Unfortunately, that will do little to help Arbeloa's prospects. 'I'm very confident (in my position),' he insisted at full time, after boos rang out around Craven Cottage. 'We lost a game we didn't deserve to lose.

'We knew this month was going to be very tough but I told my players, this month will not define our season. The players are giving everything and with this mentality and character I’m sure the victories will come.'

Don't get too settled in London just yet...

Ben Chilwell was the unlikely hero for Crystal Palace at Craven Cottage, scoring the winner just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute

This was a big game for both Alvaro Arbeloa (left) and Pierre Sage - but the Palace boss won out

Proactive Sage changes the game

Sage's side were far from abject in the first half here. Bernd Leno had a busy day in the Fulham goal, and Palace were good value for Mitchell's first equaliser - a driving run into space down the left flank, and a powerful finish at Leno's near post.

But their lack of a proper front man was obvious.

Teams like Palace, especially away from home, need a No 9 they can play up to – one that can win duels, hassle defenders, and link up play. Eddie Nketiah is not that man.

That is not to say he is without any good qualities. But when Nketiah found himself competing with Fulham centre back Calvin Bassey, that competition was embarrassingly one-sided.

No wonder Sage hooked Nketiah for the bulkier Jorgen Strand Larsen at half-time. The Norwegian was much more effective than the man he replaced.

Though Palace didn't create bundles more chances in the second half, they carried far more of a threat when they went on their forays forward.

It was one of two key substitutions from Sage, to go with match-winner Chilwell. He deserves credit for making those changes, especially the proactive introduction of Strand Larsen.

'The mindset of the team in the first half was very low,' said Sage later. 'We changed it in the second. It was a good thing because we need confidence and points to work more with less pressure.

'I was honest with the players at half-time and spoke with the players who made a mistake. I said we needed bravery.

'It's important we have "petrol", and our petrol is a victory.'

With Jean-Philippe Mateta expected to be out for another three weeks, it's safe to assume Strand Larsen will get the nod going forward.

King beats out Wharton in Tuchel audition

Thomas Tuchel was among the onlookers here at Craven Cottage. One assumed it was to cast an eye on Adam Wharton.

Wharton is a Rolls-Royce of a player. He runs Palace's midfield. But this was not his best game.

It was his failure to deal with a cross that led to Fulham's opener. Wharton appeared a little off it physically at times, beaten in footraces on several occasions.

'He didn’t touch the ball in the first half, because we were really bad offensively,' admitted Wharton's boss Sage. 'These players can have the worst half of their life in the first half and the best in the second half because they’ve got so much talent.'

But if Tuchel may have been underwhelmed with what he saw of Wharton, he will have been thrilled with King's display.

Josh King celebrates putting Fulham in front on an impressive afternoon for the 19-year-old

Thomas Tuchel was among the guests at Craven Cottage and will have been delighted with what he saw from King

The 19-year-old opened the scoring – albeit with the help of a big deflection – after showing some tidy footwork on the edge of the box.

He was at the heart of Fulham's second too, selling Chris Richards a dummy before spinning past him, leaving him in his wake before playing the ball which led to Palacios' goal.

'He’s a massive player for us, a very good player,' said Arbeloa. 'He has everything – talent, ambition… he’s so important for us. I’m so happy for him.'

The teenager has long been regarded as an extraordinary talent at Fulham, but his game appears to have gone up a notch this season.

King was said to have impressed England coaching staff when away at the Three Lions' pre-World Cup camp in the US. He certainly will have impressed Tuchel today.

Sports.title: Ragged in attack, messy in defence - chaotic Newcastle were bettered by Bournemouth for most of their 2-2 draw... but Eden Hazard-like £51m Matias Fernandez-Pardo brings excitement, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
There remains a little more chaos than cohesion with Newcastle 2.0, but character has survived the reboot.

Without that, they would have lost for the first time this season. On the balance of technical execution, they could have had few complaints.

For new boss Matthias Jaissle, this is a work in progress with a young team. Whilst that work is ongoing, it helps that a summer of change has brought with it renewed optimism on Tyneside.

That is why the mood inside St James’ Park did not sour, despite Bournemouth being the better team. And that is why, from 2-0 down, Newcastle were able to salvage a point.

That they scored with their only two shots on target tells the story of a disjointed attacking display - too many final balls were sloppy, as Jaissle admitted - and they were just as ragged in defence. They lost the midfield battle to the outstanding Alex Scott, too.

Across four matches, they have now faced 74 shots. There is a fragility in the middle of the park that needs to stiffen if those numbers are to improve. Scott out-fought and out-thought adversaries Nico Gonzalez and Lewis Miley.

Jacob Ramsey celebrates scoring Newcastle United's late equaliser against Bournemouth

£51m signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo has draw comparisons with Eden Hazard

Bournemouth led through Marcus Tavernier, followed by an unfortunate Newcastle own goal

Yet, for all of that, Jaissle and his team were applauded from the pitch post match, and rightly so. Newcastle would have - and did - lose this game in seasons past. They did not this time because of their spirt and Jaissle’s changes.

With two minutes remaining, substitute Jacob Ramsey smashed the equalising goal at the Gallowgate End. Newcastle might even have won it when, moments later, Yoane Wissa was inches away from collecting a Sean Steur pass and running clear. St James’ was bouncing by then.

Ramsey’s goal was the fourth from a substitute under Jaissle, who had recognised his team’s drift and addressed it. In every game, his changes have had the desired impact, and how they needed it here.

‘To come back was special and I think there is something we can build on,’ said Jaissle. ‘The desire to win the game was there until the end.

‘But the frustration is also there. In the first half, aspects were missing to be competitive. We could not match Bournemouth. In the Premier League, you need to be at your best over 90 minutes to get three points. But, if there were 10 minutes more at the end, I thought we could have gone for the winner.’

Harvey Barnes curls in his brilliant response to Newcastle going 2-0 down at home

MATCH FACTS NEWCASTLE (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 5; Dedic 5, Thiaw 5, Botman 5, Hall 5 (Livramento 90); Gonzalez 5 (Steur 77, 6), Miley 5 (Ramsey 63, 7); Elanga 4 (Murphy 78, 5), Willock 5 (Fernandez-Pardo 63, 7), Barnes 7; Wissa 6 Subs: Pope, Schar, Bamba, Toure Manager: Matthias Jaissle 6 BOURNEMOUTH (4-2-3-1): Petrovic 6; Smith 6, Hill 6, Antonio Silva 6, Truffert 7; Adams 6 (Cook 76, 5), Scott 9 (Christie 90); Rayan 6 (Doak 89), Kluivert 7 (Brooks 76), Tavernier 7 (Jebbison 89); Evanilson 6 Subs: Soler, Diakite, Di Gregorio, Sanchez Manager: Marco Rose 6 Ref: Rob Jones 5

It was the arrival of £51million debutant Matias Fernandez-Pardo that helped rescue a point as much as Ramsey’s right boot. The Belgian injected an energy and purpose lacking to the point of his 63rd-minute introduction. The comparisons to Eden Hazard are obvious, and you get the feeling the Toon Army are going to enjoy the young forward.

For too much of this match, though, there wasn’t a lot to like about Newcastle. Bournemouth came with the same game-plan from last season, and the one before that. The winning formula is not overly complicated, either - keep the ball, quieten the crowd and pin Newcastle in their own half. With that, use pacey forwards like Marcus Tavernier, Rayan and Justin Kluivert to hurt a backline that had retreated to the point of vulnerability. The hosts knew what was coming but could do little about it. The free beer given to supporters beforehand suddenly felt as flat at the lunchtime atmosphere.

By the 35th minute, Bournemouth were two goals in front and it was entirely deserved, even if a deflection presented Tavernier with the chance for his opener and the second was an own goal via a looping ricochet off Malick Thiaw.

They were still showing replays of that bizarre concession on the monitors in the ground when Harvey Barnes raced up the other end from the restart and curled in a trademark reply from 18 yards.

‘A world class goal,’ said Jaissle. ‘I could not have wished for that goal more in that moment.’

If the reprieve was supposed to signal a home improvement, it did not. Bournemouth were the more organised and looked to have kept Newcastle at bay until the ball bounced around the penalty area and Ramsey took it off the toe of Fernandez-Pardo to score. The two subs queuing up to convert spoke of their eagerness to impress.

It was the third game on the spin that Marco Rose’s side had conceded late goals to forgo Premier League victories, but they still look like a very competent team.

As for Newcastle, it is hard to know what their season will look like. Good, bad or indifferent, it sure promises to be fun.

Sports.title: Max Verstappen lashes out at Lewis Hamilton over near-miss at the Italian Grand Prix - before Pierre Gasly shocks everyone to take pole position!
Sports.content:
Pierre Gasly sprung one of the shocks of the season by taking pole position for Sunday's Italian Grand Prix, 24 hours after learning he had been stripped of his podium finish in Monaco.

That controversy, so long after the event in June, a verdict delivered by the FIA's International Court of Appeal, has convulsed the paddock this weekend.

Gasly, a Frenchman who drives for Alpine and lives in Milan, 30 minutes down the road from the Monza circuit, just pipped George Russell to pole by 0.060sec.

Oscar Piastri was third for McLaren, Charles Leclerc fourth and Lewis Hamilton fifth – a poor day for the two Ferrari men.

Hamilton also endured an awkward moment with old rival Max Verstappen. Verstappen and Hamilton were almost wheel-to-wheel as the Brit tried to get ahead of the Dutchman, who blamed him for the closeness.

'He caused that,' Verstappen shouted. Hamilton said: 'I got blocked by Max, so...' Carlo Santi, Hamilton's Ferrari race engineer, added: 'Yes, we saw.'

Max Verstappen gestures towards Lewis Hamilton after they came close at the Italian GP

Max and Lewis going wheel to wheel down the main straight 😮#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/xrTXkrvVqg — Formula 1 (@F1) September 5, 2026

Gasly's sole victory came here six years ago, driving for AlphaTauri, and this was his first pole.

As for Hamilton, the 41-year-old had turned up at the Temple of Speed on Thursday in his £6million Ferrari F40 road car, wearing a suit and a coat and a beret, and told the world that he wished to become the first black winner of this fabled race.

Yet his Ferrari, the one he needs to propel him to victory, appears not to be up to the standard.

If there is not an improvement in the Ferraris during the race, it will be inquest time at Maranello (again).

Hamilton only squeezed into Q3 by the skin of his teeth – the smallest margin possible, one-thousandth of a second ahead of Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto.

'We are through, that is very tight,' he was told by his race engineer Carlo Santi.

Pierre Gasly was delighted as he caused a major shock by taking pole position

Hamilton only squeezed into Q3 with his Ferrari not appearing up to standard

'Ah, f*** me,' responded Hamilton.

Prior to the Gasly incursion, Russell had been superb throughout qualifying as he was in practice. This looks like the moment he must make a serious dent in the championship lead held by his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli, the 20-year-old Italian who will start at the back of the grid despite taking on a new engine, having qualified seventh.

Russell is 59 points back from Antonelli with 11 races of the campaign remaining.

Aston Martin continued to trail the field, with Lance Stroll at the very back, his team-mate Fernando Alonso only a place above him.

So much for their upgrades. Some steps forward but a steep incline.

Gasly, 30, said: 'We had the car to challenge for pole. We were surprised to see us up there. I didn't want to get too excited but I was third after the first run in Q3 and I knew I had a shot at it, and I had a true chance.

'I left it all out there. Crossing the line, I knew it would be a lap that would be rewarded – but a chance to get to pole position, I didn't expect that. It is definitely one of those laps that I will put up there. It has been emotional with everything going on this weekend, and I have been trying to stick to my job and that is what we did.

'I am really proud and happy to have seized this chance. It was a heck of a lap. Nine years waiting for that feeling. I got my first win here in Monza and now my first pole, too. It is a special place for me, a unique track.'

Sports.title: Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo in line to play TOGETHER for the first time ever as their former team-mate plots star-studded farewell match
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo in line to play TOGETHER for the first time ever as their former team-mate plots star-studded farewell match

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo will line up for the same team for the first time ever later this year... if Carlos Tevez gets his way.

The world superstars have gone head to head over the years with their biggest tussles coming while they were at the top of the game with Barcelona and Real Madrid.

Messi and Ronaldo were pitted as rivals as they vied for the Ballon d'Or with either player winning the honour an incredible 10 years in a row between 2008 and 2017.

With Messi now plying his trade in the United States with Inter Miami and Cristiano Ronaldo happy in Saudi Arabia with Al Nassr, it doesn't look like they will be club team-mates before they retire in the not so distant future.

However fans of both players might finally see the duo share a dressing room as Tevez, who is a former team-mate of both players, plans to invite them to his testimonial match in December.

'Leo Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo will be there,' promised Tevez.

'I'll go pick them myself if I have to. I have both of them on WhatsApp.'

Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi could finally line up as team-mates in December

Carlos Tevez is planning to invite Wayne Rooney and Ronaldo to his testimonial match

Tevez lined up alongside Messi when representing Argentina's national team

Tevez hung up his boots back in 2021 but is yet to host a celebratory match to honour his career despite achieving great success with the likes of Manchester United, Manchester City, Juventus and Boca Juniors.

Juan Roman Riquelme has granted Tevez his wish of hosting his testimonial match at Boca Juniors' legendary La Bombonera Stadium, according to A Bola.

And both Messi and Ronaldo are set to top the guestlist of stars taking part, along with Wayne Rooney, Rio Ferdinand, Andrea Pirlo and Gianluigi Buffon.

Messi, who retired from international duty with Argentina on Monday, represented his country alongside Tevez between 2005 and 2015.

Ronaldo and Tevez formed a deadly three-pronged attack alongside Rooney during the Argentine's two-year spell at Old Trafford between 2007 and 2009.

They won back-to-back Premier League titles as well as the Champions League, League Cup and Club World Cup.

Tevez didn't win a major honour with Argentina's national team but did finish as a Copa America runner-up in 2004, 2007 and 2015. He also won a gold medal with Argentina's Olympic team in 2004.

Sports.title: Humiliating moment college football star is caught with his pants down on live TV after opponent's bruising tackle
Sports.content:
A college football player suffered the ultimate live TV nightmare on Friday after having his pants pulled down during a tackle – leaving his backside exposed to viewers.

Michigan State running back Cam Edwards endured the unfortunate disaster during the first quarter of the Spartans' season opener against Toledo in East Lansing.

Taking a handoff on a run up the middle, Edwards was swallowed up by a swarm of Toledo defenders near the line of scrimmage.

However, as Toledo's Lucas Lambert-Pipkin dragged him to the turf, the defender's hand got caught on Edwards' pants, pulling them down beyond his backside.

As Edwards lay on the turf, the FS1 broadcast camera zoomed right in on the downed running back as he struggled to pull his pants back up.

To make matters worse, Edwards' compression shorts had also ridden down, briefly exposing his bare backside to the viewers at home.

Michigan State running back Cam Edwards suffered the ultimate live TV nightmare after having his pants pulled down and his backside exposed following a tackle on Friday evening

Toledo's Lucas Lambert-Pipkin dragged him to the turf, pulling his pants down in the process

He did whatever it took to make the tackle happen… pants included 🤣 pic.twitter.com/V2yp0F2Epi — FOX College Football (@CFBONFOX) September 5, 2026

The camera lingered for several excruciating seconds while Edwards scrambled on the turf to fix his uniform, sparking disbelief and jokes across social media.

One fan on X wrote: 'No model has a variable for losing your pants during a tackle. Week 1 remains undefeated.'

Meanwhile, another said: 'Michigan State RB Cam Edwards just got pantsed in front of 75,000+ people. This is why we love college football!'

Despite the mortifying on-field moment, Edwards brushed off the mishap to lead the Spartans' ground attack in his Michigan State debut.

The UConn transfer carried the ball 27 times for 98 yards and scored a touchdown, helping propel Michigan State to a 30-20 victory in front of the home crowd.

Edwards arrived in East Lansing during the offseason after a four-year stint at UConn, where he established himself as the Huskies' primary offensive weapon.

Sports.title: Judd Trump makes telling Ronnie O'Sullivan comment as he thumps Zhao Xintong
Sports.content:
Judd Trump makes telling Ronnie O'Sullivan comment as he thumps Zhao Xintong

Judd Trump has had many battles with Zhao Xintong and Ronnie O'Sullivan and he believes there are similarities between the two snooker aces

View 3 Images Judd Trump has compared Ronnie O'Sullivan and Zhao Xintong (Image: Tai Chengzhe/VCG via Getty Images)

Zhao Xintong is the closest thing snooker has to Ronnie O'Sullivan, according to Judd Trump. Trump overcame the World No. 1 5-1 in the British Open to book a semi-final meeting with Jak Jones.

‌



It was a sweet victory for Ace In The Pack, as Zhao has overtaken him to become the World No. 1 just the week before. Nevertheless, he got the better of the Chinese sensation in ruthless fashion.

‌



Despite the convincing victory, Trump admits there is little comparison between Zhao and the rest of the snooker world - except from O'Sullivan.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Channel 5 British Open snooker viewers issue same complaints just minutes in READ MORE :

When quizzed about Zhao's capabilities, Trump said: "Tough question. It's hard to say as it's still early days. I think it's just the manner of how he makes it look.

"I don't think he's necessarily got a better standard, but I think the way he makes it look, it's maybe only Ronnie in the past has made it look that easy. So I think sometimes when you're sat down, you can be a little bit mesmerised by how easy he makes it look.

‌



"And that's more of a challenge to someone that makes it look a bit harder. He's a great player and he's got great potential still. He's already a great player, but he's someone that I enjoy playing against and it's a good challenge."

View 3 Images Trump convincingly beat Zhao (Image: Tai Chengzhe, VCG via Getty Images)

Beyond discussing his technical ability, Trump also reckons the style Zhao brings to the table is reminiscent of O'Sullivan. He added: "It's just a very relaxed walk, isn't it?

‌



"Very slow, he just looks very relaxed down on this shot and everything looks very at comfort out there. He looks very comfortable on the main stage and it's something that you can't really teach."

However, Zhao was far from satisfied with his own performance against Trump. The world No. 1 admitted: "Sometimes I play some stupid shots.

View 3 Images O'Sullivan is, and may always be, the bar-setter (Image: Tai Chengzhe, VCG via Getty Images)

‌



"In an important game that I know John Higgins, Mark Selby or Judd Trump will never do those mistakes. I know for myself, the mental game, this part I can do better.

"I will still go for my style. I just try to study from Judd Trump. He and Mark Selby were world number one for a very long time.

"I don't just want a few days or a few weeks to be world number one, I want a lot longer, so I have a long way to go and I just try to study them, but also I will keep my style."

Sports.title: Richard Hughes' 18 Liverpool transfer ranked with best and worst deals decided
Sports.content:
Richard Hughes has left Liverpool after two years at the helm of the club as sporting director. The 47-year-old has decided to leave the club a year early, leaving behind a mixed legacy at Anfield.

Hughes arrived from Bournemouth in the summer of 2024 and was responsible for the decision to appoint Arne Slot as Jurgen Klopp's successor. He therefore took plenty of the plaudits when Slot delivered the Premier League title in his first campaign. But he has also been on the receiving end of his fair share of criticism, given what followed in a disappointing second season.

Liverpool splashed out over £400million on signings last summer, bringing in Alexander Isak (£125m), Florian Wirtz (£116m) and Hugo Ekitike (£79m) as the headline additions which were supposed to help solidify the Reds as the best team in the league. Those deals didn't immediately pay off, with Liverpool finishing fifth in the Premier League.

That cost Slot his job and prompted the hiring of Andoni Iraola for a summer rebuild. Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate all left on free transfers, leaving Hughes and his colleagues with a major task on their hands.

‌

After a frustrating window, Liverpool signed Bradley Barcola (£123m) from Paris Saint-Germain, following the arrivals of Jeremy Jacquet, Ronald Araujo and Victor Munoz. But the failure to add a specialist right winger, as well as a holding midfielder and a right-back, has drawn criticism.

In total, Hughes has overseen the signings of 18 players for Liverpool, ranging from Federico Chiesa and Giorgi Mamardashvili two years ago, to Barcola days before his departure to Al-Hilal became official.

‌



Hughes was likely delighted to see Isak - his most expensive signing - score twice against Ipswich on Friday night, providing a glimpse of his potential following a difficult debut campaign. Isak's move from Newcastle was expensive and controversial and was followed by a serious injury which derailed the majority of his 2025/26 season.

Sports.title: Man Utd still in talks to complete transfer deal after failed deadline day move
Sports.content:
Man Utd still in talks to complete transfer deal after failed deadline day move

Manchester United failed to make a single signing on transfer deadline day, with one particular deal collapsing late on, and talks to agree terms are continuing

View 2 Images Manchester United are still in talks over signing another player for Michael Carrick (Image: Getty Images)

Leicester City and Manchester United are still in talks over Louis Page despite being unable to agree on the terms of a deal during transfer deadline day.

‌



Hopes of him moving to the Premier League effectively ended when Russell Martin included his midfielder in their starting XI for a League One match on the same night against Plymouth Argyle. Page, 18, had previously missed their opening match of the season. He will now be staying until at least January.

‌



United, however, are said to remain confident of signing the England under-19 international. Page made 18 Championship appearances last season.

‌



Our sister title the Manchester Evening News reports that lines of communication remain open between the two clubs. They understand that their issue earlier in the week concerned payment terms for the initial fee that Leicester City would receive, as well as the makeup of the add-ons.

Eight players could miss Everton vs Man Utd Premier League clash including £70m signing READ MORE :

It is understood that the League One club wanted a fee in excess of the £10million plus £2.5million in add-ons deal that Manchester City agreed for Jeremy Monga. A deal which would have seen Page stay at Leicester for the remainder of this season was understood to be close before the 11pm deadline.

‌



Arsenal have been credited with an interest in the midfielder. However, he is said to be sold on the pathway and vision that United presented.

Page's father, Don, was born in Manchester, and they still apparently have family in the area. Like his son, Page Sr was a footballer, playing for several teams in Greater Manchester, including Altrincham, Hyde United, Rochdale and Wigan Athletic.

View 2 Images Manchester United made a deadline day attempt to sign Leicester City midfielder Louis Page. (Image: Plumb Images, Leicester City FC via Getty Images)

‌

Martin acknowledged after Tuesday's match that Leicester rejected a bid from United on deadline day. He said: "The owner (Aiyawatt 'Top' Srivaddhanaprabha) was here today [and] we sat in the office and received a very big offer from Manchester United.

"Myself, Jon [Rudkin] (chief football officer), James [McCarron] (sporting director) and the owner, Khun Top, sat in [the office] and he said no.

‌



"So whatever's going on with the noise around the club and all that stuff, he was strong, and he wanted the player to stay and be part of us. It would have been so easy for him to sell Louis and take a lot of money, but he didn't.

"It's a brilliant thing for us. Louis, you can see the level of quality and potential he possesses is amazing. He's really helped us since coming into the team. I'm really grateful that he's still here."

Sports.title: Liverpool confirm departure of Richard Hughes days after difficult transfer window ends
Sports.content:
Liverpool confirm departure of Richard Hughes days after difficult transfer window ends

Richard Hughes has decided to leave Liverpool after just two years at the club and will join Saudi Arabian club Al-Hilal following a turbulent summer on Merseyside

View 2 Images Richard Hughes has left Liverpool (Image: Robin Jones/Getty Images)

Liverpool have confirmed the departure of sporting director Richard Hughes. The club chief was contracted until June 2027 but has decided to leave after just two years following a difficult summer.

‌



Hughes arrived from Bournemouth in the summer of 2024 and oversaw the hiring of Arne Slot as manager after Jurgen Klopp stepped down. He was behind the big-money transfers of Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz last summer, as well as the £123million signing of Bradley Barcola this summer.

‌



The 47-year-old has decided to leave shortly after the departure of Michael Edwards from Fenway Sports Group and following a difficult summer which saw Liverpool struggle to bring in new players for Andoni Iraola.

‌



Liverpool said in a statement: "The process of appointing a successor is under way and the outcome will be confirmed in due course."

Hughes said: “First and foremost, I would like to reiterate what I said upon my arrival – it has been a source of great pride to have been given the opportunity to serve this incredible and unique institution. That is something I will always be grateful for.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“My appreciation extends to ownership for their support and leadership, to club staff at all levels who give so much to make Liverpool FC what it is, to the players who make such an enormous contribution and to the fans who support the team in great numbers whenever and wherever games take place.

“I’ll always follow and support the club with great affection, and I wish everyone involved nothing but success for this season and beyond.”

‌



He will team up with Simon Francis - the man who replaced him at Bournemouth two years ago - in Saudi Arabia. Francis left the Cherries at the end of the season and has been overseeing Al-Hilal's transfer activity this summer, including the recent £60million signing of Gabriel Martinelli from Arsenal.

View 2 Images Richard Hughes has followed Michael Edwards out of the door at Liverpool (Image: Robin Jones/Getty Images)

Fenway Sports Group president Mike Gordon said: “Richard joined us at the start of a period of change, embracing that responsibility by leading our football operations department and overseeing recruitment while also providing valuable support to our coaching staff.

‌



“The results we achieved in these areas during this period are testament to this contribution. Nevertheless, we respect Richard’s life choices and wish him and his family well in their next venture."

Hughes' exit continues a summer of change at Liverpool, with Edwards, the chief executive officer of football of FSG, having also left back in July. FSG made the decision to sack Slot after two seasons following a disappointing 2025/26 campaign and the arrival of Iraola as his successor has triggered a changing of the guard behind the scenes.

Liverpool signed wingers Barcola and Victor Munoz and centre-back Ronald Araujo this summer, while defender Jeremy Jacquet also arrived having agreed a transfer in January. Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
