Sports.title: Briatore questions Monaco GP appeal integrity in explosive Italian GP press conference
Sports.content:
Alpine Formula 1 boss Flavio Briatore has questioned the fairness of the appeal procedure against the Monaco Grand Prix results, claiming one judge has a close relationship with McLaren.

Pierre Gasly was one of several drivers penalised in Monaco for exceeding the pitlane speed limit, which was later found to be the result of an incorrect measurement by FOM. Gasly lost his third place, but Alpine launched a right of review against the penalties, with the FIA race stewards agreeing to rescind the Frenchman's penalty.

McLaren and Red Bull appealed against that decision, as the other drivers involved had already served their penalties and didn't have the opportunity to get those rescinded.

Following a lengthy procedure, the FIA's International Court of Appeal ruled in favour of the appellants and reinstated Gasly's two five-second penalties, dropping him to seventh as Red Bull's Isack Hadjar reclaimed a podium spot.

Read Also: Formula 1 Gasly loses Monaco GP podium as penalties reinstated following McLaren and Red Bull appeal

In a statement the Alpine expressed "its disappointment and frustration" with the ruling. But in the FIA's Italian Grand Prix press conference on Friday, executive advisor Flavio Briatore went much further, suggesting the hearing had been unfair as he claimed one of the four judges, Italian-American Filippo Marchino, had links to McLaren.

"I think it's very unfair. We accept the decision, but what is very strange was there were four judges on the panel and one of the judges acted like a prosecutor," Briatore said. "It was four judges, and this one was really a prosecutor against the FIA, against us, against FOM.

"Afterwards we found out what is the reason why this guy was so nasty. It's very linked with McLaren. We have a nice picture of this guy [giving a] speech for McLaren in 2018 at MSO Beverly Hills. He has a foundation, it's called One Drop Foundation and McLaren gave two or three McLaren cars, and this was quite unfair.

Flavio Briatore, Executive Advisor of Alpine F1 Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

"We accept the decision, we accept everything, but it's quite strange to have one guy in the panel linked to the team. This is unfair. The judge normally needs to be independent completely."

Sitting alongside Briatore, McLaren team principal Andrea Stella was visibly taken aback by those accusations.

"I find that this conference is going in a direction that is quite insulting for McLaren, for the reputation of a team that deserves a lot of respect," Stella shot back. "And if anybody makes these kinds of allegations, which seem quite serious, they are going to have to take the responsibility for what they are saying in a public forum.

"The hearing, the whole International Court of Appeal was conducted to the highest standards, and we should not question this case like it's been done."

Commenting on the Monaco appeal outcome, which also moved up McLaren driver Oscar Piastri up from fifth to fourth and earned the two additional championship points, Stella said: "It's a decision that definitely we welcome. It's very important, because it adds clarity in relation to the application of Article 1.1.1 of the International Sporting Code of the FIA, which is foundational for anything that derives from there.

"We appealed because we wanted to make sure that this clarity was sought. We had concerns which were beyond the fact that we might have lost two championship points. Probably these two championship points are not going to make any difference. We were concerned about the application of sporting equality and fairness. This is important and this is not only important for McLaren.

Andrea Stella, McLaren Photo by: Eric Le Galliot

"In fact, not only Red Bull applied, but all teams were present in the hearing because this was a very important moment in terms of clarification as to how we apply the rules, as to how we apply consistency, and also in the specific case, consistency is related to the methodologies that are valid through our race weekend."

Briatore returned to F1 in June 2024 as an executive advisor to then-Alpine CEO Luca de Meo. Earlier in his career, the Italian helped steer the Benetton and Renault teams to consecutive world championships, with Michael Schumacher and Fernando Alonso respectively.

But he was subsequently handed a lifetime paddock ban for his instrumental role in the 2008 Singapore 'Crashgate' scandal. Briatore had been implicated in a plot that involved his driver Nelson Piquet Jr crashing deliberately to cause a safety car intervention that helped his team-mate Alonso win. That lifetime ban by the FIA was overturned in 2010, with the Italian a regular paddock presence as a dealmaker until his official return with Alpine.

Sports.title: Why Norris wanted to set up his own single-seater race team
Sports.content:
Lando Norris says he hopes establishing his own junior team and driver programme can help guide underfunded talent all the way to the Formula 1.

On Wednesday Norris announced two separate projects; a single-seater race team called LN4 Fusion and the LN4 Legacy programme which aims to support a young driver's career through the FIA's ladder.

LN4 Fusion will be run by former long-time Prema team boss Rene Rosin, with Dan Hazlewood running the team's UK arm, and is working on fielding cars in F2, F3 and British F4.

LN4 Legacy Programme, led by former Alpine sporting director Julian Rouse, is a fully-funded programme aimed at supporting young talents all the way to the top. Norris says he was keen to give back to the sport in the face of the spiralling costs of single-seater racing.

"The legacy programme is more to pick out individuals, people that we believe can get to Formula 1 and try and help them one at a time. That's our initial goal," Norris explained. "The fact that drivers have to kind of go out of their way to do it is, I think, an acknowledgement of how difficult it is."

Given the finances involved, LN4 Legacy Programme is starting by backing one yet-to-be-named junior driver, but Norris is hoping he can raise the backing to scale up the programme in the future.

Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

"The scale we're talking about, you're talking tens of millions to start projects like this. And you need good backing from a lot of investors, things like that. And that can easily be and will be a longer-term project," he said.

"We've got to start somewhere. And I'm happy that I'm trying to help at least one to begin with, and then we'll work on two and then three and then four and five."

On the team side, Norris said former Prema chief Rosin was the ideal candidate to lead LN4 Fusion after racing against the Italian's powerhouse team for years, and Rosin surprisingly became available after ceding control of the family-owned team last winter.

"I've known Rene for many years, since I started to go into single-seaters," Norris explained. "We wanted to put together a group that is experienced and knows how to lead a team and not just create one good team, whether that's just in F3 or just in F2, but be able to put together a project and something long term.

"I've also been able to experience over the course of the last seven years what makes a good leader, what makes a good team. A lot of it starts with the person at the very top and he is that person. He was the inevitable choice."

Norris revealed Rosin had received plenty of interest from various corners to join LN4 Fusion, with the project getting a positive reception from around the industry.

Doriane Pin, PREMA Racing, Rene Rosin of PREMA Photo by: Sam Bloxham / Motorsport Images

"The reactions have been great. Rene said he got over a few hundred job requests within the space of an hour or so of the announcement," Norris said. "So, there's a lot of attraction from a range of drivers, but also mechanics, engineers, all the people that make a team. I'm proud that we've been able to put something very special together."

Norris credited the team he had built around him for helping him take on projects like this, meaning he can still focus on his day job at McLaren and pitch in whenever he is available.

But he was also conscious that it will take much more than his project, or fellow world champion Max Verstappen's GT3 race team, to make a lasting impact, as he called upon the FIA and on F1 management to help bring the exorbitant costs on the single-seater ladder.

"If you want to help bigger areas and economies that are just worse to kind of start racing and allow people to start their dream, it's much bigger than just me doing my job and trying to help out on that," he said. "That takes the sport itself. That takes a lot more work from F1, from FIA, from karting companies.

"It's just simply too expensive, so you cannot rely on people just to fund more people. You have to find other ways to make it more friendly for people to start racing and especially financially. You've got to lower the costs somehow of teams, of the ability to go testing, of just signing up to do Formula 2. F2 is over €2million euros, I think, to start.

"You've got to start somewhere. My ability is starting with one and that's already a big project. Hopefully, over time and with more partners coming on board and more money, more support, we can turn it into a way of helping more people from around the world."

Sports.title: F1 Italian GP: Leclerc heads Ferrari 1-2 in opening practice
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc led a Ferrari 1-2 to set the fastest time in first free practice at Formula 1's Italian Grand Prix.

Leclerc's time of 1m23.008s, set on medium tyres, was quick enough to pip team-mate Lewis Hamilton on a hot summer afternoon at the historic Monza circuit.

Leclerc set his time halfway through the first of three practice sessions, boosting expectations from the partisan home crowd in Italy.

Sporting a throwback livery paying tribute to Michael Schumacher's first season with Ferrari in 1996, Ferrari came to its home track with its latest suite of upgrades. Those updates include a refined low-drag rear wing and the Scuderia's second permitted engine upgrade that aims to help slash its power unit deficit to Mercedes.

Read Also: Formula 1 Ferrari to bring upgraded engine to Italian GP under ADUO

Reigning world champion Lando Norris had been leading the early running before the session was interrupted by Colton Herta's stricken Cadillac. The American was asked by his team to park the car with hydraulic issues, bringing out the red flag.

Test driver Herta had been hunting another superlicence point with his practice outing, but due to his lack of mileage the former IndyCar ace will not get one for his Monza run.

The session resumed with 34 minutes on the clock, with Mercedes' George Russell dipping below Norris' time before Leclerc took charge with a 1m23.008s on medium rubber.

Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Hamilton followed Leclerc through in second, shipping 0.173s to his team-mate on the same medium compound, as Russell reclaimed third with a 1m23.312s lap on soft tyres, three tenths down on the leading Ferrari.

Liam Lawson, who returned to Red Bull as regular driver Isack Hadjar continues to recover from his wrist injury, set fourth ahead of championship leader Antonelli.

Antonelli faces a back-of-the-grid penalty for a full power unit change, meaning the championship leader is fully focused on optimising his race set-up.

The Italian demoted Norris to sixth ahead of Racing Bulls man Arvid Lindblad and Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto. Alpine duo Franco Colapinto and Paul Aron, performing rookie FP1 duties in Pierre Gasly's car, rounded out the top 10.

In the second McLaren, Oscar Piastri was 11th ahead of Yuki Tsunoda, who received a second opportunity to fill Lawson's temporarily vacated Racing Bulls seat.

Herta and Aron were just two of four rookie drivers out on track in FP1. Ayumu Iwasa took place in Max Verstappen's Red Bull and Williams young driver Luke Browning got a run in Alex Albon's car as teams took the opportunity to satisfy one of the four mandated rookie FP1 runs for the season on a non-sprint weekend.

With temperatures soaring above the agreed threshold of 31 degrees and expected to do so for every on-track session, the FIA declared a heat hazard for this weekend's running, forcing drivers to either wear cooling vests or carry additional ballast.

Sports.title: Piastri handed three-place grid drop for impeding Lawson | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The stewards have issued Oscar Piastri a three-place grid drop for impeding Liam Lawson during qualifying for the Italian Grand Prix.

Piastri originally qualified third on the grid but will now start from sixth place. Charles Leclerc will take third place on the grid, followed by Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen.

The stewards ruled Piastri did not intend to delay Lawson but did impeded him at the Rettifilo chicane. The incident occured after Piastri left the pits as the two Red Bull cars overtook him. Max Verstappen narrowly made it past without being held up but Piastri was unable to avoid getting in Lawson’s way.

“On leaving the pits, the driver of car 81 [Piastri] was advised [by his race engineer] ‘Verstappen, Lawson and Sainz just crossing, Sainz has pitted, just Verstappen and Lawson, watch out for them as you join’. The driver of car 81 stated that he was not alerted to the fact that [Verstappen] and [Lawson] were on push laps but realised as he was almost at turn one that Verstappen was on a push lap. He slowed significantly and kept to the right to allow Verstappen to pass but was unable to do anything to avoid impeding Lawson who was close behind.

“The stewards accept that with the information he had, and the situation he was placed in, the driver of car 81 had, at this stage, no other options available and hence, inadvertently, and also unnecessarily, impeded car 30 [Lawson].”

Piastri previously received a penalty for impeding Nico Hulkenberg during final practice at the Japanese Grand Prix earlier this year.

Sports.title: How “clever” Verstappen spoiled Russell’s bid for pole in qualifying at Monza | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff punched the team’s monitor in fury after George Russell lost pole position for the Italian Grand Prix.

Russell was held pole position after the drivers’ first runs in Q3 but fell to second on the grid behind Pierre Gasly when the drivers completed their final runs.

After the session Wolff said “we got done over by Max in the final run when preparing.”

As Russell’s team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli will serve a grid penalty for a power unit change this weekend, Mercedes arranged for Antonelli to run a short distance ahead of his team mate to give him a ‘tow’. However Verstappen disrupted this on their final runs.

The McLaren drivers led the field out of the pits at the end of Q3. Verstappen followed them both out with the two Mercedes behind him.

However immediately after leaving the pits Verstappen went across the run-off at turn one. “Tyres are extremely cold somehow,” he told his race engineer Gianpiero Lambiase.

As the gap between Verstappen and the McLarens grew, Verstappen told Lambiase: “I’m not going to catch up to them.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

On the straight approaching the final corner, Parabolica, Verstappen slowed down significantly and pulled to the inside of the track. As Antonelli drew up alongside on the left of the Red Bull, Verstappen moved back onto the racing line.

This forced Antonelli to slow down and brought Russell onto his tail. Russell’s run through the first sector was compromised and his time through there was slower than his previous effort.

“It didn’t go to plan,” said Wolff afterwards. “I think Max was very clever there.

“He just slowed it down, made Kimi and George bunch up. So throughout the lap, George was much too close to Max to do a proper lap and that cost us both.”

Wolff suggested the team should have chosen “another guy to follow than Max.”

Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies apologised to Verstappen at the end of the session after he qualified sixth. “It’s frustrating but much improved compared to yesterday.”

Verstappen, who complained about his car performance degrading during the session, said: “It’s bad, this car is made out of paper, it just loses two tenths already just in ride.” He likened his car to a Fiat Punto during practice.

Sports.title: Gasly takes surprise Monza pole ahead of Russell, Piastri and the Ferraris | 2026 Italian Grand Prix qualifying report
Sports.content:
Pierre Gasly will start the Italian Grand Prix from pole position after beating George Russell by six hundredths of a second in qualifying.

The Alpine driver was in contention for the quickest time throughout qualifying. Just over 24 hours since he learned he had lost his podium finish in the Monaco Grand Prix, and at the same track where he scored his only Formula 1 victory six years ago, Gasly claimed his first pole position and the first for his team in their current guide.

The first runs in Q3 left four different cars separated by less than a tenth of a second: Russell, who gained a tow from team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli approaching turn one, Oscar Piastri, Gasly and Charles Leclerc. Hamilton in the other Ferrari found himself without a tow and was seven-tenths of a second slower than his team mate.

McLaren’s hopes of strengthening their position on their final runs faded when Piastri went off at the first corner. He secured third on the grid but his team mate Lando Norris running behind him was unable to improve and wound up a lowly ninth.

Russell appeared to have secured pole until Gasly nabbed it off him. He had also set the quickest time earlier in the session in Q1, though team mate Franco Colapinto had to settle for eighth place.

Hamilton improved to claim fifth ahead of a frustrated Max Verstappen. The Red Bull driver said his car degraded throughout the session.

The pace of the Alpines created a headache for several teams, notably Ferrari, who were fortunate to get both their cars through into Q3. Gabriel Bortoleto came within a thousandth of a second of beating Hamilton into the top 10 shoot-out and Charles Leclerc was only seven-thousandths faster than his team mate.

A frustrated Liam Lawson missed Q3 after being held up by Piastri at the Rettifilo chicane on his final lap. But Lawson didn’t just direct his frustration at the McLaren driver: he also described his team’s tactics as “appalling”, saying they “left me out to dry”. The stewards will investigate the Piastri incident after qualifying.

Oliver Bearman split the Audis in his upgraded Haas. Lawson came next, followed by Carlos Sainz Jnr and the other Haas of Esteban Ocon.

Yuki Tsunoda failed to make the cut for Q2 in his second appearance for Racing Bulls this year. Alexander Albon, who will take a power unit change penalty, also dropped out in the first round after giving his team mate a tow. The Aston Martins were slowest of all behind the Cadillacs.

Sports.title: Verstappen told Red Bull his car has “less power than a Fiat Punto” in practice | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen made his dissatisfaction with his car clear in final practice for the Italian Grand Prix.

“Mate I have less power than the Fiat Punto,” he told race engineer Gianpiero Lambiase as he prepared for his final run. “I can’t do anything, I can’t even race with them.”

Verstappen made his comment shortly before his run-in with Lewis Hamilton at the Rettifilo chicane late in the session.

Verstappen told his team several times during the session he needs to use the slipstream of another car to have a competitive straight-line speed at the track.

“It’s just slow driving by yourself,” he said early in the session. Following another run he told Lambiase: “I need the tow. You can see the difference again, this is slow.”

“I have no power in the laps,” he added on another run. “I can’t even stay close.”

Verstappen hit a top speed of 331kph on his fastest run as he passed the pits. As is typical with the current cars, his speed tailed off long before he reached the braking zone for the first corner.

The Red Bull driver ended the session third-fastest behind George Russell’s Mercedes and Lewis Hamilton’s Ferrari. His team mate Liam Lawson was 12th fastest, six-tenths of a second off Verstappen.

Sports.title: Russell fastest ahead of scrapping Hamilton and Verstappen in final practice | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell was quickest again in the final practice session ahead of qualifying for the Italian Grand Prix.

He led Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen, who almost collided at the Rettifilo chicane in the final minutes of the session.

The incident began after Verstappen’s race engineer Gianpiero Lambiase told him he could pass Hamilton as both drivers prepared to start their final laps. Verstappen passed Hamilton heading into Ascari, but the Ferrari driver re-passed him approaching the next corner.

Verstappen immediately tried to re-pass Hamilton on the straight but fell back behind the Ferrari, either out of choice or because his car ran low on energy before his rivals. When they reached the chicane, Verstappen dived down the inside while Hamilton swerved onto the run-off area to avoid contact.

“He caused that,” claimed Verstappen. “I got blocked by Max,” said Hamilton.

The pair were separated by a tenth of a second at the end of the session. Andrea Kimi Antonelli, who will start the race from the back of the grid due to a power unit change penalty, was fourth-fastest.

Russell was fortunate to emerge from the session without incurring the wrath of the stewards. He clearly held Oscar Piastri up in Lesmo One yet they opted not to investigate. He also had to slam on his brake to avoid crossing the pit exit line when the light turned red at the end of the session.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Piastri went quickest of all through the first sector but ended up only eighth. His team mate Lando Norris was a tenth of a second quicker and the pair were separated by Charles Leclerc’s Ferrari and Arvid Lindblad’s rapid Racing Bulls. His usual team mate Liam Lawson was only 12th in his Red Bull.

The two Alpine drivers completed the top 10. The Williams drivers were much lower down and both are under investigation for potential yellow flag infringements.

As the cars’ lack of energy means they are losing significant amounts of speed on the straight, drivers used practice to work out how to best improve their lap times by getting a tow from another driver. Lambiase advised Verstappen “I would not recommend starting the lap closer than five seconds to Stroll” as the Red Bull was gaining around three seconds per lap on the Aston Martin.

Temperatures remained high at the Monza circuit, with the track surface hitting 53C during the session.

Prior to the session Cadillac were fined €30,000, all but €5,000 of which was suspended, but Colton Herta’s Clutch Deactivation System did not operate when his car stopped in first practice.

Sports.title: Court of Appeal issues defence to Briatore’s allegations of bias over Gasly decision | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The International Court of Appeal has issued a statement in reaction to the allegations of bias made by Alpine executive director Flavio Briatore yesterday.

The ICA, which is independent of the FIA, ruled against Alpine and the governing body in a case brought by Red Bull and McLaren over a decision made in the Monaco Grand Prix three months ago. The court reinstated two penalties issued to Alpine driver Pierre Gasly which the Monaco stewards previously struck out. Gasly fell from third place to seventh in the classification as a result.

Briatore suggested one of the four ICA judges involved in the decision, Filippo Marchino, favoured McLaren. In response the ICA defended the integrity of its selection process.

“The FIA Courts are aware of public comments questioning the independence and impartiality of the judges of the panel that decided Case ICA-2026-06-07-08-0,” it said in a statement issued by ICA president Laurent Anselmi, ICA vice-president Waltraud Wunsch, International Tribunal president Rui Botica Santos and vice-president Gerard Martin.

“The FIA Courts wish to make clear that the appointment and participation of the judges in that case, like for any other case, were conducted in accordance with the applicable FIA judicial procedures and usual practice, which are inspired by the highest standards like the IBA Guidelines on Conflicts of Interest in International Arbitration.

“All judges are elected by the FIA General Assemblies, some of them upon proposition of a group of at least five F1 teams in accordance with the FIA Statutes. They are all subject to the independence and confidentiality requirements contained in the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, make annual disclosures of interests to the FIA Compliance Officer, and sign a specific declaration of independence for each particular case in consideration of the issue at stake and the parties involved, which is served to the parties.”

The ICA pointed out all parties involved in the case, including Alpine, had the opportunity to raise any concerns they had over the selection of judges.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“At both the beginning and conclusion of the hearing, the parties were invited to raise any issue concerning the proceedings or the composition of the Court,” they said. “None did so.

“No objection was raised during the hearing concerning the manner in which the Court questioned the witness or conducted the proceedings.”

Marchino, a US-based lawyer, was one of four judges involved in the decision. Michael Grech presided over the hearing and Tomas Borec and Luigi Fumagalli were also appointed.

“The ICA emphasises the importance of constituting panels with judges from different cultural and geographical backgrounds,” the statement continued, “This helps ensure that the deliberations and discussions reflect a diversity of legal traditions, perspectives and approaches, further strengthening the fairness, independence, credibility of the process and access to a fair trial.

“A Court’s decision can leave room for various interpretations and comments as for its legal merits; that is fair and accepted by all the judges. The Court is confident in the soundness of the proceedings and the integrity of the judges. The FIA Courts remain committed to the independence and impartiality of their judges and to the integrity of the judicial process.”

Sports.title: Katie Taylor vs Flora Pili Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Super bantamweight Joe McGrail (14-0, 7 KOs) stopped Matthew Boreland (7-1) with a left hook to the body in the fifth round of a 10-round scheduled bout. The win earned McGrail the vacant WBA Continental Gold title. Boreland fought competitively from the opening bell and began building momentum as the rounds progressed. McGrail remained composed, worked to the body, and found the decisive opening late in the fifth. His sharp left hook dropped Boreland, who remained down for the referee’s full count. The stoppage gave the 23-year-old Liverpool southpaw his seventh knockout and handed Boreland his first professional defeat.

Paddy Gallagher (17-6-1 entering) was initially announced as the majority decision winner over Paul Ryan (11-2 entering) after six competitive middleweight rounds. The score was given as 58-55 for Gallagher, but later reports stated that the referee’s card had been read incorrectly. The actual score was reported as 58-56 for Ryan, leaving the announced result subject to an official correction. Gallagher applied steady pressure and used his experience to force exchanges throughout the fight. The taller Ryan worked from his southpaw stance, boxing at range and looking to counter the advancing Belfast veteran. There were no knockdowns, and the result remained in question while the fighters’ official records were being updated.

Bobbi Flood (4-0, 2 KOs) defeated Jack Swallow (4-14-1) by unanimous decision over four rounds in a junior middleweight fight. The referee scored the contest 40-36, giving Flood every round. The 21-year-old Dublin native controlled the action from the opening bell with his cleaner and more consistent punching. Flood used his amateur experience to outbox Swallow, who remained durable but offered little effective offense. No knockdowns occurred as Flood continued piling up points without placing himself in unnecessary exchanges. The Croke Park crowd supported the local prospect throughout his comfortable points win.

Heavyweight prospect Adam Olaniyan (4-0, 4 KOs) overwhelmed Matej Hudak (6-3, 6 KOs) for a first-round stoppage on the preliminary card. The aggressive 20-year-old immediately closed the distance, established his jab, and hurt the much heavier Hudak with combinations upstairs.

A sustained flurry sent Hudak to a knee as blood flowed from his nose and face. Referee Emile Tiedt stopped the fight after Hudak covered up without returning fire. Eddie Hearn is extremely high on Olaniyan, who has the raw talent and marketability to become Matchroom’s flagship heavyweight after Anthony Joshua retires.

Sports.title: Terence Crawford Tests Jaron Ennis’ Easy Work Claim
Sports.content:
“For sure. Anybody that y’all ask me, if somebody gives y’all a list and y’all ask me who I think is easy work, I’m going to say easy work every single time because I believe in myself,” Ennis told TNT Sports. “Can’t nobody in this game do what I do. I feel like I’m the best.”

Nobody expected him to back down. Admitting Crawford could beat him while standing right next to the man was never going to happen. Crawford just wanted to see if Ennis truly believed what he was saying.

Crawford Wants More Than Josh Kelly

Crawford questioned the punishment Ennis took in recent outings, insisting he would have gone in for the finish instead of letting Boots off the hook. Ennis fired right back, telling Crawford he would have done the exact same thing to him.

The talk soon shifted toward Vergil Ortiz Jr. alongside Sebastian Fundora. From Crawford’s perspective, getting past Josh Kelly will not bring Ennis the respect that handling either of those top junior middleweights would produce.

“We would have seen it if you would have fought Vergil,” Crawford pointed out.

Ennis maintained that he fires right back whenever opponents catch him. Crawford acknowledged that grit, yet he still wants to see that fire tested against an elite pressure monster, or a towering champion who drowns rivals in sheer punch volume.

“If you step on Fundora, I give you props,” Crawford said. “If you step on somebody like Vergil, I give you props.”

Naturally, critics might say Boots opted for Kelly instead of taking on the fiercest talent at 154 pounds. Jumping to conclusions ignores the business side. Ortiz works with Golden Boy, Fundora features on PBC cards, while Ennis answers to different promoters. Those corporate barriers easily kill fights without either boxer dodging. Still, Crawford made a valid point. Ennis cannot establish himself as the next face of the sport solely by blowing out fringe contenders.

Ortiz would pose a genuine test for Boots defensively. In Ennis’s eyes, Ortiz brings the ideal style for him. Fluid switch hitting, blistering combinations, sharp counters, all of it looks tailored to pick apart a relentless stalker.

Crawford conceded the matchup looks good on paper, but warned that spotting openings differs greatly from enduring heat long enough to capitalize. Ortiz never just hunts one big shot. He digs to the ribs, smothers space, making opponents fight during moments they want a breather. Boots sometimes retreats straight back, trusting pure reflexes to slip danger. Against Ortiz, backing into the ropes gives away real estate, making brutal body shots impossible to avoid.

Climbing to 154 pounds brings extra danger. Ennis took clean punches from Karen Chukhadzhian, Avanesyan too, without buckling at welterweight. Natural junior middleweights pack extra muscle into every exchange. Boots might own the superior toolkit, yet Crawford wants proof those skills survive several grueling rounds against a bigger puncher.

Crawford also brought up David Avanesyan to downplay Kelly. Avanesyan stopped Kelly inside six rounds back in 2021. Crawford followed up by stopping Avanesyan in round six a year later. Ennis then made Avanesyan quit after five rounds in 2024.

“Kelly already got knocked out by a person that you knocked out,” Crawford remarked, momentarily fishing for Avanesyan’s name.

Boxing math rarely proves anything. Kelly falling to Avanesyan years ago hardly guarantees defeat against everyone who stopped the Russian afterward. Timing shifts, fight camps vary, fighters evolve.

Besides, Boots can flip the script here. Crawford cannot easily separate his own resume by mentioning Avanesyan since both men stopped him. Ennis actually forced the stoppage a round faster, even if Crawford scored the cleaner highlight-reel finish.

“You know what I would’ve done to you if you would’ve got hurt in that last fight?” Crawford meant he would have closed the show immediately, though Ennis insisted Crawford would suffer the same fate. Crawford ultimately struck a warmer tone, mentioning that he wants Boots to thrive across 154, 160, even 168 pounds. Plenty of mutual respect surfaced, though Crawford made sure to protect his own spot at the top.

Sports.title: What Does Hearn Do With Andy Ruiz Jr. Now?
Sports.content:
Knyba was supposed to provide a credible bridge to something lucrative. If Ruiz Jr. handled the tall Polish heavyweight, Hearn could begin selling another fight with Joshua or offer him to Moses Itauma, Filip Hrgovic, Daniel Dubois, or Fabio Wardley. Instead, Ruiz Jr. lost a unanimous decision and was dropped heavily in the seventh round.

The official scores also disguised how poorly he performed. One judge had Knyba winning 117-110, while Glenn Feldman and Kevin Morgan returned narrow 114-113 cards. Those two tallies flattered Ruiz Jr., who spent most of the fight struggling to cross the distance behind Knyba’s jab.

Without the knockdown, Feldman and Morgan would each have scored the fight 114-114, producing a majority draw. Ruiz Jr. came surprisingly close to escaping without another defeat, but the 117-110 card gave a more accurate picture of Knyba’s control.

Scraping out a draw would not have repaired the damage to his value, either. Matchroom needed Ruiz Jr. to beat Knyba convincingly enough to support talk of something bigger.

Matchroom Had to Take the Risk

Plenty will second-guess the decision to put Ruiz Jr. in with Knyba after such a long absence. The matchmaking was not the mistake.

Ruiz Jr. was a fringe contender when he replaced Jarrell Miller against Joshua in June 2019. His stunning knockout victory changed boxing history, but everything that followed suggested the performance was an extraordinary night rather than the beginning of a dominant championship run.

Poorly prepared for the Joshua rematch, he then fought sporadically against Chris Arreola, Luis Ortiz, and Miller. Weight changes, injuries, trainer switches, and long absences became the story of his career.

If he required two or three soft opponents before facing somebody at Knyba’s level, Matchroom had no reason to sign him. Hearn needed immediate proof that the old-hand speed, combination punching, and hunger were still there. He did not receive it.

The lower weight created another false signal. Ruiz Jr. came in at 254.3 pounds, his lightest weight in eight years, allowing the comeback to be presented as evidence of renewed discipline. The scale showed that he had lost weight. It did not show that he had recovered the timing, hand speed, or mobility that once made him dangerous.

Faced with a 6’7″ opponent possessing an 86-inch reach, Ruiz Jr. struggled to cut off the ring and rarely got into punching range in position to release combinations. He followed Knyba, reached with punches, and repeatedly allowed the taller man to jab before tying him up.

Weight can be managed during a training camp. The physical decline caused by age, injuries, and years of inactivity is harder to reverse. Matchroom signed Ruiz Jr. because his fast combinations once made him unusually dangerous for a heavyweight. Against Knyba, that version was nowhere to be found.

What Does Queensberry Gain?

The defeat also leaves Hearn dependent on other promoters if he wants to recover value from Ruiz Jr.’s name.

Itauma needs rebuilding after his loss to Hrgovic, but Frank Warren gains little from helping Matchroom rescue a failed signing. A victory over Ruiz Jr. carries far less weight now that Knyba has exposed him. If Itauma struggles or loses, Queensberry damages one of its most important young heavyweights.

The same issue applies to Hrgovic, Dubois, and Wardley. Ruiz Jr. remains experienced and can still punch, yet beating him no longer proves that one of Warren’s heavyweights belongs near a championship. Queensberry would accept the risk while Matchroom received most of the benefit.

Money might persuade Warren, but he has plenty of available opponents without taking responsibility for Matchroom’s problem.

David Adeleye may be the only recognizable heavyweight Hearn can match with Ruiz Jr. without seeking help from another promoter.

Such a fight would amount to combining two damaged investments. Adeleye was comprehensively beaten by Hrgovic, while Ruiz Jr. has now lost to a lower-level heavyweight. It may produce entertaining action, but it would not restore either man to serious contention.

At 36, Ruiz Jr. would also be facing a younger, larger puncher after Knyba dropped him and left him badly marked around the left eye. Another loss might erase the remaining value of his name.

Saudi-funded heavyweight cards offered Hearn the easiest way to turn Ruiz Jr.’s reputation into money. A convincing comeback win would have allowed Matchroom to offer him for Itauma, Hrgovic, Dubois, Wardley, or another boxer being positioned for a lucrative event.

Losing to Knyba removes much of that appeal. Ruiz Jr. can still be advertised as a former unified champion, but he no longer resembles a credible opponent for a championship fight. The familiar name remains while the sporting justification has disappeared.

Hearn is left without the cash-out opportunity that made the original gamble worthwhile. Ruiz Jr. is too diminished to sell as a contender and still dangerous enough that a rival promoter receives little benefit from using him.

Can Hearn Escape the Contract?

Matchroom announced Ruiz Jr.’s agreement as a multi-fight promotional deal. Other reports described it as a three-fight arrangement, although the full terms and any release clauses have not been made public.

An escape clause after a first fight loss would give Hearn an easy answer. Without one, Matchroom remains tied to a former champion who was signed to reach lucrative bouts quickly but failed at the first stage.

A long rebuilding program makes no sense for Ruiz Jr. His age, inactivity, and history of poor discipline make further investment difficult to justify. Another Joshua fight now looks like nostalgia; Queensberry has little incentive to lend Hearn one of its heavyweights, and easier opposition only delays the same question.

Ruiz Jr. was supposed to provide a shortcut to a profitable heavyweight event. Following the loss to Knyba, Hearn is on his own with an albatross.

Sports.title: Knyba Upsets Andy Ruiz Jr. in Newark
Sports.content:
The Polish heavyweight dropped Ruiz heavily in the seventh round after hurting him with a right hook and following with a barrage. Referee David Franciosi administered the count and allowed Ruiz to continue, with the bell arriving before Knyba could launch another sustained attack.

Ruiz fought with greater urgency in the eighth and ninth, finding some success with body punches and right hands. Knyba regained command over the final three rounds by returning to his jab and maintaining distance.

The judges scored the fight 117-110 and 114-113 twice for Knyba. The two narrow cards did not reflect his overall control or the seventh-round knockdown.

Mielnicki Outboxes Williams

Vito “White Magic” Mielnicki Jr. (24-1, 13 KOs) retained his WBO Global and WBC Continental Americas middleweight titles with a clear unanimous decision over Austin “Ammo” Williams (20-3, 13 KOs). All three judges scored the 10-round fight 98-91.

Mielnicki dropped Williams with a hard right hand during the opening round. Williams rose quickly and survived Mielnicki’s attempt to finish him before the bell.

The New Jersey fighter continued landing the cleaner punches, rocking Williams late in the third and fourth rounds. A right hand from Mielnicki bloodied Williams’ mouth in the fifth.

Williams produced his best sequence in the eighth, landing a counter left that bloodied Mielnicki’s nose and briefly hurt him. Mielnicki recovered, returned to his jab and movement, and finished the fight with the sharper work. David Fields served as the referee.

Garcia Drops Chaves Four Times

Eridson Garcia (24-2, 14 KOs) captured the WBO Latino lightweight title by defeating Alan “Veneno” Chaves (22-1, 19 KOs) over 10 rounds. The scores were 99-87, 99-88, and 98-88.

Garcia scored the first knockdown with a combination during the opening minute of round two. He floored Chaves twice more with body shots in the fifth, leaving the heavily favored Argentinian far behind on the cards.

Garcia slipped while avoiding a punch in the sixth. The referee initially ruled it a knockdown for Chaves, but the commission corrected the call.

A right hook sent Chaves down for the fourth time midway through the ninth. Chaves pursued a stoppage in the final round but never came close to overcoming Garcia’s lead. Earl Brown served as the referee.

Moses Stops Contreras After Five

Newark lightweight Zaquin Moses (8-0, 4 KOs) stopped Angel “Cachorro” Contreras (18-11-2, 12 KOs) after five rounds of their scheduled eight-round fight.

Moses controlled the action with his jab, hand speed, and southpaw pressure. Contreras remained on his stool after the fifth, giving Moses the stoppage victory at the official time of 3:00. Harvey Dock served as the referee.

Sports.title: Damian Knyba Destroys Eddie Hearn’s Andy Ruiz Plans
Sports.content:
Ruiz had a little success attacking the body in the sixth, but the fight nearly ended one round later. Knyba hurt him with a right hook, poured on punches, and dropped him hard near the bell. Ruiz rose with his legs gone and was fortunate that the referee allowed the fight to continue.

The official gave Ruiz a long look and considerable time before restarting the action. Without that delay, Knyba likely would have finished him. The bell then provided another escape before Ruiz had to survive any meaningful follow-up attack.

Hearn’s Ruiz Plans Collapse

Ruiz showed some urgency in the eighth and ninth while Knyba recovered from his attempt to secure the knockout. That brief rally did not make the contest close. Knyba returned to his jab during the later rounds and resumed landing the cleaner punches from distance.

The result leaves Eddie Hearn in a difficult position after recently signing Ruiz to Matchroom. Hearn had discussed moving him quickly toward an IBF title fight with Filip Hrgovic or matching him against Moses Itauma. He can forget about either option after this performance.

Hrgovic is larger, stronger, busier, and far more dangerous than Knyba. Itauma possesses the speed and power to punish the slow feet and defensive openings Ruiz displayed in Newark. Sending Ruiz into either fight next would look less like title planning and more like cashing him out.

Knyba deserves credit for refusing to serve as the opponent in somebody else’s comeback story. Ruiz, however, looked fortunate to hear the final bell. The former unified champion did not resemble a heavyweight one fight away from another title opportunity.

Sports.title: Andy Ruiz Jr vs Damian Knyba Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Undercard results

Vito “White Magic” Mielnicki Jr. (24-1, 13 KOs) defeated Austin “Ammo” Williams (20-3, 13 KOs) by unanimous scores of 98-91, 98-91, and 98-91. Mielnicki dropped Williams with a hard right hand in the opening round, then controlled most of the fight with his jab, movement, and counters. Williams bloodied Mielnicki’s nose and briefly stiffened his legs with a counter left during his strong eighth round. The hometown fighter recovered, regained command through cleaner punching, and retained his WBO Global and WBC Continental Americas middleweight titles in his Matchroom debut.

Eridson Garcia (24-2, 14 KOs) scored a massive upset over Alan “Veneno” Chaves (22-1, 19 KOs), winning the WBO Latino lightweight title by unanimous decision. The judges scored the 10-round fight 99-87, 99-88, and 98-88. Garcia dropped the heavily favored Argentine four times: once in the second, twice in the fifth, and once in the ninth. The Dominican controlled the fight with pressure, counters, and superior activity as Chaves never produced the rally he needed.

Super featherweight Zaquin Moses (8-0, 4 KOs) stopped Angel Antonio Contreras (18-11-2, 12 KOs) when Contreras remained on his stool after the fifth round. Moses controlled the fight with his jab, hand speed, and southpaw pressure. Contreras absorbed steady punishment before his corner ended the fight. The official time was 3:00 of round five in Moses’ first professional appearance at Newark’s Prudential Center.

Viewing Information

Start time: 8:00 p.m. ET

TV: TNT

Streaming: DAZN

Location: Prudential Center, Newark, New Jersey

Running Order

Andy Ruiz Jr vs Damian Knyba, 12 rounds, heavyweight

Vito Mielnicki Jr vs Austin Williams, 12 rounds, middleweight

Alan Chaves vs Eridson Garcia, 10 rounds, lightweight

Zaquin Moses vs Angel Antonio Contreras, 8 rounds, super featherweight

Live Results

Sports.title: Vito Mielnicki Uses Size to Defeat Ammo Williams
Sports.content:
Williams continued pressing, but his defense remained too porous. He frequently followed Mielnicki without moving his head, allowing the New Jersey fighter to land jabs and counters before sliding away. When they exchanged at closer range, Mielnicki’s uppercuts and body shots were sharper. He couldn’t miss with his uppercuts on Ammo all night.

How Much Did Ammo Have Left?

This was the best name on Mielnicki’s record, although Williams may no longer be the same dangerous contender he was several years ago. Ammo had already been softened up in a one-sided loss to WBC middleweight champion Carlos Adames last March. That beating, combined with Friday’s knockdown and wide scores, raises questions about how much punishment Williams can continue absorbing at this level. Ammo looked half-stunned from the get-go, legs looking wobbly with every hard shot that Mielnicki threw. The heavy pounding that Ammo took in the Adames fight couldn’t have helped him.

He still produced one threatening moment in the eighth, landing a counter left that bloodied Mielnicki’s nose and briefly stiffened his legs. Mielnicki responded intelligently rather than getting dragged into a reckless exchange, returning to lateral movement and cleaner combinations over the final two rounds.

The performance was an important step for Mielnicki, but the size advantage and Williams’ recent damage should be considered before treating it as proof that he is ready for the leading middleweights. He handled the opponent Matchroom placed in front of him and showed more discipline than in earlier fights. The next test needs to come against a physically comparable middleweight who has not already been through a punishing loss.

Sports.title: Eridson Garcia Exposes Alan Chaves in Newark
Sports.content:
Garcia floored Chaves in the second round and nearly put him down again in round four. Things grew worse in the fifth, when Chaves took a knee before hitting the canvas again moments later. In the ninth, Chaves went down again after eating a left from Garcia.

The referee Albert Earn Brown looked like he was ready to stop the contest after Chaves was dropped in round nine. By that stage, the fight had become less about who would win and more about whether Chaves would survive the full 10 rounds. You got to give Chaves credit for being a warrior to toughen it out, but there are no words to describe how one-sided this fight was. Chaves looked like he didn’t belong in the same ring with Eridson. The size advantage Eridson had was noticeable. He looked like he’d rehydrated to a welterweight, and appeared considerably bigger than Chavez.

Matchroom’s Lightweight Plans Take a Hit

Chaves was completely out of his league against a 32-year-old opponent brought in to test him. Garcia was quicker, smarter, and far more comfortable during every phase of the fight. Hearn recently signed Chaves to Matchroom and regarded him as a future lightweight star, but this performance exposed how far he is from competing with the division’s better fighters.

The result makes retaining Andy Cruz even more important for Hearn. Matchroom has spent time and money developing Cruz, yet the Cuban is unhappy with the promotion and has discussed becoming a free agent. Watching Chaves fall apart against Garcia should erase any thought that Matchroom can afford to lose its best lightweight.

Cruz would likely have cleaned Eridson out tonight. His timing, footwork, defensive awareness, and ability to read a southpaw would have made this a completely different fight. Chaves had none of those answers, and Eridson made him pay for it from the first bell to the last.

Ghana News.title: MTN Ghana webinar urges SMEs to get financial discipline right
Ghana News.content:
MTN Ghana has urged entrepreneurs to adopt stronger financial discipline and smarter money management practices to build sustainable businesses.

The call was made during a virtual financial literacy webinar organised as part of activities marking the company’s 30th anniversary.

Held under the theme “Making Money Moves: Building a Financially Smart and Sustainable Business,” the webinar brought together Yaw Saifah, Senior Manager for BankTech at MobileMoney Fintech Limited; Paul Mante, Managing Director of EDC Investments; and Desmond Bredu, Head of Client Coverage at Stanbic Investment Management Services.

The speakers addressed financial discipline, cash flow management, digital payments, and investment and wealth creation.

Mr Saifah advised entrepreneurs to separate their personal finances from business funds to improve financial visibility and discipline.

He said mixing the two made it difficult for business owners to determine their actual revenue, profit and available working capital.

“Separating personal and business funds gives you visibility and discipline,” he said.

He also encouraged businesses to use digital tools to monitor sales, payments, invoices and cash flows.

According to him, digital platforms can help businesses with multiple branches monitor their operations remotely and maintain verifiable transaction records.

He further advised entrepreneurs to consider Enterprise Resource Planning systems for managing customer records, inventory, and other business activities.

“Your problem may not be limited capital or illiquidity. It may be that you are not managing your inventory properly,” he said.

Mr Mante, meanwhile, warned entrepreneurs against confusing revenue with profit.

He said some businesses collapse because owners begin spending heavily as soon as sales increase without first determining whether the business is profitable.

“Don’t spend before you calculate your profit. You make a profit before you start spending; you don’t spend before you start making a profit,” he advised.

He also cautioned against rapid expansion without sufficient working capital.

“Sales do not mean profitability. You can be making sales and still collapse,” he said.

“Revenue makes the noise, profit creates wealth, and cash keeps an SME alive,” Mr Mante added.

He urged entrepreneurs to be patient with wealth creation and avoid the pressure to become rich quickly.

“Building wealth is not a sprint; it is a marathon. It cannot happen overnight,” he said.

Mr Bredu, for his part, encouraged Ghanaians to start investing regardless of the size of their income.

He said entrepreneurs and individuals could begin with small amounts instead of waiting until they had substantial funds.

“You do not need a huge amount of money to invest. You can start with GH¢50,” he said.

He cautioned against keeping money idle because inflation gradually reduces its purchasing power.

“If you keep GH¢100 under your bed or leave it idle, it may still be GH¢100 after one year, but inflation would have reduced what it can buy,” he explained.

Mr Bredu also stressed the need for discipline after earning money.

“Making money requires taking risks, but managing money requires frugality and discipline,” he said.

He urged business owners to track their expenses, control lifestyle inflation and retain part of their earnings for reinvestment.

“Having the money coming in is not enough. You need to retain it because retaining the money is what enables you to scale up and move to the next level,” Mr Bredu said.

Ghana News.title: Duvor Klu, Hua crowned champions as J30 Accra Week 1 concludes
Ghana News.content:
Ghana’s Gwendolyn Duvor Klu and China’s Ruoyu Hua have been crowned singles champions as the first week of the J30 Accra – Tennis Foundation Ghana Open came to an end.

Klu claimed the Girls’ Singles title after an impressive campaign on home soil, while Hua emerged as the Boys’ Singles champion.

Ghanaian Jeff Frimpong finished as runner-up in the Boys’ Singles competition, while Togo’s Winner Gakpo was the Girls’ Singles finalist.

The opening week also produced competitive doubles contests, with players from across the world combining to battle for the titles.

Israel’s Yarden Shalom Gamliel and India’s Shivtej Shirfule, the top seeds, won the Boys’ Doubles title. They overcame the challenge of Great Britain’s Denzell Darkey and Ghana’s Jeff Frimpong, who finished as finalists.

In the Girls’ Doubles, Klu and Gakpo combined successfully to claim the title.

Nigeria’s Goodnews Aina and India’s Sharanya Sawant finished as finalists after putting up a strong challenge in the competition.

The results highlight the international nature of the J30 Accra tournament, which brought together junior players from Africa, Europe, Asia and beyond to compete in Accra.

For Ghana, Klu’s Girls’ Singles and Doubles triumphs, together with Frimpong’s two finalist finishes, provided some of the major highlights of the opening week.

With Week One now concluded, attention turns to the next stage of the tournament next week as the young players continue their development on the ITF World Tennis Junior Tour.

Ghana News.title: Gov’t to make rural telephony services cheaper by first quarter of 2027 – Sam George
Ghana News.content:
The Minister of Communications, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, says the government is putting in place measures to make calls and data services on rural telephony networks cheaper by the end of the first quarter of 2027.

He said the Ministry was engaging the National Communications Authority (NCA) and the Ghana Investment Fund for Electronic Communications (GIFEC) as well as mobile network operators to review the current charging arrangements and ensure that subscribers using rural telephony sites could benefit from their existing voice and data bundles.

The Minister disclosed this on Friday, September 4, when he toured some rural telephony sites in the Akwapim South District and an ongoing cell site at the Koforidua lorry terminal in the Eastern Region.

Areas visited included Dumpong, Nkumkrom, Nsakye and Obosono, as part of a nationwide assessment of telecommunications infrastructure to identify areas requiring urgent intervention.

Mr George said, “We have rural telephony largely in our rural communities and when you look at those communities, the economic ability is not like that of the urban area, but call and data on the rural telephony is more expensive than the urban area. It makes no sense to me.”

The Minister explained that under the current arrangement, customers with existing voice or data bundles could be charged directly when they connected to a rural telephony site, rather than using their purchased bundles.

He said a policy directive had consequently been issued to reverse the arrangement, with the NCA working with telecommunications operators on the technical integration required to implement the change.

“So we've given a directive, I've given a policy directive to reverse that. The NCA is working with the telecom players to ensure that the necessary technical integrations are done,” he said.

The Minister also announced plans to upgrade rural telephony sites to support at least 4G technology, noting that it was no longer appropriate to provide communities with predominantly 2G and 3G services when the world was advancing towards 5G and beyond.

“We must give them at the very least 4G,” he said, adding that government would have to make a deliberate investment in telecommunications infrastructure just as it invested in roads and hospitals.

On network expansion, Mr George said mobile network operators were currently undertaking one of the largest increases in cell-site infrastructure in the country in the past decade.

He said MTN was deploying 800 sites, while Telecel was expected to deploy about 350, with nearly 180 of the MTN sites already completed.

The government expected about 400 of the 800 MTN sites to be completed by the end of the year, with all expected to be operational by the first or second quarter of 2027.

Mr George said the expansion, together with the ongoing 5G spectrum auction, was expected to ease network congestion and improve customer experience nationwide.

He also disclosed that about GH¢30 million had been allocated to rural telephony under the GIFEC budget this year, equivalent to nearly US$3 million, with US$400,000 earmarked for immediate remedial works on 20 sites.

He said approximately 1,400 rural telephony sites were currently carrying traffic, while another 300 completed sites were awaiting connection to donor sites.

He appealed to communities to support the deployment of telecommunications infrastructure to enable citizens to benefit from improved connectivity.

Meanwhile, residents of Nkumkrom appealed to the government to fast-track the construction of the telephony site in the community to improve mobile service in the area.

The project has been delayed due to what the Minister said was the unavailability of a line site to enable connections to already existing masts within the catchment area.

Materials for the construction of the mast have already been shipped to the community.

A resident of the community, Michael Osei, told the Ghana News Agency that the delay in setting up the mast was impacting negatively on their lives, urging the government to speed up the process.

The Minister was accompanied on the tour by Dr Edmund Yirenkyi Fianko, Director-General of the NCA; Mr Rashid Tanko Computer, Chief Executive Officer of GIFEC; Mrs Rita Akosua Adjei Awatey, Eastern Regional Minister; and engineers from the Ministry, NCA and Mobile Network Operators.

Ghana News.title: National Chief Imam remains Ghana’s strongest symbol of interfaith harmony – Mahama Ayariga
Ghana News.content:
Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs has described the National Chief Imam, Sheikh Dr Osman Nuhu Sharubutu, as Ghana’s strongest symbol of interfaith harmony, urging Muslims and other citizens to emulate his example of tolerance and peaceful coexistence.

Mahama Ayariga made the remarks when he paid a courtesy call on the Chief Imam at his residence in Accra, to seek his blessings and prayers following his assumption of office as Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs.

The Minister said the Chief Imam had demonstrated unwavering support for him by sending delegations to support him during his parliamentary vetting and swearing-in ceremony.

He explained that his new portfolio came with enormous responsibilities, including overseeing the country’s 261 Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies, matters relating to chieftaincy, religious affairs and sanitation.

Mr Ayariga said he considered it important to begin his engagement with key stakeholders by visiting the National Chief Imam to seek spiritual guidance and prayers.

“I have come this morning to seek his blessings and his prayers so that I will be able to stand up to the challenge and perform the task entrusted to me by His Excellency, President John Dramani Mahama,” he added.

He also conveyed the appreciation of President John Mahama to the National Chief Imam for his continued prayers, guidance and support.

Mr Ayariga said the President’s decision to entrust him with responsibility for religious affairs reflected the importance the government attached to religious harmony and the welfare of all faith communities.

Drawing inspiration from Islamic teachings, Mr Ayariga said Muslims must not only follow religious texts but also learn from the example set by their leaders.

He described the National Chief Imam as a quintessential example of a good Muslim whose life and leadership should inspire others to promote peace, tolerance and unity.

The Minister expressed confidence that Ghana would continue to enjoy peaceful relations among its diverse religious and cultural communities if citizens embraced the values championed by the National Chief Imam.

The National Chief Imam offered prayers for the Minister, asking Allah to grant him the strength, wisdom and good health to successfully execute his new responsibilities, as he had taken over from the good works of his predecessor.

He acknowledged the enormity of the task placed on the Minister’s shoulders and said the assignment required both physical and mental strength.

“May Allah help you to overcome the enormity of this onerous duty that has been put on your shoulders. May He grant you good health and the strength of body and mind,” he said

The National Chief Imam stressed that national development could not be achieved without peace and harmony, reiterating his commitment to continually pray for Ghana to remain a peaceful and secure country.

He said peace was a prerequisite for the successful implementation of policies and projects aimed at improving the lives of citizens.

The Chief Imam also prayed for President Mahama, asking Allah to grant him the vision, wisdom and support needed to successfully implement projects and policies that would benefit Ghanaians.

He further prayed for government appointees, ministers and district chief executives to support the President and work towards the success of his administration.

The National Chief Imam said he continued to pray not only for peace in Ghana but also for other countries facing conflict and instability, stressing the importance of global peace and security.

Ghana News.title: Gov’t to upgrade all rural telephony networks to 4G capability – Sam George
Ghana News.content:
The government will upgrade all Rural Telephony Project (RTP) sites across the country to at least 4G capability to improve connectivity and enhance digital services in underserved communities.

The Minister of Communications, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, said the move was necessary because 2G and 3G connectivity were no longer adequate at a time when the world was advancing towards 5G and 6G technologies.

He said the upgrade formed part of a broader review of the Rural Telephony Project, which the Ministry would soon present to Cabinet.

“The world has moved to 5G, getting to 6G, so at the very least we must give 4G to our networks,” he said.

The Minister said this in an interview with the media after inspecting rural telephony sites at Dumpong, Nkumkrom, Nsakye and Obosono in the Akwapim South District, as well as an ongoing cell site at the Koforidua lorry terminal in the Eastern Region.

He was accompanied by Dr Edmund Yirenkyi Fianko, Director-General of the National Communications Authority (NCA); Mr Rashid Tanko Computer, Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Investment Fund for Electronic Communications (GIFEC); Mrs Rita Akosua Adjei Awatey, Eastern Regional Minister, and engineers from the Ministry, NCA and mobile network operators.

The visit formed part of the Ministry's nationwide assessment of telecommunications infrastructure to identify areas requiring urgent intervention.

Mr George said donor and mast sites under the RTP were already configured to support 4G services, but receiving equipment and radios at local sites needed upgrading.

He said Government would make deliberate investments in telecommunications infrastructure, just as it invested in roads, schools and hospitals.

“We must invest in telecom and decide that we are going to convert all our Rural Telephony sites to do a minimum of 4G, ready for 5G as well,” he said.

The Minister also announced plans to reverse additional charges associated with calls and data usage on some rural telephony networks.

He explained that some subscribers connected to RTP sites could have their regular data bundles bypassed, resulting in direct data charges.

He said the NCA was working with mobile network operators to undertake the technical integration required to resolve the challenge.

On network expansion, Mr George said MTN was deploying 800 new sites this year, while Telecel was constructing about 350, bringing the total number of new sites to about 1,100.

He said nearly 180 of MTN’s sites had already been completed, with about 400 expected to be operational by the end of the year and all 800 completed by the first or second quarter of 2027.

According to him, the development represented the biggest investment in cell-site infrastructure expansion by a major telecommunications operator in the past decade.

The Minister said the expansion, together with the ongoing 5G spectrum auction, would help reduce network congestion and improve service quality nationwide.

He said the government had allocated about GH¢30 million to rural telephony projects under the GIFEC budget this year, including GH¢4 million for urgent remedial works on 20 sites.

Some sites, he said, had suffered damage to radio equipment due to lightning strikes and power surges, while others required cabling works.

He announced that about 1,400 RTP sites were currently carrying traffic, with another 300 completed and awaiting connection to donor sites. About 300 additional sites remained under construction towards the project’s target of 2,016 sites.

The Government was also developing a peri-urban network strategy to address connectivity challenges in rapidly expanding communities and congested urban settlements.

He described it as “the biggest investment in infrastructure in terms of cell sites increase in the last 10 years” by a major telecommunications operator.

The Minister said the expansion, together with the ongoing 5G spectrum auction, was expected to ease network congestion and improve customer experience across the country.

“We’re going to do more of a peri-urban network that’s going to look at these new settlements that are springing up, both as telcos and as governments invest in building their infrastructure,” the Minister emphasised.

He appealed to communities to support the construction of new cell sites, assuring them that telecommunications infrastructure was regulated by the NCA, the Ghana Standards Authority and the Radiation Protection Institute.

“Cell sites do not produce radioactive waste. They produce radiation. Radiation is healthy,” he said.

Ghana News.title: ‘We’ve never seen a CJ in our judiciary system who is everywhere like MTN’ – Janet Nabla
Ghana News.content:
People's National Party (PNP) flagbearer hopeful Janet Nabla has criticised Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie over what she describes as his extensive public engagements and association with activities involving members of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC).

According to her, the Chief Justice’s frequent appearances at political and social events involving NDC members raise questions about the perceived political neutrality of Ghana’s Judiciary.

“I have a problem. It is a very huge problem with the Chief Justice because we have never seen in our lives that a Chief Justice becomes MTN and goes everywhere. Everywhere you pass, you see him," she said on Joy Prime on Saturday, September 5.

She cited the Chief Justice’s presence at football-related activities and funerals involving individuals associated with the NDC as examples of what she considers political engagements.

“When we talk about football, you will see him with NDC people. This football that just ended, the World Cup, NDC people put their constituency executives over there. They were there. Who were they there with? With the Chief Justice,” she said.

“When an NDC person is having a funeral, they invite the Chief Justice. You see him sitting with the NDC people,” she added.

Her comments come amid growing public discussion about the Chief Justice’s recent engagements outside the courtroom and his remarks during visits to public institutions.

She rejected suggestions that such engagements should not be viewed through a political lens, arguing that the nature and frequency of the Chief Justice’s interactions with political actors could affect public perceptions of the Judiciary.

“People are saying that he is not doing political. Those are political activities,” Janet Nabla said.

She therefore questioned whether the Chief Justice’s conduct is consistent with the expected neutrality and independence of the office.

Ghana News.title: Lawyers, prosecutors fume over abandoned 26-year-old Upper West High court project
Ghana News.content:
Members of the legal fraternity in the Upper West Region, alongside state prosecutors, have registered fierce displeasure over the stalled construction of the multi-million-cedi regional High Court complex, describing the deserted site as a “cemetery” after two decades of dashed hopes.

The regional leadership of the Ghana Bar Association (GBA) and the Office of the Attorney General revealed that despite high-profile inspections and firm commitments given by national delegations, the three-storey court structure has once again been abandoned by the contractor, leaving the regional capital without a single purpose-built modern courtroom.



Visiting the deserted project grounds on Friday, legal practitioners expressed dismay that equipment had been packed off, leaving open gates, uninstalled fittings exposed to theft, and fresh paint peeling off exterior walls just three months after application.

Chairman of the Ghana Bar Association in the Upper West Region, Siddique Ubeidu, warned that members fear for their lives daily due to the worsening decay of the makeshift buildings currently housing justice delivery in the region.



“You will recall that this work was started almost 20 years ago, and it has been one reason or excuse for another,” Siddique Ubeidu stated.

“Our national executive committee of the GBA was here on the 1st of April and was given assurances that within three to four months, the building would be completed.

Subsequently, the Chief Justice sent another team led by a Supreme Court judge, Justice Yonny Kulendi, alongside all directors from the Judicial Service, assuring us it would be available for use within two to three months.”

“Here we are today, 4th September, and the place is a cemetery. If you look at the way they packed their equipment, there is no sign that they will be back anytime soon.

What is even more worrying is that the paint done less than three months ago has started peeling off, pointing to the suspect quality of the work,” he added.

According to the bar president, a visit inside the operational Wa Circuit Court exposes severe structural deterioration that poses a daily hazard to occupants.

“We feel very depressed and disappointed, and we even fear for our lives. You can see gaping, life-threatening cracks inside the judge's chambers and the courtroom. Staff have no offices and compete with litigants inside the courtroom, even eating their meals there.

"Years ago, former Chief Justice Sophia Akuffo came to town and threatened to shut the court down due to its state, yet nothing was done while the population grew,” Siddique Ubeidu lamented.



Principal State Attorney, Upper West Region, Saeed Abdul-Shakur, described the state of affairs as a national embarrassment that borders on institutional neglect of the region. “It didn’t take China 20 years to build the Three Gorges Dam, nor Dubai 10 years to build the Burj Khalifa.

Why is it taking a whole nation 20 years to set up just a three-storey building for a court complex?” Saeed Abdul-Shakur queried. “We are serving 11 districts, yet the High Court, District Court, and Circuit Court are all operating out of colonial and temporary makeshift structures.

We thought the visits by the Parliamentary Select Committee and the Chief Justice’s delegation meant light at the end of the tunnel, without knowing it was an oncoming train bound to crash the justice system.

We cannot be delivering justice under trees,” the Principal State Attorney stated, stressing that lawyers and litigants travel from Accra, Kumasi, and Tamale to litigate in Wa.

Weighing in on the missed schedules, Acting Secretary, Ghana Bar Association, Upper West Region, Crispin Wura-Sey Ziekah, warned that the continuous delays have left vital court infrastructure compromised. “Are we waiting for our courts to collapse before we complete this structure?” Crispin Wura-Sey Ziekah questioned.

“At the District Court, a magistrate has to wait in his vehicle until proceedings are assembled before stepping inside. We were assured the new complex would be commissioned during the Bar Conference hosted here last year; it failed.

We were promised we would start the new legal year this October in the complex, but the contractor has packed out completely, and the unsecured gates leave installations vulnerable to vandalism.”

The legal practitioners have appealed directly to the Chief Justice, the Attorney General, and the Minister for Justice to step in and compel the contractor and project consultants back to site, demanding that the facility be operationalised to avert a catastrophe in the region's makeshift courtrooms.

Meanwhile, the contractor for the project, Project Seven Limited, has refuted claims that it has abandoned the site. A director of the company, Simon Sowah, speaking to JoyNews, said the company has unpaid certificates pending with the Judicial Service and central government.

According to him, the company will return to the site once the government does the needful and settles its indebtedness.

Ghana News.title: At least two dead in blast at Bolivia military barracks
Ghana News.content:
At least two people have been killed after an explosion at a military barracks in Bolivia—but authorities fear the toll could be higher.

Bolivian Defence Minister Ernesto Justiniano said at least 81 people had been injured when "pyrotechnic material" detonated at the barracks, where an artillery regiment was stationed, at about 14:30 local time (18:30 GMT) on Friday. Fourteen others remain missing.

Health official Rita Nebraska told local television between 10 and 15 people were believed to have died in the incident in Viacha, about 30km (19 miles) from La Paz, according to Reuters.

Police said dozens of homes had been damaged by the blast and that emergency workers were searching the rubble.

Nebraska said there was a risk of a further explosion and urged people to stay at least 150m from the military base.

Base commander Colonel Antonio Amaru told reporters on Saturday that a sergeant and 13 conscripted soldiers aged between 18 and 19-years-old were among the missing.

Bolivia's President Rodrigo Paz expressed his "deepest solidarity" with the families of those who had died and had been injured.

He wrote on social media that a "thorough, technical, and transparent investigation" would take place into what happened.

Police spokesman Roger Roca told news agency AFP that fireworks had been stored at the barracks and the cause of the blast remained under investigation.

Viacha's authorities have declared three days of mourning.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.
