Fathi stood beneath a newly restored plaque from the National Organization for Urban Harmony’s “Lived Here” memorial initiative, which honors Egypt’s cultural and intellectual luminaries.

The moment followed a high-profile incident in which thieves targeted the building entrance and stole the original brass commemorative marker honoring Qandil.

Refusing to let his tribute be erased, Fathi petitioned cultural authorities and pushed until the official memorial plaque was reinstalled at the doorstep of their longtime home.

Fathi is now experiencing deep sorrow following the loss of her only daughter, Yasmine, whose recent funeral service at the mosque saw chaotic media scenes.

In response, the family—specifically Yasmine’s father, Saif Abol Naga—decided to prohibit all photography and filming at the condolence service.

I hope her request is respected by everyone.

Fathi originally stepped away from acting studios in 2000, though she did not view the move as the end of her artistic career.

She pursued several projects, including a self-produced film intended to co-star Omar Sharif and be directed by Samah Anwar, who had formally studied filmmaking.

Despite holding multiple working sessions together, creative differences arose between Fathi and Sharif, halting communication and bringing the project to a complete standstill. Subsequent project offers failed to spark her interest.

Years ago, several websites published a recent photograph of the veteran actress.

Some expected the image to provoke sadness among observers tracing the effects of time, seemingly preferring she resemble certain older female stars whose faces appear decades younger through artificial means.

Contrary to those expectations, the photograph brought happiness to millions.

Fathi stepped away from public life in a quiet manner that reflects her personality—one that avoids noise and stays clear of any battle outside the artistic realm.

Over the course of her long artistic journey, Fathi frequently served on festival jury panels, demonstrating a sharp capacity for technical film analysis alongside her signature wit and quick intellect.

During daily gatherings alongside her late husband, renowned journalist Hamdi Qandil—in Cairo and Dubai while he hosted his widely viewed weekly show “Qalam Rasas” on Dubai TV—an agreement was forged to document Fathi’s life story across a 30-episode television program directed by Ali Badrakhan.

Initial structural planning for the series had already commenced, relying heavily on Fathi’s candor, humor, and extensive cinematic legacy.

However, the project was ultimately shelved before completion. The author refrained from pressing Fathi for an explanation, recognizing that as the originator of the idea, she maintained full discretion to withdraw from its execution.

Over the past decade, Fathi tightly closed her personal circle, limiting phone calls to a very small group of family and close friends. Respecting her decision, the author refrained from reaching out to avoid obligating her to respond.

Numerous film festivals both inside Egypt and abroad attempted to honor Fathi, but she firmly closed the door on public tributes. She has never denied her historic career—studded with dozens of artistic and social achievements—including humanitarian work that she consistently preferred to keep out of the spotlight.

Fathi is currently living through the peak of grief following the death of Yasmine, who was always the apple of her eye.

With unwavering faith in God and the warmth of love from millions of fans, Fathi continues to draw strength, carrying Yasmine’s memory deep within her heart.

Author’s biography:

Tarek al-Shenawy is a journalist, film critic, and professor of film criticism at the Faculty of Mass Communication, Cairo University.

He holds a Bachelor’s degree from the Faculty of Mass Communication in Cairo University, and a Bachelor’s degree from the Institute of Cinema.

Shenawy has won numerous awards for best critical article from the Syndicate of Journalists multiple times, as well as from film societies. He was awarded the title of Best Popular Film Critic by the “Der Giest” Association in 2015 – a title that has not been awarded to anyone since.

He has also chaired and participated in the judging committees of numerous international film festivals, including the Valencia and Dubai Film Festivals.

He began practicing film criticism nearly 35 years ago in the Rose al-Yousse magazine and continues to write a weekly column titled “Kalma we Nos” (Word and a Half) on its pages. He has written for numerous magazines, newspapers, and websites both inside and outside Egypt.

He currently writes a daily column in Al-Masry Al-Youm newspaper and a weekly column in Al-Sharq al-Awsat newspaper, and has published over thirty books.

World.title: 24 hours that show how preoccupied Trump is
World.content:
It can be difficult to decide which Roman metaphor more aptly captures President Donald Trump’s posture these days.

Is it “bread and circuses,” feeding the American people a series of distractions — amusing or otherwise — from their worries about the economy? Or is it Nero, fiddling with his ballroom plans while the Republican Party’s midterm hopes burn?

What’s clear is that Trump and his administration aren’t going to course correct any time soon.

The last 24 hours have been a case in point. And the last couple weeks have been inauspicious for anyone who hoped Trump might suddenly focus on the political task at hand.

Thursday marked exactly two months until Election Day 2026. And the first votes are about to be cast, with North Carolina sending out mail ballots on Friday.

But despite a bevy of polling showing Americans want Trump to focus on affordability and the economy, he appears preoccupied with anything but.

On Thursday alone, we learned the Trump administration has hired a new pool contractor to clean up the mess he made of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, announced the start of construction on Trump’s 250-foot “triumphal arch” and launched a series of arcade-style video games, including one that allows users to arrest undocumented immigrants.

The White House is also reportedly launching a reality show-like competition for entrepreneurs, just weeks after Trump’s “Patriot Games” flopped and after an actual reality show from the Department of Transportation was released. (It says a nonprofit paid for it; not taxpayers.)

By Friday morning, two big stories — from the New Yorker and New York Magazine — detailed what can only be called Trump’s obsession with his ballroom and other construction and beautification projects in Washington, DC.

Trump even sat for an interview — and gave a construction tour, of course — for the New York Magazine piece.

Reporter Ben Terris reported that the president’s official calendar is “peppered with meetings about other projects around Washington that can often last an hour or longer.”

And in perhaps the most eyebrow-raising scene, Trump actually agrees with Georgia Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff’s contention that he’s building monuments to himself because he doesn’t think others can be counted on to do it.

“That’s true,” Trump said. “Nobody will do it once I’m gone. When I leave here, nobody will.”

The fact that Trump would say this out loud is stunning. Ossoff meant this as a dig.

But it also suggests Trump might be feeling the pressure to get these projects done fast. He has a finite amount of time to plaster his name on things and build things that he’ll be remembered by. It could get more difficult by January, when Democrats could control one or both chambers of Congress.

Trump even talks about how it will supposedly be impossible for Democrats to demolish his ballroom, if they wanted to. (“It’s nuclear concrete,” he told New York Magazine. “I think it would be very hard. It’s meant for if there’s a nuclear attack.”)

Terris also runs through how Trump in his public appearances often seems distracted by his construction projects as he’s attending to much more serious business.

And that’s really the problem with all of this, at least if you’re a congressional Republican staring at a concerning midterm election.

It’s not just that Trump is distracted; it’s that he’s focused on things that polls show Americans view as frivolous and don’t want — at the expense of things they really want him to do (i.e. lowering prices and ending the war with Iran).

Trump’s ballroom is 2-to-1 unpopular.

Americans opposed his 250-foot “triumphal arch” 52%-21% in an April poll.

A July poll showed 65% of Americans described themselves as upset or dissatisfied with the ballroom, arch and Reflecting Pool projects.

While Trump tries to put his name on things like the Kennedy Center, just 9% of Americans think that’s appropriate for him to do as an incumbent president.

And Trump’s other preoccupation in recent days and weeks — his new trade war with Canada, which led him move to rename Lake Ontario as “Lake America” — fares little better. Reuters-Ipsos polling this week showed Americans opposed the Canada tariffs 57%-20% and the “Lake America” renaming 63%-14%.

Trump last week held a White House event for the latter move, which it turns out even his fellow Republicans oppose by double digits.

All of this cements a tough picture for the GOP. Polling has for months shown that Americans view Trump as neglecting more important fare.

CBS News polling has recently shown 78% of Americans said he’s not focused enough on lowering prices, and July CNN polling shows around the same percentage (73%) said he hasn’t paid enough attention to the country’s most important problems.

It’s not fair to say Trump has completely neglected the cost of living.

He recently announced he would pause tariffs on imported beef to try to lower prices for consumers, and on Friday he threatened to stop trading with other countries if the Federal Reserve doesn’t lower interest rates.

Both moves could theoretically save people money.

But both moves also betray Trump’s preference for questionable quick fixes. The beef tariffs move, for example, is expected to have a negligible impact, CNN reported, while irritating domestic cattle ranchers and even some Republicans. And the extortionate threat to the Fed seems unlikely to bear fruit. (Indeed, lowering interest rates could actually send inflation higher.)

The CNN poll in July contained another telling finding. Fully 66% of Americans said Trump did not put the good of the country above his own personal gain. That included 76% of independents and 30% of Republicans.

And more than a month later, with the 2026 general election truly kicking off, it’s as if he’s bent on proving those people right.

World.title: US oil deal promises a flood of investment in Venezuela. When will its people feel the benefits?
World.content:
The enormous investments that the US and Venezuela have promised from their new oil production deal have brought cautious optimism that Venezuelans face a new period of prosperity after more than a decade of economic and social turmoil.

As the country with the world’s largest proven reserves of crude oil, some analysts expect Venezuela to reap some benefits from foreign investment even before it begins to increase production.

But its biggest economic gains will take time to unfold, analysts warn, and it remains unclear exactly when the general population will feel the effects.

Some residents have expressed fears the US will extract the greatest profits and leave little left over for them.

Moreover, the Venezuelan opposition has questioned the current government’s ability to manage these new investments, citing a lack of transparency and civil liberties.

Still, experts believe there’s reason to be cautiously optimistic, saying the project should not be analyzed solely on oil revenue, but also on the boost it could give other sectors of Venezuela’s battered economy.

Doubts and challenges

The US government signed the deal with Venezuelan company North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP) to develop 17 oil fields with an estimated potential of about 65 billion barrels of crude. US President Donald Trump called the agreement “historic,” saying it would allow the US to purchase 20 percent of the production at cost.

Separately, several international firms have signed additional agreements for new energy projects in the country.

Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado on Thursday backed Washington’s role in developing the country’s oil reserves but said the US needed a more competent partner than the current Venezuelan government, which she called an “illegitimate regime.”

“All of this requires sustained work under the non-negotiable principles of absolute transparency, legality and efficiency. And this is only possible with the legitimacy and stability offered by a serious and democratic government,” she said.

Experts have also expressed doubts over the limited information the government has released, including some contradictions between Washington and Caracas regarding the duration of the concessions, as well as over officials’ optimism about achieving such investment figures.

One of the challenges posed by such an agreement is that the inflow of capital could distort Venezuela’s economy if not handled properly, according to economist Manuel Sutherland, director of the Center for Workers’ Research and Education.

He said Venezuela would need “new economic institutions and new rules that can change the nation’s monetary, political and exchange-rate structure” to avoid small devaluations and issuing unbacked money. “Otherwise, no matter how much money comes in, it will be diluted.”

Boosting the energy infrastructure

For the investments to materialize, Venezuela will also need to restore or build entirely new energy infrastructure, experts say. The deal involves oil fields that haven’t been developed.

“It requires electrical infrastructure that does not exist in the country today and needs resources, investment, technology and, especially, an entire support workforce in surrounding clusters, which undoubtedly has a huge multiplier effect on the economy,” said Venezuelan economist Luis Vicente León, president of the consulting firm Datanálisis.

He stressed that the new oil fields need five or 10 years to be developed.

Oil platforms and pumpjacks at Lake Maracaibo, as residents around the oil‑rich center of Maracaibo in Zulia state remain uncertain about new investments, in Cabimas, Venezuela, on January 26. Leonardo Fernandez Viloria/Reuters/File

The program will also require “a rescue of the electrical system” since there is currently a deficit that forces some regions to ration electricity, according to Sutherland. He estimated transforming the electrical system could take more than $15 billion.

Sutherland stressed that the investment amounts that officials have mentioned (up to $100 billion) would not arrive in the short term.

“They will be spread out. It’s not as though 10 companies are going to come in and put $100 billion into the country tomorrow; that doesn’t happen. The investments will be $10 million, $20 million, $100 million, and they will gradually increase,” he explained.

Still, he emphasized that even an annual investment of $5 billion would ease the country’s liquidity problem.

“In such a small economy, when you have a project of that magnitude ahead of you, its impact on the country is very large and very rapid, because it changes expectations and improves the investment climate,” León noted.

Residents await results

Venezuelan residents have responded to the deal with a mix of hope and concern.

“We have to be patient because the economy doesn’t pick up overnight,” said resident Erasmo Rojas.

“It takes time for the economy to pick up, and, well, we’re in a transitional phase that I think it’s positive for the country – that the country is moving toward a better future. We have to believe in the country.”

Some say the deal will amount to nothing if the money isn’t used to fix longstanding problems like unreliable public services.

A man walks past a mural depicting oil pumps and the Venezuelan flag, with portraits of Venezuelan independence leader Simon Bolivar (L) and former late President Hugo Chavez (R), in Caracas on September 3. Federico Parra/AFP/Getty Images

“What I want is for us to improve, you know? It’s the people who suffer the most. With sanctions or without them, in the end, it’s the people who suffer,” merchant Gian Gómez told CNN.

In the past two years, Venezuela has recorded a slow but steady increase in oil production, which recently exceeded 1 million barrels of crude oil per day for the first time since early 2019.

León said the increase was already having an impact and would be even greater in the final quarter. However, he said this path is not necessarily sustainable without new investment.

Even if investments are confirmed, it’s unclear when the population would begin to feel that things are improving.

For León, “that is a more complex story,” since GDP growth does not necessarily translate into tangible benefits.

“Now there is much more money, but what happens? If you ask the Venezuelan population, they will still tell you that they do not feel it, and that creates an unmet expectation that is negative in terms of national perception,” he said.

Acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez said she aims to raise production to 1.5 million barrels per day, which León believes would improve some economic indicators, though he warned that if production stalls there, “social demands will remain.”

“Do you have more money? Yes. But the power goes out for five or six hours in Barquisimeto, San Cristóbal, Mérida or Maracaibo. In other words, the electricity or water infrastructure problem has not been resolved,” he said.

He estimated that it would take at least a year for the population to feel that services are being managed better.

“Whether (the agreement) is sufficient, whether it is fair, and how it compares with the rest of the world is another story,” he added. “But I have no doubt whatsoever that there will be growth.”

World.title: Nvidia inks $13 billion deal to buy the AI startup that was hacked by OpenAI
World.content:
New York —

Nvidia announced on Thursday that it will buy artificial intelligence startup Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, a massive bet by the chipmaker to expand the reach of open-source AI technology.

Hugging Face, a service for hosting and accessing open-source AI models and data sets, has been in the spotlight recently after it was hacked by OpenAI models that went rogue during a testing incident.

The company has also been at the center of an industry debate over whether access to advanced AI technology should be available openly — or whether it should be “closed,” like popular models from OpenAI and Anthropic, and restricted to prevent misuse. Hugging Face said it was forced to use an open-source Chinese model to defend itself from the OpenAI hack because of restrictions in how popular closed models could be used.

Unlike closed models, open-source AI models like those hosted on Hugging Face allow companies and developers to download the parameters that determine how a model functions and customize them for specific purposes. By downloading and running the models on their own infrastructure, some believe it also makes customers’ proprietary or sensitive data more secure.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has spoken in support of open models, arguing they can improve safety and speed up innovation. The acquisition could also benefit Nvidia’s plans to secure its role as the technology backbone of the AI boom.

Huang said in a blog post on Thursday that by acquiring Hugging Face, Nvidia could expand access to the platform’s models to more developers and companies around the world. Already, Hugging Face boasts more than 18 million developers and researchers using more than 3 million models, as well as 200,000 enterprise customers. Nvidia itself has released more than 500 open models on Hugging Face, prior to the deal.

“To the millions of builders on Hugging Face: thank you for pushing the boundaries of what is possible,” Huang said in a blog post, reiterating Nvidia’s plan to keep the platform open. “Together, we will make AI more open, more capable and more accessible to people and institutions around the world.”

The chipmaker last week said its sales more than doubled in the most recent quarter to more than $96 billion. But investors continue to question whether the spending spree on AI infrastructure will continue, and whether Nvidia can stay ahead of a growing slate of competitors.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has committed to continuing to make Hugging Face available as an open-source platform. Philip Fong/AFP/Getty Images

Nvidia has made major investments in propping up and expanding the AI ecosystem, including investing in AI labs and lending money to customers who buy its chips to build data centers.

Under the deal announced Thursday, Nvidia will pay $11.9 billion to Hugging Face shareholders. The agreement also includes an additional $1 billion in equity to retain Hugging Face employees joining Nvidia. The acquisition is expected to close in the first half of next year, according to a securities filing.

The agreement marks a significant jump from Hugging Face’s $4.5 billion valuation in 2023, following a $235 million funding round. Hugging Face turned down a $500 million investment from Nvidia last year that would have valued it at $7 billion, wanting to keep its independence, according to a report from the Financial Times.

But Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue said in an interview with CNBC on Thursday that he pursued the deal with Nvidia over the summer after realizing that open-source AI was at a “turning point and that it needed more resources, more scale, more visibility.”

World.title: Trump promised ‘economic D-Day’ for Iran. So far, actions have come in drips
World.content:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio this week instructed diplomats around the world to tell their host countries they must “systematically identify and sever” ties to Iran, and those with branches of Iranian banks must shut them down immediately.

On Friday, the US Treasury Department announced it was targeting a Turkish bank and its subsidiaries that allegedly serve as “critical financial lifelines” to Iran.

They marked the latest sanctions under “Operation Economic Outcast,” a pressure campaign that President Donald Trump had previewed as “economic D-Day” for Iran.

However, rather than a sweeping, singular assault, the measures have come in drips in the nearly two weeks since it was announced.

Meanwhile, there remains deep skepticism from experts and diplomats that the US will take meaningful action against key Iranian partners like China. They also continue to question the impact the sanctions will have on Tehran, which has withstood decades of economic pressure.

“The Iranians have been handling and evading sanctions for half a century for bloody sake, they can take pretty much anything thrown at them,” a regional source said.

Experts have noted that the impact of sanctions takes time. A former senior State Department official noted that signs of economic strain in Iran, like long gas lines or empty grocery shelves, seem to be “part of what has been happening, and not something new.”

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has disputed the notion that sanctions don’t work and insisted that the US has “never engaged… at this level of intensity.”

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announces a new set of sanctions against Iran, describing them as “an economic D-Day,” at the Treasury Department in Washington, DC, onn August 24. Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images

Last week, the Treasury Department proposed cutting off the UAE branches of Banque Misr, Egypt’s second largest bank, from the US financial market. It also sanctioned the general manager of the Dubai branch of Bank Melli, Iran’s biggest bank.

Friday’s sanctions hit Turkey’s Golden Global Bank and its subsidiaries, which Treasury claims have “facilitated tens of millions of dollars’ worth of transactions,” including in oil revenues from China, for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Quds Force.”

Daniel Tannebaum, a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council, said “the significance isn’t so much in the scale of the bank.” Rather, “it shows, especially in the run-up to the Trump-Xi bilat in a couple weeks, that there’s other countries, including allies… that the US is willing to make a move at.”

Experts and diplomats who spoke with CNN have cast doubts that the administration will make such a move at China.

“If they go at China, it will be very carefully orchestrated, where there are no surprises,” said Tannebaum, who is also a partner at management consulting firm Oliver Wyman.

Trump administration officials, meanwhile, have suggested that Beijing is being more cooperative than it may seem.

“We have more in common with the Chinese on Iran than we disagree with them on,” Bessent said at an event on the sidelines of the G20 Finance Ministers meeting this week.

There is also skepticism that the US will take significant actions against Pakistan or Oman, who also have trade ties with Iran, given their roles in the diplomacy around the war.

“I think they are trying to be balanced and careful. That’s why they’re targeting small banks now and hoping to freak out the others and again trying to be careful not to jeopardize any hope for the peace deal,” another regional source said.

Bessent said this week that the US has seen “great support around the world” for their latest economic campaign.

“We are speaking to our allies here, who have all come forward, and we have had a great show of support,” he said at the G20.

One diplomatic source described discussions with their country so far as being in the explanatory phase.

In the cable sent earlier this week, Rubio told diplomats to inform their host countries about “Operation Economic Outcast.” For embassies in places like London and Muscat, the diplomats were instructed to stress the imperative that “countries take immediate action to shutter all branches of Iranian banks located in their jurisdictions.”

“The bank branches must go dark – immediately,” said the diplomatic cable, which was seen by CNN.

CNN’s Kylie Atwood contributed reporting.

World.title: Everything you need to know about the Unified Card, a new alternative to the Ration Card
World.content:
The unified card, a replacement for the ration card has sparked widespread interest following its gradual rollout across Egypt.

The Supply and Internal Trade Ministry announced that the unified card will be delivered to citizens free of charge.

The Egypt Post plays a key and effective role in the unified card issuance system.

Obtaining the Card

Those interested must visit the Egypt Post to open a personal account for every citizen receiving the unified card.

Register your national ID card details and your mobile phone number registered in your name with a mobile network operator.

The card is equipped with a smart fingerprint to ensure that the service reaches those entitled to it.

Uses of the Unified Card

The unified card is a prepaid electronic card used for depositing or receiving funds directly onto the card and completing purchases at point-of-sale terminals at merchants or withdrawing cash from National Post Authority ATMs, with the amount being deducted directly from the card account.

The card is also used for making payments for digital government services, disbursing subsidized bread and rationed goods to citizens at bakeries and ration card distributors, and for comprehensive health insurance services.

How to Receive the Unified Card

Cards will be distributed after the head of the household receives a text message on their mobile phone instructing them, their spouse, and children over 16 years of age to go to a specific post office or supply office within a specified timeframe.

The head of the household will receive their card, which includes subsidized food and bread for the entire family.

Other family members will receive their individual cards, which include comprehensive health insurance and payment services.

The unified card will be available for collection at designated distribution centers, including post offices, supply offices, comprehensive health insurance offices, and the governorate headquarters, for one month from the date the citizen receives the text message.

Upon arriving at the designated collection point as indicated in the message, each family member can collect their package free of charge using their national ID card and the mobile phone number registered in their name.

This service is provided by Egypt Post employees.

Payment services are activated immediately, while the activation of food subsidy and comprehensive health insurance services will be announced later.

If the message is not received, citizens can call the Egypt Digital Platform hotline at 15999 to find out their collection location and scheduled time.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Video: Brad Pitt braves the wilderness in ‘Heart of the Beast’
World.content:
Brad Pitt reunites with director David Ayer in the upcoming survival movie “Heart of the Beast,” following their previous collaboration on “Fury.”

The film is slated for release on September 25.

Pitt portrays James Belmont, a former Special Forces officer on a camping trip in the Alaskan wilderness with his retired fighting dog, Odin.

Their trip turns into a fight for survival after their single-engine plane crashes into the icy waters.

David Ayer presents a departure from his previous work, which spans war, thriller, crime, action, and drama films.

He emphasizes that “Heart of the Beast” presented a unique challenge due to the nature of the story and the harsh filming conditions faced by the cast and crew.

“I had no idea what it was going to be like when I started on the project,” Ayer told Entertainment Weekly.

“It’s a story about a man and a dog, forests, a mountain, and an airplane; how hard is that? Oh my God! That was our recurring joke on set; Brad and I would look at each other at the end of the day and say, ‘We’ve got a dog, how hard is that?’”

He added: “It was an enormous challenge, physically demanding, with the wetness, fatigue, and cold, along with a great deal of emotional strain. Brad poured all his feelings and emotions into the performance, and I was directing the camera, sharing the moment with him. It was grueling work, but you feel that effort in every shot of the film.”

Struggle with the past

The film explores the psychological trauma of Pitt’s character, James Belmont, following painful memories from his military service through flashbacks.

Brad Pitt said of the character: “I see James as a soul haunted by painful memories of the past, but he strives to calm his mind and open his heart. Nature is a balm for his soul, and Odin is the greatest love and friend he has left on Earth.”

Co-starring a dog

Ober, who plays the dog Odin in the film, marks his acting debut, accompanying Pitt throughout most of the movie.

David Ayer revealed the behind-the-scenes details of working with the dog during filming, saying, “We put Odin first on the casting list. Brad really considered himself Odin’s co-actor, even though he was also training him.”

He added, “He had to handle and control the dog while maintaining his own character, presence, and performance, even when the dog was busy trying to bite a bee flying by. So, his ability to manage all of that was amazing.”

Pitt spoke about the difficulty of sharing the screen with a dog for about 95 percent of the film, explaining, “Because dogs don’t memorize lines, of course; they just act naturally as dogs. I became very attached to that hero dog, and I always had to carry treats for the dogs with me.”

He continued, “In the middle of a scene, let’s say an emotional one, the dog might start to wander off, and then I’d have to stop filming and say, ‘Ober, come here, mate, take this,’ and then immediately get back into the emotional mood of the scene. I became very good at that.”

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Liberia: CDC Debunks NPP Chairman Mulbah, Says NPP Was Never Invited to Opposition Roundtable
World.content:
Monrovia — The opposition Congress for Democratic Change has rejected claims by National Patriotic Party Chairman George Mulbah that his party declined an invitation to participate in a proposed opposition roundtable, insisting that no such invitation was extended to the NPP as an institution.

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

CDC Secretary-General Jefferson Koijee said the record must be set straight, arguing that the NPP and its national leadership were never formally invited to the planned engagement.

“At no time and at no point did the Congress for Democratic Change extend an invitation to the National Patriotic Party or its national leadership to participate in the proposed opposition roundtable discussion,” Koijee said.

His comments followed an announcement by Mulbah that the NPP would not participate in the planned opposition meeting.

Koijee said while a number of “outstanding, uncompromising” members of the NPP were invited, they were invited in their individual capacities and not as representatives of the party.

“Neither the NPP as an institution nor its National Chairman, Mr. George Mulbah, was invited,” he said.

He accused Mulbah of creating the impression that the CDC had sought the institutional participation of the NPP and was subsequently rejected.

“The National Chairman should therefore immediately cease and desist from creating the impression that the CDC sought the institutional participation of the NPP and was subsequently rejected,” Koijee added.

The dispute comes against the backdrop of the two parties’ political history. The NPP was a key component of the Coalition for Democratic Change during the 2017 presidential and legislative elections. The coalition brought together the CDC, which produced then-presidential candidate George Manneh Weah, and the NPP, which produced then-Vice Standard Bearer Jewel Howard-Taylor.

The CDC-led coalition won the 2017 presidential election and subsequently governed Liberia from 2018 to 2024.

Koijee also questioned the political circumstances surrounding Mulbah’s statement, particularly his reported employment within the Office of Vice President Jeremiah Kpan Koung.

He said the relationship raises questions about the “independence, timing and motivation” of statements directed at opposition cooperation.

Koijee further criticized what he described as the NPP leadership’s weak response when its standard bearer and former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor faced criminal allegations and incarceration.

“At that defining moment, the statement attributed to the party leadership was, in our view, one of the weakest responses in the history of a party once renowned for its fighting spirit, political potency and revolutionary character,” he said.

The CDC Secretary-General maintained that his party would not allow what he described as political distractions and manufactured controversies to undermine cooperation among opposition forces.

“The mighty Congress for Democratic Change has no room for political distractions, manufactured controversies or attempts to fracture genuine opposition solidarity,” Koijee said.

He pledged that the CDC would remain “vigilant” and respond to what it considers efforts to undermine democratic cooperation among opposition groups.

Koijee concluded by thanking individuals and institutions that were formally invited to the roundtable and accepted the invitation, saying their participation demonstrated that the broader democratic conversation would continue.

“The democratic conversation continues, and no political grandstanding will derail it,” he said.

World.title: Co-Defendant Challenges Judge’s Ruling Granting Ex-VP Taylor House Arrest, Calls It Unlawful
World.content:
MONROVIA — A day after Criminal Court “C” ordered former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor moved from Monrovia Central Prison to guarded house detention on medical grounds, a co-defendant in the same narcotics case has formally challenged the ruling, arguing that Judge Ousman F. Feika had no legal authority to grant it and asking him to reverse himself.



In a filing captio ned “Exceptions to His Honor Ousman F. Feika’s Ruling in Granting Co-Defendant Jewel Howard Taylor Compassionate Release,” Garpue K. Wonlue takes issue with the September 4 order on six separate grounds, most of them turning on a single argument: that the law Judge Feika relied on does not apply to someone in Taylor’s position.



The Case So Far



Taylor, Liberia’s vice president from 2018 to 2024, was arrested at Roberts International Airport on August 19 in connection with what officials have described as a transnational narcotics trafficking investigation tied to a record cocaine seizure earlier this year.

She was formally charged over eight counts, including unlicensed importation, unlicensed sale and trading, and illicit trafficking of drugs, along with money laundering and abuse-of-office allegations.



Her lawyers spent the following weeks trying, without success, to keep her out of the general prison population.

A Monrovia City Court magistrate denied an initial request for compassionate detention, ruling that granting it fell within the authority of the Ministry of Justice rather than the judiciary the defense’s follow-up appeal to the Supreme Court challenging that denial did not stop Taylor from being remanded to Monrovia Central Prison. She entered custody on September 2.



The case then moved to Criminal Court “C,” the circuit with jurisdiction over major drug offenses, where Judge Feika ordered Taylor’s immediate transfer from prison to 24-hour guarded house detention at her residence, converting her pre-trial custody into house arrest pending the outcome of the criminal proceedings.

Feika was explicit that the order rested solely on medical grounds and carried no bearing on guilt, writing that the release “shall therefore not constitute dismissal, acquittal, pardon, immunity, or termination of the criminal proceedings.

The judge also noted that the State itself had not opposed the request.



The Challenge



Wonlue’s filing does not dispute that Taylor has a medical condition. Instead, it argues that the court used the wrong statute to address it — and in doing so, exceeded its authority. The exceptions raise six points:



1. Jurisdiction: The filing argues that Chapter 34, Section 34.20 of the Criminal Procedure Law — the provision Judge Feika relied on — applies only to people who have already been indicted, tried, convicted, sentenced and committed to prison. Taylor, still awaiting trial, doesn’t fit that description, the filing contends, and Wonlue asks the court to rescind the ruling and have her returned to custody at Monrovia Central Prison.



2. No such remedy exists: The Criminal Procedure Law provides for bail under Chapter 13 for the accused, and for commitment under Chapter 34 for the convicted, the filing says — but nothing in between for a pre-trial detainee seeking release on medical grounds. Granting “compassionate leave” from pre-trial detention, it argues, is a remedy the court created rather than one the statute authorizes.



3. Consent doesn’t create jurisdiction: The fact that the State did not oppose Taylor’s request doesn’t change the analysis, the filing argues — parties cannot agree to give a court power the statute doesn’t grant it.



4. Equal treatment. This is the filing’s broadest argument: that granting one high-profile, pre-trial detainee a form of release unavailable to others sets up a two-tier system, at odds with the fairness-in-administration standard in Section 1.2 of the Criminal Procedure Law and Article 11 of the 1986 Constitution. The filing points out that many pre-trial detainees at Monrovia Central Prison have untreated medical conditions of their own, and argues the proper remedy was to order the Bureau of Corrections to provide adequate care in custody — not to release one defendant from it.



5. The nature of the charges and the cost of enforcement: Given that Taylor faces serious felony charges — importation of controlled drugs, money laundering and abuse of office, as the filing describes them — Wonlue argues the release conditions impose an unfunded, unauthorized burden on the State, which must now provide round-the-clock security at her residence. Surrendering travel documents, the filing adds, doesn’t eliminate flight risk on its own.



6. The inquiry should have ended sooner: Once the court determined that Section 34.20 doesn’t apply to pre-trial detainees, the filing argues, that finding should have ended the motion rather than being followed by relief anyway. It maintains the appropriate avenue for a detainee with medical concerns is a bail motion under Chapter 13 — with bond, sureties and monitoring conditions — not compassionate leave.



What’s Being Asked



The filing asks Judge Feika to reverse course: to rule that Section 34.20 doesn’t apply to pre-trial detainees, to direct the Bureau of Corrections and Ministry of Health to provide Taylor medical treatment at JFK Medical Center or another approved facility while she remains in custody, and — if release is warranted at all — to take it up as a bail application under Chapter 13, with a substantial bond and formal sureties, rather than as compassionate leave.



Judge Feika has not yet ruled on the exceptions. Taylor remains under house arrest at her residence pending the outcome. All defendants in the case, including Taylor, are presumed innocent, and the charges against them remain allegations that have not been tested at trial.

World.title: Liberia Champions Key Discussions on Preventive Diplomacy and a Robust E10 Voice at the 9th E10 & I5 Annual Dialogue in Panama
World.content:
Panama – Liberia’s Political Coordinator to the United Nations Security Council, Cllr. Aloysius Jappah assumed an active role in the 9th E10 & I5 Annual Dialogue, hosted by the Republic of Panama in Panama City from 1 to 2 September 2026, delivering substantive interventions on preventive diplomacy, Council effectiveness, and the responsibilities that come with elected membership of the UN Security Council.

Since 2019, the Dialogue has convened annually to unite the ten elected members of the Council (the E10) with the five incoming members (the I5) to enhance institutional memory, coordinate priorities, and bolster the Council’s ability to uphold international peace and security.

This year’s event was inaugurated and concluded by Panama’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, H.E. Javier Eduardo Martínez-Acha Vásquez, and honored at its closing by former President H.E. Mireya Moscoso.

The current E10 for 2026 includes Bahrain, Colombia, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Denmark, Greece, Latvia, Liberia, Pakistan, Panama, and Somalia.

Starting on 1 January 2027, the newly elected I5 will consist of Austria, Kyrgyzstan, Portugal, Trinidad and Tobago, and Zimbabwe, replacing Denmark, Greece, Pakistan, Panama, and Somalia as their mandates end on 31 December 2026.

Speaking during the session on “Preventive Diplomacy in Action,” moderated with the support of the Dag Hammarskjöld Foundation and its presenters Sigrid and Henrik, Cllr. Jappah anchored Liberia’s contribution in the letter of the United Nations Charter — Chapter VI (Articles 33–38) on the pacific settlement of disputes, Chapter VIII (Article 52) on regional arrangements, and Article 99 on the Secretary-General’s early-warning authority.

“The best Council intervention is a crisis that diplomacy prevents,” Cllr. Jappah affirmed, adding that “the Charter calls on us to extinguish the spark of conflict before it becomes a blaze. When we subscribed to this organization, we pledged to fulfill that obligation.”

Commenting on the operational challenge of moving from early warning to early action, the Political Coordinator emphasized what he called the prevention paradox — that when preventive diplomacy succeeds, the crisis does not occur, and success is therefore less visible than failure.

He cautioned that sovereignty concerns and geopolitical divisions frequently delay Council action, resulting in inaction until violence erupts. He warned that “Early warning without early action,” he warned, “is only a forecast of failure.”

Drawing on Liberia’s own post-conflict experience, Cllr. Jappah stressed that peace agreements close a chapter but do not, by themselves, remove the grievances, institutional weaknesses, or local tensions that can reignite conflict.

He called for the sustained deployment of good offices, mediation support, regional engagement, inclusive dialogue, confidence-building measures, early-warning capacity, and local peace infrastructures — with the consent and ownership of the country concerned.

“Peace agreements close a chapter; preventive diplomacy helps keep the next chapter from reopening the war,” he said, noting that sustained international, regional, and national engagement has been decisive in consolidating and protecting Liberia’s hard-won peace.

Contributing to Session V on reinvigorating the Council’s role in preventive diplomacy, Cllr. Jappah observed that the Dialogue offered members a valuable opportunity to internalize how a hasty drawdown of peacekeeping operations can leave a country vulnerable.

He was speaking in response to interventions on how transnational organized crime — including transcontinental drug trafficking — can undermine governance in states just emerging from conflict, where institutions remain fragile.

On the question of how the E10 should engage the incoming Secretary-General, Cllr. Jappah urged elected members to first conduct an honest internal assessment and to invest deliberately in strengthening themselves as a caucus.

He proposed that the E10 build the discipline and coordination required to create what he described as a collective “veto,” together with the guardrails to use that leverage responsibly. He observed that, over a two-year tenure, “before an elected member really gets to understand the Council and its dynamics, it is time to exit,” and he called on the E10 to systematically leverage the institutional memory of what he termed the “Farewell Five” — the five outgoing members concluding their terms each year — so that hard-earned experience is transferred rather than lost.

He further cautioned that the Council too frequently holds briefings and open meetings at which statements are made that contain useful antidotes but are followed by no concrete action.

He urged that the traditional E10 luncheons move beyond merely setting the agenda for the Secretary-General’s luncheon with Permanent Representatives, and instead become a forum in which elected members act with one voice on decisive issues before the Council.

Cllr. Jappah welcomed the newly elected members—Austria, Kyrgyzstan, Portugal, Trinidad and Tobago, and Zimbabwe—emphasizing the importance of continuity in preventive practice, disciplined coordination among members, and adherence to the Charter as the Council’s composition changes.

“Prevention is not an abstract ideal,” he concluded. “It is the disciplined practice of acting before choices disappear.”

The E10 & I5 Annual Dialogue, established in 2019, gathers incoming, serving, and outgoing UN Security Council members to enhance institutional memory and align objectives. Panama, holding a non-permanent seat, hosted the 9th edition during its term, ending on December 31, 2026.

World.title: Liberia Elevates Diplomatic Standing as August E10 UN Security Council Coordinator
World.content:
NEW YORK — Liberia has successfully concluded its leadership as Coordinator of the Ten Elected Members (E10) of the United Nations Security Council for August 2026, marking a historic milestone in its global diplomatic resurgence.

Stepping into the helm of the E10 alongside Bahrain, Colombia, DRC, Denmark, Greece, Latvia, Panama, Somalia, and Pakistan, Liberia strategically projected African leadership, unified non-permanent members, and shaped critical debate on pressing global peace and security files.

Key Achievements and Diplomatic Interventions

High-Level Security Council Diplomacy: Hosted UN Secretary-General António Guterres and E10 Ambassadors for a strategic luncheon centered on accelerating humanitarian interventions in Gaza and the West Bank.

Regional & Crisis Resolution:

Chaired the Political Coordinators’ Meeting to align consensus on the Libyan political process, security dynamics across West Africa and the Sahel, and the E10 Joint Statement on Security Council Working Methods.

International Judicial Oversight: Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary Lewis G. Brown II convened high-level negotiations with International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT) President Judge Graciela Gatti Santana, driving resolution terms on judicial archives, institutional downsizing, and UN oversight sensitivities involving Rwanda and Tanzania.

🇹🇿 Humanitarian Advocacy & International Law: Spearheaded expert briefings on the Ukraine humanitarian crisis and led targeted press interventions demanding the immediate release of illegally detained UN and aid personnel in Yemen.

Council Reform & Strategic Alignment: Championed reform of Security Council Subsidiary Bodies to streamline operations and ensure unified diplomatic alignment between the E10 and the Permanent Five (P5).

A Lasting Legacy on the World Stage

Liberia’s month-long tenure as Coordinator demonstrated strategic leadership, robust policy alignment, and an elevated ability to forge consensus among diverse international partners. Upon concluding its leadership, the E10 alliance formally commended Liberia for its decisive steering of the Council’s thematic priorities throughout August.

Meanwhile, Pakistan has assumed the E10 Coordination role for September, while Liberia remains positioned as an influential, principled voice on the Security Council, committed to driving international peace, stability, and multilateral cooperation.

World.title: Liberia: Ex-Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor to Receive Medical Care at Residence Under Restrictions as Drug Case Continues
World.content:
MONROVIA — Former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor is set to receive medical attention outside detention under strict conditions imposed by Criminal Court “C” Judge Ousman F. Feika amid ongoing concerns about her health.

By Selma Lomax, [email protected]

The court’s decision comes after Howard-Taylor’s lawyers raised medical concerns and sought her release from detention to allow her to receive treatment.

Under the court’s directive, Howard-Taylor is required to surrender all travel documents, effectively restricting her ability to leave the country while the case remains pending.

The former vice president will also be subject to limitations on visitors at her residence, with access restricted to a family member and her physician or physician’s assistant.

Howard-Taylor remains entangled in an ongoing investigation and prosecution involving allegations connected to an alleged transnational cocaine-trafficking operation.

Her legal team has maintained that her medical condition requires appropriate care, while the case continues to attract public attention because of the seriousness of the allegations.

The court’s latest action provides for medical considerations while maintaining judicial controls over Howard-Taylor as proceedings continue.

World.title: Liberia: Judge Feika Grants Jewel Howard-Taylor Compassionate Release
World.content:
Monrovia — Criminal Court “C” Judge Ousman F. Feika has granted former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor’s request for compassionate release from detention on medical grounds.

The ruling follows concerns raised by Howard-Taylor’s legal team about her medical condition and their request that she be permitted to receive medical care outside detention.

Under the court’s ruling, Howard-Taylor is required to surrender all travel documents to the court as part of the conditions of her release.

The court also ordered that visits to her residence be limited to a family member and her physician or physician’s assistant.

Howard-Taylor is facing criminal charges in connection with an ongoing narcotics investigation. She has denied the allegations.

The court’s decision allows her to leave detention while the legal proceedings continue.

This is a developing story.

World.title: Liberia: LIS Officer Thomas Kesselly Reportedly Shot in Foya
World.content:
MONROVIA — Thomas Kesselly, a member of the Liberia Immigration Service (LIS), was reportedly shot on Thursday, September 3, 2026, with conflicting accounts emerging over the incident.

Kesselley was reportedly shot at the LIS Academy in Foya.

While initial reports said Kesselly was shot, another account claims he shot himself.

However, family sources have expressed doubts about the self-inflicted shooting claim and are seeking clarity on what happened.

Kesselly’s condition and the circumstances surrounding the incident remain unclear as authorities have yet to provide a definitive account.

World.title: Liberia: Witness Alleges Howard-Taylor Link to Cocaine Trafficking Investigation and Political Plot
World.content:
Monrovia — A police investigator has testified in court about an alleged cocaine-trafficking operation in Liberia, telling the court that former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor was allegedly approached over a proposed protection arrangement and that discussions also involved an alleged plan targeting the administration of former President George Weah.

The testimony was given by Raphael Wilson, Acting Commissioner of Police for the Crimes Services Division, who said he supervised the investigative team that conducted the probe.

Wilson told the court that investigators traced the alleged network to meetings involving Liberians and foreign nationals in Dubai and Liberia, beginning around 2021.

According to his testimony, a Liberian identified as Sheikh Bashir Kanti met individuals in Dubai who expressed interest in returning to Liberia to resume business activities.

Wilson alleged that the individuals later disclosed plans to establish a cocaine-trafficking operation, with Liberia allegedly intended to serve as a transit point.

The witness further testified that the foreign nationals sought protection from a senior government official to facilitate their activities in Liberia.

According to Wilson, meetings were subsequently arranged in Liberia involving Bashir, the foreign nationals and individuals identified in the investigation as Tony and Maga.

He said investigators secretly recorded at least one of the meetings using cameras and written notes as part of their investigation.

Wilson testified that cocaine trafficking and the use of Liberia as a transit route were discussed during the meeting.

The witness further alleged that participants wanted assurances that their activities would receive protection from influential government officials.

According to Wilson, Jewel Howard-Taylor agreed to provide the requested protection but indicated that she would first return to Liberia and discuss the matter with her superior.

The testimony forms part of the prosecution’s effort to establish Howard-Taylor’s alleged connection to the broader investigation.

Alleged Political Plot

Wilson also testified about discussions that, according to the prosecution, involved an alleged plan directed against the government of former President George Weah.

The witness said the discussions surrounding the alleged protection arrangement were connected to a broader political plan involving senior political figures and an alleged attempt to undermine or overthrow the government.

However, Wilson’s testimony did not establish in court who allegedly initiated the plan, the specific actions contemplated or the precise role Howard-Taylor allegedly played.

Those matters remain subject to further evidence and examination by both the prosecution and defense.

Wilson said the alleged operation continued during the Weah administration and that investigators expanded their inquiry after some of the individuals involved returned to the region.

Foundation Mentioned in Testimony

The court also heard testimony concerning an alleged connection between some of the individuals under investigation and the Jewel Starfish Foundation, an organization associated with Howard-Taylor.

Wilson said one of the participants mentioned that Howard-Taylor operated the foundation.

The witness further testified that an individual identified as Nicholas expressed willingness to assist with the foundation.

The prosecution is presenting the alleged connection as part of the broader relationship it says existed between political figures and individuals under investigation.

US$45,000 Allegedly Delivered

Wilson also testified about an alleged cash delivery during one of the meetings.

According to the witness, a shopping bag was handed over during the meeting, and investigators later received information that approximately US$45,000 had been placed inside the bag.

The circumstances surrounding the alleged payment, including its intended recipient, purpose and connection to the alleged drug-trafficking operation, remain issues for the court to determine.

Investigation Continued After Weah Presidency

Wilson told the court that the investigation continued after the conclusion of the Weah administration in 2024.

He said investigators later determined that some of the individuals under investigation had returned to the region in 2025, prompting further investigative activity.

According to the witness, intelligence officers subsequently identified additional individuals allegedly connected to the investigation.

Wilson maintained that the investigation relied on intelligence gathering, recorded meetings and information obtained during the probe.

The testimony places several issues before the court, including the alleged cocaine-trafficking operation, claims of political protection, financial transactions and an alleged plan targeting the former Weah administration.

However, the allegations remain matters to be tested through evidence and cross-examination.

Howard-Taylor’s alleged involvement has not been established merely by Wilson’s testimony. She remains entitled to the presumption of innocence unless and until a competent court determines otherwise.

The defense is expected to challenge aspects of the investigation, including the credibility and interpretation of the witness’s account, the alleged recordings, meetings, financial transactions and claims concerning the political plan.

The court will ultimately determine whether the prosecution has produced sufficient admissible and credible evidence to establish the charges against Howard-Taylor and the other defendants.

World.title: ECZ Says Two Parties Qualify for Proportional Seats
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) says only two political parties currently qualify for the allocation of proportional representation seats in the National Assembly and all 116 local authorities.

The determination is based on the Presidential election results declared on August 18, 2026.

ECZ Chief Electoral Officer Brown Kasaro says following the inauguration of President Hakainde Hichilema, the Commission is within the initial seven-day period provided by law to allocate the proportional representation seats.

Mr. Kasaro said the Electoral Process Amendment Act sets out the procedure for allocating the seats, beginning from the date of the inauguration of the President-elect.

He said the Commission is required to distribute the seats among qualifying political parties within seven days of the President’s inauguration.

Mr. Kasaro said the Commission has not yet received names of candidates for the proportional representation seats because the process has not reached that stage.

He said once the allocation is completed, the Commission will write to the qualifying political parties to submit their lists of candidates.

Mr. Kasaro said the parties will then have seven days to submit separate lists comprising women, youth and persons with disabilities.

He said the proportional representation system applies to both the National Assembly and all 116 local authorities.

Mr. Kasaro explained that the Electoral Process Amendment Act provides for a formula based on the valid votes obtained by presidential candidates sponsored by political parties.

He said the Commission will use the total valid votes obtained by the 12 political-party-sponsored presidential candidates to determine the number of proportional representation seats each qualifying party is entitled to.

World.title: Army Commander Praises Troops for Professionalism
World.content:
Zambia Army Commander Lieutenant General Geoffrey Zyeele has commended officers and soldiers for their dedication and professionalism in carrying out their duties.

General Zyeele said unity, teamwork and collective responsibility enabled the Zambia Army to maintain security during the Presidential inauguration ceremony.

Speaking during a thanksgiving service held at Arakan Barracks in Lusaka, General Zyeele urged officers and soldiers to uphold the values of courage, sacrifice, loyalty and professionalism.

He said military service is a serious responsibility that requires God’s grace, guidance and protection in carrying out assigned missions and tasks.

World.title: Govt to Build New Petroleum Refinery at $1.2 Billion
World.content:
Government plans to build a new petroleum refinery next to the Indeni site in Ndola on the Copperbelt at a cost of 1.2 billion US dollars.

The project will be undertaken through the Industrial Development Corporation (IDC).

In an interview with the media, IDC Chief Executive Officer Cornwell Muleya said investors are on standby and ready to take up the project.

Mr. Muleya said the new refinery will give Government greater control over fuel production and help ensure affordable fuel for Zambians.

He said the project is expected to create 3,000 jobs during the construction phase and about 800 permanent jobs once the refinery becomes fully operational.

Mr. Muleya said the project will also help restore Ndola’s position as one of the country’s major industrial hubs.

He said the refinery will have a wider impact on other industries, with by-products such as bitumen and polyethylene expected to support road construction and plastics manufacturing.

World.title: No Political Prisoners in Zambia – Muchende
World.content:
The Office of the Attorney-General has rejected claims that people recently arrested by police are being politically detained, saying those in custody are facing serious criminal charges.

In a statement made available to ZNBC News in Lusaka today, Acting Attorney-General Marshal Muchende said Zambia has no prisoners of conscience or political prisoners.

Mr. Muchende said the individuals apprehended by police have been charged with offences including treason and terrorism-related crimes.

He said the charges stem from allegations of sponsoring, aiding and abetting unlawful paramilitary training, as well as other conduct allegedly in breach of Zambian law.

Mr. Muchende said the cases are now before courts of competent jurisdiction, where the accused persons will have an opportunity to receive due process.

He said the recent handover of people who had sought refuge at the United Nations House in Lusaka was facilitated by the Special Envoy of the United Nations Secretary-General to enable the individuals to face due process before Zambian authorities.

Mr. Muchende said there was no established basis to conclude that the individuals were being persecuted because of their political views or affiliations.

He said the Constitution does not provide immunity from criminal liability on the basis of political status, adding that no one is above the law and no one is beneath its protection.

Mr. Muchende said Government regards the arrests as matters of national security and public safety.

He said the State has a responsibility to protect the country’s constitutional order and territorial integrity, as well as citizens from terrorism, unlawful armed formations and attempts to undermine the State through violence or insurrection.

Mr. Muchende said Government remains committed to fundamental human rights and freedoms, including the rights to life, liberty, expression, association and conscience.

He said Government also remains committed to its partnership with the United Nations and its human rights mechanisms, and will continue to engage through dialogue and technical cooperation.

The statement was issued in response to remarks by the United Nations Special Rapporteur on the Right to Freedom of Peaceful Assembly and of Association.

World.title: UN Votes to Adopt New World Map to Reflect Africa’s True Size
World.content:
The United Nations General Assembly has voted to replace the traditional world map with one that more accurately reflects the size of Africa.

The “Correct the Map” resolution, sponsored by Togo and backed by African Union (AU) members, was supported by 164 countries, including France and the United Kingdom. The United States was the only country to vote against the resolution, while six countries abstained.

Although the UN vote is non-binding, it is expected to lead to changes in the maps used by institutions around the world.

The Mercator map, which has been widely used since the 16th Century, has faced criticism because it depicts Africa as being similar in size to Greenland, despite Africa being 14 times larger.

Critics argue that the distortion contributes to the development needs and potential of countries near the equator being minimised.

The Mercator map was designed in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator to assist European explorers with navigation across the world.

The distortion results from the difficulty of accurately representing the curved surface of the Earth on a two-dimensional map. Any world map requires compromises in how the Earth’s surface is represented.

The Mercator projection makes countries near the equator appear smaller than they are, while countries closer to the poles appear larger.

In an effort to address this distortion, a team of cartographers created an equal-area map in 2018 known as the Equal Earth projection.

In February, the African Union’s 54 member states adopted the projection, saying it “more accurately represents the sizes of all continents, particularly Africa.”

Online campaign group #CorrectTheMap said: “You could fit the United States, China, India, Japan, Mexico and much of Europe into Africa and still have land to spare.”

Ahead of Friday’s vote, Togolese Foreign Minister Robert Dussey told Reuters: “A fair world begins with a fair map.”

He had earlier told a UN briefing that maps are not neutral because they shape perceptions and influence how the place of peoples and continents in the world is understood.

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot backed the initiative, saying his ministry would stop using the Mercator map.

“Changing the map obviously doesn’t change the world. But correcting a representation that distorts it is already an act of truth,” he said.

However, Yaryna Ferencevych, a US representative at the UN, criticised the resolution, saying it mocked the work and purpose of the UN General Assembly.

“Instead of focusing on genuine problems of international peace, prosperity, or good relations, this body is debating map projects from the 16th Century, and their role in promoting reparations and ‘cognitive justice’,” she said.

In March, the United States also criticised the adoption of a resolution declaring the transatlantic slave trade “the gravest crime against humanity.”

Lerato Mogoatlhe from Africa No Filter, one of the groups behind the campaign to replace the Mercator map, told the BBC that Africa’s misrepresentation on world maps is not simply a cartographic error but also a narrative issue.

She said the campaign was part of efforts to address what she described as the “world’s longest misinformation and disinformation” about Africa.

Kenyan geographer Kioko Muendo told the BBC that the Mercator map has implicitly downplayed Africa’s vast resources, population and investment opportunities.

“Maps are more than just guides for travellers – they shape how regions are perceived politically and economically,” he said.

World.title: Over 1400 Milenge farmers supply maize to FRA
World.content:
Over 1,400 small scale farmers have supplied white maize to the Food Reserve Agency (FRA) in the 2026 crop marketing season.

Milenge District Agricultural Coordinator, Bright Chota has disclosed that the FRA has purchased 6,378.55 metric tonnes of maize as of September 2nd, 2026 with a total crop value of over K44.27 million.

Mr Chota said over K22.91 million has already been paid to 681 farmers.

“We have so far served 1,418 farmers, and out of this number, 681 farmers have been paid while 737 farmers are still due for payment,” Mr Chota said.

He stated that the FRA will soon be releasing the outstanding payment balance of over K21.36 million owed to farmers whose produce has already been purchased.

Mr Chota further observed that the FRA operationalised ten depots in the district to facilitate the purchase of the crop and ensure farmers have access to designated buying points.

World.title: 38 year old Chipangali defiler caged
World.content:
The Zambia Police Service in Chipangali district, in Eastern Province have arrested a 38 year old man in connection with the alleged defilement of a 13 year old girl in Nyelele Section area in Chief Chikuwe’s chiefdom.

The suspect, identified as Ives Banda, was apprehended after a report was made at Chiparamba Police Post, which falls under Chipata Central Police Station.

Eastern Province Police Commanding Officer Robertson Mweemba confirmed the incident to the media, saying the incident allegedly occurred between August 26 and 27, 2026, at the suspect’s residence.

Mr Mweemba said police officers received the report from the victim’s 44 year old mother, who alleged that her daughter had been sexually abused by her brother in law.

The Eastern Province Police Chief said the victim had been allowed to assist Banda at his restaurant at Chipitule mobile market after her elder sister, who is the suspect’s wife, requested that she help with cooking duties while she travelled to Mambwe for a church programme.

“The victim later spent the night at the suspect’s house after work and returned home the following morning complaining of tiredness,” he said.

Mr Mweemba said the victim later developed pain in her thighs and waist and subsequently disclosed to her family that she had allegedly been sexually abused.

“The matter was reported to police on September 4, 2026, after which officers, with the assistance of community crime prevention personnel, apprehended the suspect,” he said.

Mr Mweemba said police officers issued a medical report form and the victim was attended to at Chiparamba Rural Health Post.

“My officers have since launched investigations into the matter,” he said.

World.title: BRE congratulates President Hichilema on re-election
World.content:
The Bemba Royal Establishment has congratulated President Hakainde Hichilema on his re-election and swearing-in for a second term as Head of State.

The Royal Establishment has also congratulated all elected Members of Parliament, Mayors, Council Chairpersons and Councillors following the August 13 General Elections.

The Bashilubemba has further reaffirmed its commitment to work with the government of the day without aligning itself with a political party.

The Bemba Royal Establishment has since urged the government to use the new mandate to expedite development in Ulubemba.

This is according to a statement made available by Secretary to Mwinelubemba Chitimukulu, Richard Mukuka.

Bashilubemba also called for the need to reflect on the just ended electoral process with a focus on multi-partisan and christian values.

Meanwhile, the Bemba Royal Establishment cancelled the 2026 Ukusefya pa Ng’wena Traditional Ceremony of the Bemba People, which was scheduled for September 17 to 19.

The decision was arrived at during ‘Icilye ce Lamfya’, which was held at the Chitimukulu palace.

The Royal Establishment expressed regret over the inconvenience the cancellation may cause to sponsors, participants and members of the public who had made preparations for the event.

“All the sponsorships and donations that have been made to the ceremony shall be transferred to, and accounted for by, next year’s Ukusefya pa Ng’wena,” Mr Mukuka said.
